def generate_summaries(
    session: Session,
    game: Game,
    llm: LLMCallable,
) -> tuple[bool, bool]:
    """
    Generate and persist critic + user summaries for a game.

    Returns (critic_written, user_written).
    Skips a kind if the game has no quoted reviews of that kind.
    Replaces any existing summary of that kind on re-crawl.
    """
    all_reviews: list[Review] = (
        session.query(Review).filter_by(game_id=game.id).all()
    )

    critic_written = _summarise_kind(
        session, game, all_reviews,
        kind="critic",
        sampler=lambda r: _sample_critic(r, settings.llm_max_reviews),
        llm=llm,
    )
    user_written = _summarise_kind(
        session, game, all_reviews,
        kind="user",
        sampler=lambda r: _sample_user(r, settings.llm_max_reviews),
        llm=llm,
    )
    return critic_written, user_written


def _summarise_kind(
    session: Session,
    game: Game,
    all_reviews: list[Review],
    *,
    kind: str,
    sampler: Callable,
    llm: LLMCallable,
) -> bool:
    picked, rule = sampler(all_reviews)
    if not picked:
        log.debug("skip %s summary for %s — no %s reviews with quotes", kind, game.slug, kind)
        return False

    prompt_text = _PROMPT.format(
        n=len(picked),
        kind=kind,
        title=game.title,
        reviews_text=_build_reviews_text(picked),
    )
    messages = [
        {"role": "system", "content": "You summarise game reviews concisely and accurately."},
        {"role": "user", "content": prompt_text},
    ]

    raw = llm(messages)
    if raw is None:
        log.warning("LLM returned None for %s %s summary", game.slug, kind)
        return False

    parsed = _parse_llm_response(raw)
    if parsed is None:
        log.warning(
            "unparseable LLM response for %s %s: %r",
            game.slug, kind, raw[:200],
        )
        return False

    session.execute(
        delete(Summary).where(
            Summary.game_id == game.id,
            Summary.kind == kind,
        )
    )
    session.add(Summary(
        game_id=game.id,
        kind=kind,
        likes=parsed["likes"],
        dislikes=parsed["dislikes"],
        model=settings.llm_model,
        source_review_count=len(picked),
        sampling_rule=rule,
        generated_at=datetime.utcnow(),
    ))
    return True

"""
SQLAlchemy 2.0 models for the full schema described in BRIEF.md §3.
All columns that come from external sources are nullable — unreleased games
have nulls everywhere and that is the normal case.

from __future__ import annotations

from sqlalchemy import (
    Column, DateTime, Float, ForeignKey, Integer, String, Table, Text,
)
from sqlalchemy.orm import DeclarativeBase, relationship


class Base(DeclarativeBase):
    pass


# Simple join table: game_id → genre name string.  No separate genres entity
# because Metacritic genres have null ids and names are the stable key anyway.
game_genres = Table(
    "game_genres",
    Base.metadata,
    Column("game_id", Integer, ForeignKey("games.id", ondelete="CASCADE"), primary_key=True),
    Column("genre", String, primary_key=True),
)


class Game(Base):
    __tablename__ = "games"

    id = Column(Integer, primary_key=True)
    external_id = Column(Integer, unique=True, nullable=False)
    slug = Column(String, unique=True, nullable=False)
    title = Column(String, nullable=False)
    description = Column(Text)
    developer = Column(String)
    publisher = Column(String)
    cover_url = Column(String)
    video_url = Column(String)
    release_date = Column(String)        # "YYYY-MM-DD" or null
    rating = Column(String)              # "M", "E10+", …
    metascore = Column(Integer)
    userscore = Column(Float)
    first_seen_at = Column(DateTime, nullable=False)
    last_crawled_at = Column(DateTime, nullable=False)

    platform_scores = relationship(
        "PlatformScore", back_populates="game",
        cascade="all, delete-orphan", passive_deletes=True,

    reviews = relationship(

        cascade="all, delete-orphan", passive_deletes=True,

    summaries = relationship(

        cascade="all, delete-orphan", passive_deletes=True,

"""
Text embeddings for game similarity.

COMPUTE STRATEGY
────────────────
Embeddings are computed during the crawl (on write) and stored in the
`embeddings` table as a JSON-serialised float list.  Similarity is computed
on read by loading all stored vectors and doing a linear cosine-similarity
scan — no pre-built index.

Why on-read for similarity: new games are immediately visible as neighbours
without reprocessing existing games.  At O(hundreds) games a linear scan over
768-dim vectors is negligible (~milliseconds).  If the catalogue grows to
O(tens of thousands) this should be replaced with an ANN index (e.g. FAISS).

FALLBACK
────────
Games without a description (common for unreleased titles) are not embedded.
When MC_EMBED_PROVIDER is empty the embedder is disabled globally and all
similarity uses metadata overlap.  When computing similarity against a game
that lacks an embedding, find_similar() falls back to weighted Jaccard over
genres (60 %) and platforms (40 %).  The method field in each SimilarResult
records which path was taken so the UI can show it to the user.

FAILURE TRACKING
────────────────
embed_game() returns an EmbedOutcome namedtuple with two fields:
  stored  — True if the vector was written to the database
  failed  — True if the embedder was called but returned None (error, not skip)

The crawl loop accumulates failed counts into CrawlRun.embed_errors so
failures are visible in /health and the monitor — never silently discarded.

CROSS-CHECK: Metacritic related-carousel
────────────────────────────────────────
The related-games carousel on the Metacritic game page is parsed in
scrape/detail.py and logged at DEBUG level in crawl.py.
It is never used as the answer shown in the UI — the assignment requires
candidates from OUR database only.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import json
import logging
import math
from typing import Callable, List, NamedTuple, Optional

import httpx
from sqlalchemy import delete, select

from .config import settings
from .db.models import Embedding, PlatformScore, game_genres

log = logging.getLogger(__name__)

EmbedCallable = Callable[[str], "Optional[List[float]]"]


class EmbedOutcome(NamedTuple):
    stored: bool    # True if vector was written to the database
    failed: bool    # True if embedder was called and returned None (counts as error)


EMBED_STORED   = EmbedOutcome(stored=True,  failed=False)
EMBED_SKIPPED  = EmbedOutcome(stored=False, failed=False)   # no description / disabled
EMBED_FAILED   = EmbedOutcome(stored=False, failed=True)    # embedder returned None


# ── Provider availability ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────

def embedder_enabled() -> bool:
    """False when MC_EMBED_PROVIDER is empty — fall back to metadata-overlap."""
    return bool(settings.embed_provider)


# ── Text construction ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

def build_embed_text(title: str, description: str, genres: list, platforms: list) -> str:
    """
    Construct the input text for the embedding model.

    Layout:
        {title}
        {description}
        Genres: {g1}, {g2}
        Platforms: {p1}, {p2}

    Genres and platforms broaden the signal for games with terse descriptions.
    """
    parts = [title]
    if description:
        parts.append(description)
    if genres:
        parts.append("Genres: " + ", ".join(sorted(genres)))
    if platforms:
        parts.append("Platforms: " + ", ".join(sorted(platforms)))
    return "\n".join(parts)


# ── Math ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

def cosine_sim(a: list, b: list) -> float:
    dot = sum(x * y for x, y in zip(a, b))
    na = math.sqrt(sum(x * x for x in a))
    nb = math.sqrt(sum(x * x for x in b))
    if na == 0.0 or nb == 0.0:
        return 0.0
    return dot / (na * nb)


# ── Embedder — OpenAI-compatible /embeddings endpoint ────────────────────────

def call_embedder(text: str, *, _transport=None) -> "Optional[List[float]]":
    """
    Call the embeddings API and return the vector, or None on any error.

    _transport is a test seam — pass a custom httpx.BaseTransport to avoid
    real network calls (same pattern as llm.call_llm).
    """
    url = settings.llm_base_url.rstrip("/") + "/embeddings"
    headers = {"Authorization": f"Bearer {settings.llm_api_key}"}
    payload = {"model": settings.llm_embed_model, "input": text}
    try:
        kwargs: dict = {}
        if _transport is not None:
            kwargs["transport"] = _transport
        with httpx.Client(**kwargs, timeout=30) as client:
            resp = client.post(url, json=payload, headers=headers)
            resp.raise_for_status()
            return resp.json()["data"][0]["embedding"]
    except Exception:
        log.warning("embedding call failed (model=%s)", settings.llm_embed_model, exc_info=True)
        return None


# ── DB storage ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

def _store(session, game_id: int, vector: list, model: str) -> None:
    session.execute(delete(Embedding).where(Embedding.game_id == game_id))
    session.add(Embedding(game_id=game_id, vector=json.dumps(vector), model=model))


# ── Public API ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

def embed_game(session, game, embedder: EmbedCallable) -> EmbedOutcome:
    """
    Compute and store an embedding for `game`.

    Returns:
      EMBED_STORED   — vector written to DB
      EMBED_SKIPPED  — embedder disabled, or game has no description (use metadata fallback)
      EMBED_FAILED   — embedder was called but returned None (increment embed_errors)

    The caller must flush/commit after EMBED_STORED.
    """
    if not embedder_enabled():
        log.debug("skip embedding for %s — embedder not configured", game.slug)
        return EMBED_SKIPPED

    if not game.description:
        log.debug("skip embedding for %s — no description (will use metadata fallback)", game.slug)
        return EMBED_SKIPPED

    genres = session.execute(
        select(game_genres.c.genre).where(game_genres.c.game_id == game.id)
    ).scalars().all()
    platforms = session.execute(
        select(PlatformScore.platform).where(PlatformScore.game_id == game.id)
    ).scalars().all()

    text = build_embed_text(game.title, game.description, list(genres), list(platforms))
    vector = embedder(text)
    if vector is None:
        log.warning("embedder returned None for %s — embedding not stored", game.slug)
        return EMBED_FAILED

    _store(session, game.id, vector, settings.llm_embed_model)
    log.debug("stored %d-dim embedding for %s", len(vector), game.slug)
    return EMBED_STORED

"""
Text embeddings for game similarity.

COMPUTE STRATEGY
────────────────
Embeddings are computed during the crawl (on write) and stored in the
`embeddings` table as a JSON-serialised float list.  Similarity is computed
on read by loading all stored vectors and doing a linear cosine-similarity
scan — no pre-built index.

Why on-read for similarity: new games are immediately visible as neighbours
without reprocessing existing games.  At O(hundreds) games a linear scan over
768-dim vectors is negligible (~milliseconds).  If the catalogue grows to
O(tens of thousands) this should be replaced with an ANN index (e.g. FAISS).

FALLBACK
────────
Games without a description (common for unreleased titles) are not embedded.
When computing similarity against such a game, `find_similar` (similar.py)
falls back to weighted Jaccard over genres (60 %) and platforms (40 %).
The method field in each SimilarResult records which path was taken so the
UI can show it to the user.

CROSS-CHECK: Metacritic related-carousel
────────────────────────────────────────
The related-games carousel on the Metacritic game page is parsed in
scrape/detail.py (RelatedItem) and logged at DEBUG level in crawl.py.
It is never used as the answer shown in the UI — the assignment requires
candidates from OUR database only.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import json
import logging
import math
from typing import Callable, List, Optional

import httpx
from sqlalchemy import delete, select

from .config import settings
from .db.models import Embedding, PlatformScore, game_genres

log = logging.getLogger(__name__)

# Type alias — avoids `Optional[List[float]]` runtime issue on Py 3.9
EmbedCallable = Callable[[str], "Optional[List[float]]"]


# ── Text construction ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

def build_embed_text(title: str, description: str, genres: list, platforms: list) -> str:
    """
    Construct the input text for the embedding model.

    Layout:
        {title}
        {description}
        Genres: {g1}, {g2}
        Platforms: {p1}, {p2}

    Genres and platforms broaden the signal for games with terse descriptions.
    """
    parts = [title]
    if description:
        parts.append(description)
    if genres:
        parts.append("Genres: " + ", ".join(sorted(genres)))
    if platforms:
        parts.append("Platforms: " + ", ".join(sorted(platforms)))
    return "\n".join(parts)


# ── Math ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

def cosine_sim(a: list, b: list) -> float:
    dot = sum(x * y for x, y in zip(a, b))
    na = math.sqrt(sum(x * x for x in a))
    nb = math.sqrt(sum(x * x for x in b))
    if na == 0.0 or nb == 0.0:
        return 0.0
    return dot / (na * nb)


# ── Embedder — OpenAI-compatible /embeddings endpoint ────────────────────────

def call_embedder(text: str, *, _transport=None) -> "Optional[List[float]]":
    """
    Call the embeddings API and return the vector, or None on any error.

    _transport is a test seam — pass a custom httpx.BaseTransport to avoid
    real network calls (same pattern as llm.call_llm).
    """
    url = settings.llm_base_url.rstrip("/") + "/embeddings"
    headers = {"Authorization": f"Bearer {settings.llm_api_key}"}
    payload = {"model": settings.llm_embed_model, "input": text}
    try:
        kwargs: dict = {}
        if _transport is not None:
            kwargs["transport"] = _transport
        with httpx.Client(**kwargs, timeout=30) as client:
            resp = client.post(url, json=payload, headers=headers)
            resp.raise_for_status()
            return resp.json()["data"][0]["embedding"]
    except Exception:
        log.warning("embedding call failed for model=%s", settings.llm_embed_model, exc_info=True)
        return None


# ── DB storage ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

def _store(session, game_id: int, vector: list, model: str) -> None:
    session.execute(delete(Embedding).where(Embedding.game_id == game_id))
    session.add(Embedding(game_id=game_id, vector=json.dumps(vector), model=model))


# ── Public API ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

def embed_game(session, game, embedder: EmbedCallable) -> bool:
    """
    Compute and store an embedding for `game`.

    Returns True if the embedding was stored.
    Returns False without storing if:
    - game.description is None  (fallback to metadata overlap at query time)
    - the embedder returns None  (e.g. Ollama is offline; logged as WARNING)

    The caller must flush/commit after this returns True.
    """
    if not game.description:
        log.debug("skip embedding for %s — no description (will use metadata fallback)", game.slug)
        return False

    genres = session.execute(
        select(game_genres.c.genre).where(game_genres.c.game_id == game.id)
    ).scalars().all()
    platforms = session.execute(
        select(PlatformScore.platform).where(PlatformScore.game_id == game.id)
    ).scalars().all()

    text = build_embed_text(game.title, game.description, list(genres), list(platforms))
    vector = embedder(text)
    if vector is None:
        log.warning("embedder returned None for %s; no embedding stored", game.slug)
        return False

    _store(session, game.id, vector, settings.llm_embed_model)
    log.debug("stored %d-dim embedding for %s", len(vector), game.slug)
    return True

"""
LLM summary generation — critic and user kept separate.

SKIP RULES (both enforced before calling the LLM):
  1. A game with zero reviews of the relevant kind gets no summary row.
     New releases are unreleased; this is the common case, not the edge case.
  2. A game whose reviews are all missing quote text is treated as zero reviews.
     Summaries must come from actual review text, never from descriptions.

SAMPLING:
  critic: top MC_LLM_MAX_REVIEWS by score DESC (highest-rated critics first)
  user:   top MC_LLM_MAX_REVIEWS by thumbs_up DESC, then by review_date DESC
          (most-helpful users first; falls back to recency when thumbsUp is null)

  The rule name is stored in Summary.sampling_rule so downstream code can
  reason about what went into each summary.

MALFORMED RESPONSE:
  If the model returns something that is not {"likes": str, "dislikes": str},
  the summary is silently dropped (logged at WARNING).  Storing garbage is
  worse than storing nothing — a missing summary is obviously absent; bad text
  would be read as fact.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import json
import logging
from datetime import datetime
from typing import Callable

from sqlalchemy import delete
from sqlalchemy.orm import Session

from .config import settings
from .db.models import Game, Review, Summary

log = logging.getLogger(__name__)

_PROMPT = """\
Summarise the following {n} {kind} reviews for the game "{title}".

Reviews:
{reviews_text}

Reply with ONLY valid JSON (no markdown fences, no extra keys):
{{"likes": "2-3 sentences on what reviewers praised",\
 "dislikes": "2-3 sentences on what reviewers criticised or found lacking"}}"""

# Sampling rule names stored in DB.
_RULE_CRITIC = "top{n}_score"
_RULE_USER = "top{n}_thumbsup_then_recent"


def _sample_critic(reviews: list[Review], n: int) -> tuple[list[Review], str]:
    picked = sorted(
        (r for r in reviews if r.kind == "critic" and r.quote),
        key=lambda r: r.score or 0,
        reverse=True,
    )[:n]
    return picked, _RULE_CRITIC.format(n=len(picked))


def _sample_user(reviews: list[Review], n: int) -> tuple[list[Review], str]:
    def _key(r: Review):
        return (-(r.thumbs_up or 0), -(len(r.review_date or "")), r.review_date or "")

    picked = sorted(
        (r for r in reviews if r.kind == "user" and r.quote),
        key=_key,
    )[:n]
    return picked, _RULE_USER.format(n=len(picked))


def _parse_llm_response(text: str) -> dict | None:
    """Return {"likes": str, "dislikes": str} or None if unparseable/invalid."""
    try:
        d = json.loads(text)
    except (json.JSONDecodeError, ValueError):
        return None
    if (
        isinstance(d, dict)
        and isinstance(d.get("likes"), str)
        and isinstance(d.get("dislikes"), str)
        and d["likes"].strip()
        and d["dislikes"].strip()
    ):
        return {"likes": d["likes"], "dislikes": d["dislikes"]}
    return None


def _build_reviews_text(reviews: list[Review]) -> str:
    lines = []
    for i, r in enumerate(reviews, 1):
        pub = f" ({r.publication})" if r.publication else ""
        lines.append(f"[{i}] Score: {r.score}/100{pub}\n{r.quote}")
    return "\n\n".join(lines)


LLMCallable = Callable[[list[dict]], "str | None"]


def generate_summaries(
    session: Session,
    game: Game,
    llm: LLMCallable,
) -> tuple[bool, bool]:
    """
    Generate and persist critic + user summaries for a game.

    Returns (critic_written, user_written).
    Skips a kind if the game has no quoted reviews of that kind.
    Replaces any existing summary of that kind on re-crawl.
    """
    all_reviews: list[Review] = (
        session.query(Review).filter_by(game_id=game.id).all()
    )

    critic_written = _summarise_kind(
        session, game, all_reviews,
        kind="critic",
        sampler=lambda r: _sample_critic(r, settings.llm_max_reviews),
        llm=llm,
    )
    user_written = _summarise_kind(
        session, game, all_reviews,
        kind="user",
        sampler=lambda r: _sample_user(r, settings.llm_max_reviews),
        llm=llm,
    )
    return critic_written, user_written


def _summarise_kind(
    session: Session,
    game: Game,
    all_reviews: list[Review],
    *,
    kind: str,
    sampler: Callable,
    llm: LLMCallable,
) -> bool:
    picked, rule = sampler(all_reviews)
    if not picked:
        log.debug("skip %s summary for %s — no %s reviews with quotes", kind, game.slug, kind)
        return False

    prompt_text = _PROMPT.format(
        n=len(picked),
        kind=kind,
        title=game.title,
        reviews_text=_build_reviews_text(picked),
    )
    messages = [
        {"role": "system", "content": "You summarise game reviews concisely and accurately."},
        {"role": "user", "content": prompt_text},
    ]

    raw = llm(messages)
    if raw is None:
        log.warning("LLM returned None for %s %s summary", game.slug, kind)
        return False

    parsed = _parse_llm_response(raw)
    if parsed is None:
        log.warning(
            "unparseable LLM response for %s %s: %r",
            game.slug, kind, raw[:200],
        )
        return False

    session.execute(
        delete(Summary).where(
            Summary.game_id == game.id,
            Summary.kind == kind,
        )
    )
    session.add(Summary(
        game_id=game.id,
        kind=kind,
        likes=parsed["likes"],
        dislikes=parsed["dislikes"],
        model=settings.llm_model,
        source_review_count=len(picked),
        sampling_rule=rule,
        generated_at=datetime.utcnow(),
    ))
    return True

detail fetch and summary generation are skipped to avoid redundant work and

Stored in crawl_runs.next_browse_url after every successful browse run.
Survives restarts because it lives in SQLite, not in process memory.

from __future__ import annotations

import logging
from datetime import datetime, timezone

from sqlalchemy import text

from .api.detail import fetch_critic_reviews, fetch_detail, fetch_user_reviews
from .api.finder import fetch_browse_page, fetch_browse_url, fetch_new_releases
from .db.models import CrawlRun, Game
from .db.session import init_db, make_engine, make_session_factory
from .db.upsert import apply_detail, upsert_game
from .embed import EmbedCallable, call_embedder, embed_game
from .http import HttpClient
from .llm import call_llm
from .schedule import decide_crawl_source
from .summarise import generate_summaries

log = logging.getLogger(__name__)


def _today_start() -> datetime:
    d = datetime.now(timezone.utc).date()
    return datetime(d.year, d.month, d.day)


def do_crawl(
    session_factory,
    *,
    trigger: str = "manual",
    _embedder: "EmbedCallable | None" = None,
) -> CrawlRun:
    """
    One run: decide source, fetch listing, detail-fetch new games, summarise.
    Always writes a CrawlRun row; sets status='failed' if an exception escapes.
    Returns the completed CrawlRun (detached).
    """
    source, browse_url, page = decide_crawl_source(session_factory)

    with session_factory() as session:
        run = CrawlRun(
            started_at=datetime.utcnow(),
            trigger=trigger,
            source=source,
            page=page,
            status="running",
            games_seen=0,
            games_created=0,
            games_updated=0,
            games_skipped=0,
            errors=0,
        )
        session.add(run)
        session.commit()
        run_id = run.id

    embedder: EmbedCallable = _embedder if _embedder is not None else call_embedder

    created = updated = skipped = errors = 0
    games_seen = 0
    next_url: str | None = None
    status = "done"
    today = _today_start()

    try:
        with HttpClient() as client:
            # ── 1. Listing fetch ────────────────────────────────────────────
            if source == "new-releases":
                summaries = fetch_new_releases(client, limit=20)
            else:
                if browse_url:
                    summaries, next_url = fetch_browse_url(client, browse_url)
                else:
                    summaries, next_url = fetch_browse_page(client, offset=0, limit=24)
            games_seen = len(summaries)

            # ── 2. Listing upsert ───────────────────────────────────────────
            with session_factory() as session:
                for summary in summaries:
                    try:
                        _, is_new = upsert_game(session, summary)
                        if is_new:
                            created += 1
                        else:
                            updated += 1
                    except Exception:
                        log.exception("upsert failed for %s", summary.slug)
                        errors += 1
                session.commit()

            # ── 3. Detail fetch + summaries (skip if processed today) ───────
            with session_factory() as session:
                for summary in summaries:
                    game = session.query(Game).filter_by(slug=summary.slug).first()
                    if game is None:
                        continue

                    # Already processed today — skip expensive steps.
                    if game.last_crawled_at and game.last_crawled_at >= today:
                        # Still check: was it processed THIS run (just upserted)?
                        # If first_seen_at == last_crawled_at it's brand new now.
                        if game.first_seen_at != game.last_crawled_at:
                            skipped += 1
                            continue

                    try:
                        detail = fetch_detail(client, summary.slug)
                        critic_revs = fetch_critic_reviews(client, summary.slug, limit=50)
                        user_revs = fetch_user_reviews(client, summary.slug, limit=50)
                        if critic_revs:
                            detail.critic_reviews = critic_revs
                        if user_revs:
                            detail.user_reviews = user_revs
                        apply_detail(session, game, detail)
                        session.flush()

                        embed_game(session, game, embedder)
                        session.flush()

                        generate_summaries(session, game, call_llm)

                    except Exception:
                        log.exception("detail/summary failed for %s", summary.slug)
                        errors += 1

                session.commit()

    except Exception:
        status = "failed"
        errors += 1
        log.exception("crawl run %s failed", run_id)
        raise

    finally:
        with session_factory() as session:
            run = session.get(CrawlRun, run_id)
            run.finished_at = datetime.utcnow()
            run.status = status
            run.games_seen = games_seen
            run.games_created = created
            run.games_updated = updated
            run.games_skipped = skipped
            run.errors = errors
            if source == "browse":
                run.next_browse_url = next_url
            session.commit()
            session.refresh(run)
            session.expunge(run)

    return run


# ── CLI ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

def main() -> None:
    engine = make_engine()
    init_db(engine)
    Session = make_session_factory(engine)

    run = do_crawl(Session)

    print(
        f"Done: {run.games_created} created, {run.games_updated} updated, "
        f"{run.games_skipped} skipped, {run.errors} errors  ({run.status}).\n"
    )
    _print_games(engine)
    _print_run(run)


def _print_games(engine) -> None:
    with engine.connect() as conn:
        rows = conn.execute(text(
            "SELECT external_id, title, metascore, release_date, rating "
            "FROM games "
            "ORDER BY CASE WHEN release_date IS NULL THEN 1 ELSE 0 END, "
            "         release_date DESC "
            "LIMIT 20"
        )).fetchall()

    if not rows:
        print("(no games in database)")
        return

    print(f"{'ext_id':>12}  {'score':>5}  {'release':>10}  {'rating':>5}  title")
    print("─" * 90)
    for r in rows:
        ext_id, title, score, rel, rating = r
        print(
            f"{ext_id:>12}  {str(score or '–'):>5}  "
            f"{str(rel or '–'):>10}  {str(rating or '–'):>5}  {title}"
        )


def _print_run(run: CrawlRun) -> None:
    print()
    print("crawl_run row:")
    print(f"  id={run.id}  trigger={run.trigger}  source={run.source}  page={run.page}")
    print(f"  started={run.started_at}  finished={run.finished_at}")
    print(
        f"  seen={run.games_seen}  created={run.games_created}  "
        f"updated={run.games_updated}  skipped={run.games_skipped}  "
        f"errors={run.errors}  status={run.status}"
    )
    if run.next_browse_url:
        print(f"  next_browse_url={run.next_browse_url[:80]}…")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

"""
Crawl logic and CLI entry point.

`do_crawl` is the unit of work: decide which source to use (new-releases or
browse), fetch one page, upsert, detail-fetch games not yet processed today,
generate LLM summaries, write a CrawlRun row.

NEVER call `do_crawl` inside a FastAPI request handler — the rate limiter
sleeps for ~20 s per run (plus LLM latency).  See worker.py.

DAY LOGIC (UTC)
───────────────
First run of a UTC day   → New Releases carousel (20 scored games)
Subsequent runs that day → one page of the browse list (24 games)

"Processed today" = last_crawled_at >= midnight UTC today.
Games already processed today are upserted (keep metadata fresh) but their
detail fetch and summary generation are skipped to avoid redundant work and
LLM cost.

BROWSE CURSOR
─────────────
Stored in crawl_runs.next_browse_url after every successful browse run.
Survives restarts because it lives in SQLite, not in process memory.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import logging
from datetime import datetime, timezone

from sqlalchemy import text

from .api.detail import fetch_critic_reviews, fetch_detail, fetch_user_reviews
from .api.finder import fetch_browse_page, fetch_browse_url, fetch_new_releases
from .db.models import CrawlRun, Game
from .db.session import init_db, make_engine, make_session_factory
from .db.upsert import apply_detail, upsert_game
from .embed import EmbedCallable, call_embedder, embed_game
from .http import HttpClient
from .llm import call_llm
from .schedule import decide_crawl_source
from .summarise import generate_summaries

log = logging.getLogger(__name__)


def _today_start() -> datetime:
    d = datetime.now(timezone.utc).date()
    return datetime(d.year, d.month, d.day)


def do_crawl(
    session_factory,
    *,
    trigger: str = "manual",
    _embedder: "EmbedCallable | None" = None,
) -> CrawlRun:
    """
    One run: decide source, fetch listing, detail-fetch new games, summarise.
    Always writes a CrawlRun row; sets status='failed' if an exception escapes.
    Returns the completed CrawlRun (detached).
    """
    source, browse_url, page = decide_crawl_source(session_factory)

    with session_factory() as session:
        run = CrawlRun(
            started_at=datetime.utcnow(),
            trigger=trigger,
            source=source,
            page=page,
            status="running",
            games_seen=0,
            games_created=0,
            games_updated=0,
            games_skipped=0,
            errors=0,
        )
        session.add(run)
        session.commit()
        run_id = run.id

    embedder: EmbedCallable = _embedder if _embedder is not None else call_embedder

    created = updated = skipped = errors = 0
    llm_errs = embed_errs = 0
    games_seen = 0
    next_url: str | None = None
    status = "done"
    today = _today_start()

    try:
        with HttpClient() as client:
            # ── 1. Listing fetch ────────────────────────────────────────────
            if source == "new-releases":
                summaries = fetch_new_releases(client, limit=20)
            else:
                if browse_url:
                    summaries, next_url = fetch_browse_url(client, browse_url)
                else:
                    summaries, next_url = fetch_browse_page(client, offset=0, limit=24)
            games_seen = len(summaries)

            # ── 2. Listing upsert ───────────────────────────────────────────
            with session_factory() as session:
                for summary in summaries:
                    try:
                        _, is_new = upsert_game(session, summary)
                        if is_new:
                            created += 1
                        else:
                            updated += 1
                    except Exception:
                        log.exception("upsert failed for %s", summary.slug)
                        errors += 1
                session.commit()

            # ── 3. Detail fetch + summaries (skip if processed today) ───────
            with session_factory() as session:
                for summary in summaries:
                    game = session.query(Game).filter_by(slug=summary.slug).first()
                    if game is None:
                        continue

                    # Already processed today — skip expensive steps.
                    if game.last_crawled_at and game.last_crawled_at >= today:
                        # Still check: was it processed THIS run (just upserted)?
                        # If first_seen_at == last_crawled_at it's brand new now.
                        if game.first_seen_at != game.last_crawled_at:
                            skipped += 1
                            continue

                    try:
                        detail = fetch_detail(client, summary.slug)
                        critic_revs = fetch_critic_reviews(client, summary.slug, limit=50)
                        user_revs = fetch_user_reviews(client, summary.slug, limit=50)
                        if critic_revs:
                            detail.critic_reviews = critic_revs
                        if user_revs:
                            detail.user_reviews = user_revs
                        apply_detail(session, game, detail)
                        session.flush()

                        outcome = embed_game(session, game, embedder)
                        if outcome.stored:
                            session.flush()
                        elif outcome.failed:
                            embed_errs += 1

                        _, _, llm_fail = generate_summaries(session, game, call_llm)
                        llm_errs += llm_fail

                    except Exception:
                        log.exception("detail/summary failed for %s", summary.slug)
                        errors += 1

                session.commit()

    except Exception:
        status = "failed"
        errors += 1
        log.exception("crawl run %s failed", run_id)
        raise

    finally:
        with session_factory() as session:
            run = session.get(CrawlRun, run_id)
            run.finished_at = datetime.utcnow()
            run.status = status
            run.games_seen = games_seen
            run.games_created = created
            run.games_updated = updated
            run.games_skipped = skipped
            run.errors = errors
            run.llm_errors = llm_errs
            run.embed_errors = embed_errs
            if source == "browse":
                run.next_browse_url = next_url
            session.commit()
            session.refresh(run)
            session.expunge(run)

    return run


# ── CLI ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

def main() -> None:
    engine = make_engine()
    init_db(engine)
    Session = make_session_factory(engine)

    run = do_crawl(Session)

    print(
        f"Done: {run.games_created} created, {run.games_updated} updated, "
        f"{run.games_skipped} skipped, {run.errors} errors  ({run.status}).\n"
    )

            f"{str(rel or '–'):>10}  {str(rating or '–'):>5}  {title}"
        )

    print()
    print("crawl_run row:")
    print(f"  id={run.id}  trigger={run.trigger}  source={run.source}  page={run.page}")
    print(f"  started={run.started_at}  finished={run.finished_at}")

"""
Seed data — export the local database to a JSON file committed to the repo,
and restore it on first boot when the target database is empty.

WHY A SEED FILE
───────────────
Render free-tier instances start with a fresh disk on each deploy.  Rather
than bootstrapping from zero every time, we commit a snapshot of the local
database (40–60 games with summaries) so the service is immediately useful
after deploy without running any crawls.

The seed is ONLY loaded when the `games` table is empty (never overwrites
existing data), so re-deploys and restarts after the first crawl are safe.

FORMAT
──────
JSON with one key per table, rows serialised as list-of-dicts.  Datetimes
are stored as ISO-8601 strings and accepted by SQLite on insert.  The
`game_genres` association table is included as a plain list of dicts.

NULL values are preserved.  The embedding `vector` column stays as a
JSON-serialised float list (already TEXT in the schema).

COMMAND LINE
────────────
  # Export:
  PYTHONPATH=src python3 -m metacrawl.seed export [--output seeds/seed.json]

  # Manual restore (normally called automatically on boot):

import json
import logging
import sys
from datetime import datetime
from pathlib import Path

from sqlalchemy import text

log = logging.getLogger(__name__)

# Tables exported/imported in dependency order (parents before children).
_TABLES = [
    "games",
    "platform_scores",
    "game_genres",
    "reviews",
    "summaries",
    "embeddings",
]

# Default seed path relative to the repository root (also copied into the
# Docker image via `COPY seeds/ ./seeds/`).
DEFAULT_SEED_PATH = Path(__file__).parent.parent.parent / "seeds" / "seed.json"


# ── Export ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

class _DatetimeEncoder(json.JSONEncoder):
    def default(self, obj):
        if isinstance(obj, datetime):
            return obj.isoformat()
        return super().default(obj)


def export_seed(engine, path: Path) -> dict:
    """
    Dump every row from every tracked table to JSON and write to `path`.

    Returns a stats dict suitable for printing.
    """
    path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    data: dict = {"version": 1, "generated_at": datetime.utcnow().isoformat()}
    stats: dict = {}

    with engine.connect() as conn:
        for table in _TABLES:
            result = conn.execute(text(f"SELECT * FROM {table}"))
            rows = [dict(r._mapping) for r in result]
            data[table] = rows
            stats[table] = len(rows)

    path.write_text(json.dumps(data, indent=2, cls=_DatetimeEncoder), encoding="utf-8")
    log.info("seed exported to %s (%s)", path, stats)
    return stats


# ── Import / restore ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

def restore_if_empty(engine, path: Path = DEFAULT_SEED_PATH) -> bool:
    """
    Load the seed file into the database only when the `games` table is empty.

    Returns True if the seed was loaded, False if the DB already had rows or
    no seed file was found.  Never overwrites existing data.

    if not path.exists():

        return False

    with engine.connect() as conn:

    return True

    data = json.loads(path.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))

    with engine.begin() as conn:

            placeholders = ", ".join(f":{k}" for k in rows[0].keys())

            )
            for row in rows:

    sub = parser.add_subparsers(dest="cmd", required=True)

    exp = sub.add_parser("export", help="Dump local DB to seed file")
    exp.add_argument("--output", type=Path, default=DEFAULT_SEED_PATH)

    imp = sub.add_parser("import", help="Restore seed into (empty) DB")
    imp.add_argument("--input", type=Path, default=DEFAULT_SEED_PATH)
    imp.add_argument("--force", action="store_true",

    logging.basicConfig(level=logging.INFO, format="%(levelname)s %(message)s")

        stats = export_seed(engine, args.output)

    elif args.cmd == "import":

        else:
            restored = restore_if_empty(engine, args.input)
            if restored:
                print(f"Seed restored from {args.input}")
            else:
                print("Database is not empty — skipping (use --force to override)")

    _cli()

from ..worker import CrawlWorker
from .routes import router

async def lifespan(app: FastAPI):
    engine = make_engine()
    init_db(engine)
    session_factory = make_session_factory(engine)
    worker = CrawlWorker(session_factory)
    scheduler = make_scheduler(worker)
    scheduler.start()

    app.state.session_factory = session_factory
    app.state.worker = worker

    yield

    scheduler.shutdown(wait=False)

FROM python:3.11-slim

WORKDIR /app

# Install dependencies first for layer caching
COPY requirements.txt .
RUN pip install --no-cache-dir -r requirements.txt

# Application source only — no fixtures, caches, or DB files
COPY src/ ./src/

# Persistent disk mounts at /data on Render; DB lives there.

RUN mkdir -p /data

ENV PYTHONPATH=/app/src

EXPOSE 8000

CMD ["python", "-m", "metacrawl.web"]

      # Sort by score DESC, return [:k]

  def _metadata_score(genres_a, platforms_a, genres_b, platforms_b) -> float:

""" Web routes: game list, game detail, crawl trigger/status, health check. """ from __future__ import annotations from pathlib import Path import httpx from fastapi import APIRouter, Header, HTTPException, Request from fastapi.responses import HTMLResponse, JSONResponse from fastapi.templating import Jinja2Templates from sqlalchemy import select from ..config import settings from ..db.models import CrawlRun, Embedding, Game, PlatformScore, Review, Summary, game_genres from ..embed import embedder_enabled from ..similar import find_similar _TEMPLATES_DIR = Path(__file__).parent.parent / "templates" templates = Jinja2Templates(directory=str(_TEMPLATES_DIR)) router = APIRouter() _PER_PAGE = 24 @router.get("/", response_class=HTMLResponse) def games_list( request: Request, q: str = "", platform: str = "", sort: str = "score", page: int = 1, ): Session = request.app.state.session_factory with Session() as session: all_platforms = session.execute( select(PlatformScore.platform) .distinct() .order_by(PlatformScore.platform) ).scalars().all() query = session.query(Game) if q: query = query.filter(Game.title.ilike(f"%{q}%")) if platform: query = ( query.join(PlatformScore, PlatformScore.game_id == Game.id) .filter(PlatformScore.platform == platform) .distinct() ) sort_expr = { "score": Game.metascore.desc().nullslast(), "title": Game.title.asc(), "date": Game.release_date.desc().nullslast(), }.get(sort, Game.metascore.desc().nullslast()) query = query.order_by(sort_expr) total = query.count() games = query.offset((page - 1) * _PER_PAGE).limit(_PER_PAGE).all() game_platforms: dict = {} for game in games: game_platforms[game.id] = session.execute( select(PlatformScore.platform).where(PlatformScore.game_id == game.id) ).scalars().all() pages = max(1, (total + _PER_PAGE - 1) // _PER_PAGE) ctx = { "request": request, "games": games, "game_platforms": game_platforms, "all_platforms": all_platforms, "q": q, "platform": platform, "sort": sort, "page": page, "total": total, "per_page": _PER_PAGE, "pages": pages, } is_htmx = bool(request.headers.get("HX-Request")) tpl = "partials/results.html" if is_htmx else "games.html" return templates.TemplateResponse(tpl, ctx) @router.get("/games/{slug}", response_class=HTMLResponse) def game_detail(request: Request, slug: str): Session = request.app.state.session_factory with Session() as session: game = session.query(Game).filter_by(slug=slug).first() if game is None: return HTMLResponse( "

Game not found

", status_code=404, ) genres = session.execute( select(game_genres.c.genre).where(game_genres.c.game_id == game.id) ).scalars().all() platform_scores = session.execute( select(PlatformScore).where(PlatformScore.game_id == game.id) ).scalars().all() critic_reviews = session.execute( select(Review) .where(Review.game_id == game.id, Review.kind == "critic") .order_by(Review.score.desc()) .limit(20) ).scalars().all() user_reviews = session.execute( select(Review) .where(Review.game_id == game.id, Review.kind == "user") .order_by(Review.thumbs_up.desc().nullslast()) .limit(20) ).scalars().all() summaries = { s.kind: s for s in session.execute( select(Summary).where(Summary.game_id == game.id) ).scalars().all() } return templates.TemplateResponse("game.html", { "request": request, "game": game, "genres": list(genres), "platform_scores": list(platform_scores), "critic_reviews": list(critic_reviews), "user_reviews": list(user_reviews), "summaries": summaries, }) @router.get("/games/{slug}/similar", response_class=HTMLResponse) def game_similar(request: Request, slug: str): Session = request.app.state.session_factory with Session() as session: game = session.query(Game).filter_by(slug=slug).first() if game is None: return HTMLResponse("") similar = find_similar(session, game, k=5) # Load platforms for each result while the session is open result_platforms: dict = {} for r in similar: result_platforms[r.game.id] = session.execute( select(PlatformScore.platform).where(PlatformScore.game_id == r.game.id) ).scalars().all() # Note shown in UI when embedder is disabled or no embeddings exist yet embed_note = None if not embedder_enabled(): embed_note = ( "Embedder not configured — results use genre/platform overlap only. Hits GET /models (returns any response including 4xx = reachable). Returns False only on connection error or timeout. """ try: url = base_url.rstrip("/") + "/models" headers = {"Authorization": f"Bearer {api_key}"} with httpx.Client(timeout=timeout) as client: resp = client.get(url, headers=headers) return resp.status_code < 500 except Exception: return False @router.get("/health") def health(request: Request): """ One-shot status page: DB counts, LLM/embedder reachability, last crawl. Returns HTTP 200 when everything is functional. Returns HTTP 503 when the LLM is unreachable (embedder degraded is OK). """ Session = request.app.state.session_factory # ── DB counts ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────── with Session() as session: game_count = session.query(Game).count() summary_count = session.query(Summary).count() review_count = session.query(Review).count() embed_count = session.query(Embedding).count() last_run = ( session.query(CrawlRun) .order_by(CrawlRun.id.desc()) .first() ) last_ok_run = ( session.query(CrawlRun) .filter(CrawlRun.status == "done") .order_by(CrawlRun.id.desc()) .first() ) # ── Provider checks (run in parallel via threads would be nice, but # sequential is fine for a health endpoint — total budget ~6 s) ──── llm_reachable = _ping(settings.llm_base_url, settings.llm_api_key) embed_cfg = embedder_enabled() embed_reachable = _ping(settings.llm_base_url, settings.llm_api_key) if embed_cfg else None payload = { "db": { "ok": True, "games": game_count, "summaries": summary_count, "reviews": review_count, "embeddings": embed_count, }, "llm": { "provider": settings.llm_provider, "base_url": settings.llm_base_url, "model": settings.llm_model, "reachable": llm_reachable, }, "embedder": { "enabled": embed_cfg, "provider": settings.embed_provider if embed_cfg else None, "model": settings.llm_embed_model if embed_cfg else None, "reachable": embed_reachable, "note": None if embed_cfg else ( "Set MC_EMBED_PROVIDER to enable text-similarity; " "similarity falls back to genre/platform overlap." ), }, "last_crawl": { "id": last_run.id, "started_at": str(last_run.started_at), "status": last_run.status, "source": last_run.source, "games_created": last_run.games_created, "errors": last_run.errors, "llm_errors": getattr(last_run, "llm_errors", 0), "embed_errors": getattr(last_run, "embed_errors", 0), } if last_run else None, "last_successful_crawl": { "id": last_ok_run.id, "started_at": str(last_ok_run.started_at), "games_created": last_ok_run.games_created, } if last_ok_run else None, "crawl_worker_running": request.app.state.worker.is_running, } status_code = 200 if llm_reachable else 503 return JSONResponse(content=payload, status_code=status_code)

"""
FastAPI application.

Startup: initialise DB, start CrawlWorker + hourly APScheduler job.
Shutdown: stop scheduler without waiting for jobs to finish.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

from contextlib import asynccontextmanager
from pathlib import Path

from fastapi import FastAPI
from fastapi.staticfiles import StaticFiles

from ..db.session import init_db, make_engine, make_session_factory
from ..schedule import make_scheduler
from ..seed import restore_if_empty
from ..worker import CrawlWorker
from .routes import router

_STATIC = Path(__file__).parent.parent / "static"


@asynccontextmanager
async def lifespan(app: FastAPI):
    engine = make_engine()
    init_db(engine)
    restore_if_empty(engine)   # no-op when DB has games or no seed file exists
    session_factory = make_session_factory(engine)
    worker = CrawlWorker(session_factory)
    scheduler = make_scheduler(worker)
    scheduler.start()

    app.state.session_factory = session_factory
    app.state.worker = worker

    yield

    scheduler.shutdown(wait=False)


app = FastAPI(title="Metacrawl", lifespan=lifespan)
app.mount("/static", StaticFiles(directory=str(_STATIC)), name="static")
app.include_router(router)

(Tools: Bash, Read, WebFetch, WebSearch)

- Explore: Fast read-only search agent for locating code. Use it to find files by pattern (eg. "src/components/**/*.tsx"), grep for symbols or keywords (eg. "API endpoints"), or answer "where is X defined / which files reference Y." Do NOT use it for code review, design-doc auditing, cross-file consistency checks, or open-ended analysis — it reads excerpts rather than whole files and will miss content past its read window. When calling, specify search breadth: "quick" for a single targeted lookup, "medium" for moderate exploration, or "very thorough" to search across multiple locations and naming conventions. (Tools: All tools except Agent, Artifact, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)

- general-purpose: General-purpose agent for researching complex questions, searching for code, and executing multi-step tasks. When you are searching for a keyword or file and are not confident that you will find the right match in the first few tries use this agent to perform the search for you. (Tools: *)

- Plan: Software architect agent for designing implementation plans. Use this when you need to plan the implementation strategy for a task. Returns step-by-step plans, identifies critical files, and considers architectural trade-offs. (Tools: All tools except Agent, Artifact, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)
- statusline-setup: Use this agent to configure the user's Claude Code status line setting. (Tools: Read, Edit)

Reviews:
{reviews_text}

Reply with ONLY valid JSON (no markdown fences, no extra keys):
{{"likes": "2-3 sentences on what reviewers praised",\
 "dislikes": "2-3 sentences on what reviewers criticised or found lacking"}}"""

# Sampling rule names stored in DB.
_RULE_CRITIC = "top{n}_score"
_RULE_USER = "top{n}_thumbsup_then_recent"


def _sample_critic(reviews: list[Review], n: int) -> tuple[list[Review], str]:
    picked = sorted(
        (r for r in reviews if r.kind == "critic" and r.quote),
        key=lambda r: r.score or 0,
        reverse=True,
    )[:n]
    return picked, _RULE_CRITIC.format(n=len(picked))


def _sample_user(reviews: list[Review], n: int) -> tuple[list[Review], str]:
    def _key(r: Review):
        return (-(r.thumbs_up or 0), -(len(r.review_date or "")), r.review_date or "")

    picked = sorted(
        (r for r in reviews if r.kind == "user" and r.quote),
        key=_key,
    )[:n]
    return picked, _RULE_USER.format(n=len(picked))


def _parse_llm_response(text: str) -> dict | None:
    """Return {"likes": str, "dislikes": str} or None if unparseable/invalid."""
    try:
        d = json.loads(text)
    except (json.JSONDecodeError, ValueError):
        return None
    if (
        isinstance(d, dict)
        and isinstance(d.get("likes"), str)
        and isinstance(d.get("dislikes"), str)
        and d["likes"].strip()
        and d["dislikes"].strip()
    ):
        return {"likes": d["likes"], "dislikes": d["dislikes"]}
    return None


def _build_reviews_text(reviews: list[Review]) -> str:
    lines = []
    for i, r in enumerate(reviews, 1):
        pub = f" ({r.publication})" if r.publication else ""
        lines.append(f"[{i}] Score: {r.score}/100{pub}\n{r.quote}")
    return "\n\n".join(lines)


LLMCallable = Callable[[list[dict]], "str | None"]


def generate_summaries(
    session: Session,
    game: Game,
    llm: LLMCallable,
) -> tuple:
    """
    Generate and persist critic + user summaries for a game.

    Returns (critic_written, user_written, llm_errors).
      critic_written / user_written — True if a summary row was written.
      llm_errors — count of times the LLM was called but failed (returned None
                   or malformed JSON).  Zero if there were no reviews to
                   summarise (that is a skip, not an error).
                   The crawl loop stores this in CrawlRun.llm_errors so
                   failures are visible in /health and the monitor.
    """
    all_reviews: list[Review] = (
        session.query(Review).filter_by(game_id=game.id).all()
    )

    critic_written, c_failed = _summarise_kind(
        session, game, all_reviews,
        kind="critic",
        sampler=lambda r: _sample_critic(r, settings.llm_max_reviews),
        llm=llm,
    )
    user_written, u_failed = _summarise_kind(
        session, game, all_reviews,
        kind="user",
        sampler=lambda r: _sample_user(r, settings.llm_max_reviews),
        llm=llm,
    )
    return critic_written, user_written, int(c_failed) + int(u_failed)


def _summarise_kind(
    session: Session,
    game: Game,
    all_reviews: list[Review],
    *,
    kind: str,
    sampler: Callable,
    llm: LLMCallable,
) -> tuple:
    """Returns (written: bool, failed: bool)."""
    picked, rule = sampler(all_reviews)
    if not picked:
        log.debug("skip %s summary for %s — no %s reviews with quotes", kind, game.slug, kind)
        return False, False

    prompt_text = _PROMPT.format(
        n=len(picked),
        kind=kind,
        title=game.title,
        reviews_text=_build_reviews_text(picked),
    )
    messages = [
        {"role": "system", "content": "You summarise game reviews concisely and accurately."},
        {"role": "user", "content": prompt_text},
    ]

    raw = llm(messages)
    if raw is None:
        log.warning("LLM returned None for %s %s summary — counted as llm_error", game.slug, kind)
        return False, True

    parsed = _parse_llm_response(raw)
    if parsed is None:
        log.warning(
            "unparseable LLM response for %s %s: %r — counted as llm_error",
            game.slug, kind, raw[:200],
        )
        return False, True

    session.execute(
        delete(Summary).where(
            Summary.game_id == game.id,
            Summary.kind == kind,
        )
    )
    session.add(Summary(
        game_id=game.id,
        kind=kind,
        likes=parsed["likes"],
        dislikes=parsed["dislikes"],
        model=settings.llm_model,
        source_review_count=len(picked),
        sampling_rule=rule,
        generated_at=datetime.utcnow(),
    ))
    return True, False

# Default seed path relative to the repository root (also copied into the
# Docker image via `COPY seeds/ ./seeds/`).
DEFAULT_SEED_PATH = Path(__file__).parent.parent.parent / "seeds" / "seed.json"


# ── Export ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

class _DatetimeEncoder(json.JSONEncoder):
    def default(self, obj):
        if isinstance(obj, datetime):
            return obj.isoformat()
        return super().default(obj)


def export_seed(engine, path: Path) -> dict:
    """
    Dump every row from every tracked table to JSON and write to `path`.

    Returns a stats dict suitable for printing.
    """
    path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    data: dict = {"version": 1, "generated_at": datetime.utcnow().isoformat()}
    stats: dict = {}

    with engine.connect() as conn:
        for table in _TABLES:
            result = conn.execute(text(f"SELECT * FROM {table}"))
            rows = [dict(r._mapping) for r in result]
            data[table] = rows
            stats[table] = len(rows)

    path.write_text(json.dumps(data, indent=2, cls=_DatetimeEncoder), encoding="utf-8")
    log.info("seed exported to %s (%s)", path, stats)
    return stats


# ── Import / restore ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

def restore_if_empty(engine, path: Path = DEFAULT_SEED_PATH) -> bool:
    """
    Load the seed file into the database only when the `games` table is empty.

    Returns True if the seed was loaded, False if the DB already had rows or
    no seed file was found.  Never overwrites existing data.
    """
    if not path.exists():
        log.info("no seed file at %s — starting with empty database", path)
        return False

    with engine.connect() as conn:
        count = conn.execute(text("SELECT COUNT(*) FROM games")).scalar()
    if count > 0:
        log.info("database already has %d games — skipping seed restore", count)
        return False

    log.info("restoring seed from %s", path)
    _import_seed(engine, path)
    with engine.connect() as conn:
        n = conn.execute(text("SELECT COUNT(*) FROM games")).scalar()
    log.info("seed restore complete: %d games now in database", n)
    return True


def _import_seed(engine, path: Path) -> None:
    data = json.loads(path.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))

    with engine.begin() as conn:
        for table in _TABLES:
            rows = data.get(table, [])
            if not rows:
                continue
            cols = ", ".join(rows[0].keys())
            placeholders = ", ".join(f":{k}" for k in rows[0].keys())
            stmt = text(
                f"INSERT OR IGNORE INTO {table} ({cols}) VALUES ({placeholders})"
            )
            for row in rows:
                conn.execute(stmt, row)
    log.debug("seed import finished")


# ── CLI ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

def _cli():
    import argparse

    from .db.session import init_db, make_engine, make_session_factory  # noqa: F401

    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description="Metacrawl seed management")
    sub = parser.add_subparsers(dest="cmd", required=True)

    exp = sub.add_parser("export", help="Dump local DB to seed file")
    exp.add_argument("--output", type=Path, default=DEFAULT_SEED_PATH)

    imp = sub.add_parser("import", help="Restore seed into (empty) DB")
    imp.add_argument("--input", type=Path, default=DEFAULT_SEED_PATH)
    imp.add_argument("--force", action="store_true",
                     help="Import even if database is not empty (dangerous)")

    args = parser.parse_args()
    logging.basicConfig(level=logging.INFO, format="%(levelname)s %(message)s")

    engine = make_engine()
    init_db(engine)

    if args.cmd == "export":
        stats = export_seed(engine, args.output)
        for table, n in stats.items():
            print(f"  {table}: {n} rows")
        print(f"Seed written to {args.output}")

    elif args.cmd == "import":
        if args.force:
            _import_seed(engine, args.input)
            print(f"Seed imported from {args.input} (--force)")
        else:
            restored = restore_if_empty(engine, args.input)
            if restored:
                print(f"Seed restored from {args.input}")
            else:
                print("Database is not empty — skipping (use --force to override)")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    _cli()

def do_crawl(
    session_factory,
    *,
    trigger: str = "manual",
    _embedder: "EmbedCallable | None" = None,
) -> CrawlRun:
    """
    One run: decide source, fetch listing, detail-fetch new games, summarise.
    Always writes a CrawlRun row; sets status='failed' if an exception escapes.
    Returns the completed CrawlRun (detached).
    """
    source, browse_url, page = decide_crawl_source(session_factory)

    with session_factory() as session:
        run = CrawlRun(
            started_at=datetime.utcnow(),
            trigger=trigger,
            source=source,
            page=page,
            status="running",
            games_seen=0,
            games_created=0,
            games_updated=0,
            games_skipped=0,
            errors=0,
        )
        session.add(run)
        session.commit()
        run_id = run.id

    embedder: EmbedCallable = _embedder if _embedder is not None else call_embedder

    created = updated = skipped = errors = 0
    llm_errs = embed_errs = 0
    games_seen = 0
    next_url: str | None = None
    status = "done"
    today = _today_start()

    try:
        with HttpClient() as client:
            # ── 1. Listing fetch ────────────────────────────────────────────
            if source == "new-releases":
                summaries = fetch_new_releases(client, limit=20)
            else:
                if browse_url:
                    summaries, next_url = fetch_browse_url(client, browse_url)
                else:
                    summaries, next_url = fetch_browse_page(client, offset=0, limit=24)
            games_seen = len(summaries)

            # ── 2. Listing upsert ───────────────────────────────────────────
            with session_factory() as session:
                for summary in summaries:
                    try:
                        _, is_new = upsert_game(session, summary)
                        if is_new:
                            created += 1
                        else:
                            updated += 1
                    except Exception:
                        log.exception("upsert failed for %s", summary.slug)
                        errors += 1
                session.commit()

            # ── 3. Detail fetch + summaries (skip if processed today) ───────
            with session_factory() as session:
                for summary in summaries:
                    game = session.query(Game).filter_by(slug=summary.slug).first()
                    if game is None:
                        continue

                    # Already processed today — skip expensive steps.
                    if game.last_crawled_at and game.last_crawled_at >= today:
                        # Still check: was it processed THIS run (just upserted)?
                        # If first_seen_at == last_crawled_at it's brand new now.
                        if game.first_seen_at != game.last_crawled_at:
                            skipped += 1
                            continue

                    try:
                        detail = fetch_detail(client, summary.slug)
                        critic_revs = fetch_critic_reviews(client, summary.slug, limit=50)
                        user_revs = fetch_user_reviews(client, summary.slug, limit=50)
                        if critic_revs:
                            detail.critic_reviews = critic_revs
                        if user_revs:
                            detail.user_reviews = user_revs
                        apply_detail(session, game, detail)
                        session.flush()

                        outcome = embed_game(session, game, embedder)
                        if outcome.stored:
                            session.flush()
                        elif outcome.failed:
                            embed_errs += 1

                        _, _, llm_fail = generate_summaries(session, game, call_llm)
                        llm_errs += llm_fail

    session: Session,

) -> tuple:
    """
    Generate and persist critic + user summaries for a game.

    Returns (critic_written, user_written, llm_errors).

      llm_errors — count of times the LLM was called but failed (returned None

        session, game, all_reviews,
        kind="user",
        sampler=lambda r: _sample_user(r, settings.llm_max_reviews),
        llm=llm,
    )
    return critic_written, user_written, int(c_failed) + int(u_failed)

def generate_summaries(
    session: Session,
    game: Game,
    llm: LLMCallable,
    *,
    skip_existing: bool = False,
) -> tuple:
    """
    Generate and persist critic + user summaries for a game.

    Returns (critic_written, user_written, llm_errors).
      critic_written / user_written — True if a summary row was written.
      llm_errors — count of times the LLM was called but failed (returned None
                   or malformed JSON).  Zero if there were no reviews to
                   summarise (that is a skip, not an error).
                   The crawl loop stores this in CrawlRun.llm_errors so
                   failures are visible in /health and the monitor.
      skip_existing — when True, do not re-generate summaries that are already
                      present.  Used by the backfill command to avoid wasting
                      LLM calls on games that were successfully summarised
                      during a previous crawl.
    """
    from sqlalchemy import select as _select

    all_reviews: list[Review] = (
        session.query(Review).filter_by(game_id=game.id).all()
    )

    existing_kinds: set = set()
    if skip_existing:
        existing_kinds = set(
            session.execute(
                _select(Summary.kind).where(Summary.game_id == game.id)
            ).scalars().all()
        )

    critic_written, c_failed = _summarise_kind(
        session, game, all_reviews,
        kind="critic",
        sampler=lambda r: _sample_critic(r, settings.llm_max_reviews),
        llm=llm,
        already_exists="critic" in existing_kinds,
    )
    user_written, u_failed = _summarise_kind(
        session, game, all_reviews,
        kind="user",
        sampler=lambda r: _sample_user(r, settings.llm_max_reviews),
        llm=llm,
        already_exists="user" in existing_kinds,
    )
    return critic_written, user_written, int(c_failed) + int(u_failed)

"""
LLM summary generation — critic and user kept separate.

SKIP RULES (both enforced before calling the LLM):
  1. A game with zero reviews of the relevant kind gets no summary row.
     New releases are unreleased; this is the common case, not the edge case.
  2. A game whose reviews are all missing quote text is treated as zero reviews.
     Summaries must come from actual review text, never from descriptions.

SAMPLING:
  critic: top MC_LLM_MAX_REVIEWS by score DESC (highest-rated critics first)
  user:   top MC_LLM_MAX_REVIEWS by thumbs_up DESC, then by review_date DESC
          (most-helpful users first; falls back to recency when thumbsUp is null)

  The rule name is stored in Summary.sampling_rule so downstream code can
  reason about what went into each summary.

MALFORMED RESPONSE:
  If the model returns something that is not {"likes": str, "dislikes": str},
  the summary is silently dropped (logged at WARNING).  Storing garbage is
  worse than storing nothing — a missing summary is obviously absent; bad text
  would be read as fact.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import json
import logging
from datetime import datetime
from typing import Callable

from sqlalchemy import delete
from sqlalchemy.orm import Session

from .config import settings
from .db.models import Game, Review, Summary

log = logging.getLogger(__name__)

_PROMPT = """\
Summarise the following {n} {kind} reviews for the game "{title}".

Reviews:
{reviews_text}

Reply with ONLY valid JSON (no markdown fences, no extra keys):
{{"likes": "2-3 sentences on what reviewers praised",\
 "dislikes": "2-3 sentences on what reviewers criticised or found lacking"}}"""

# Sampling rule names stored in DB.
_RULE_CRITIC = "top{n}_score"
_RULE_USER = "top{n}_thumbsup_then_recent"


def _sample_critic(reviews: list[Review], n: int) -> tuple[list[Review], str]:
    picked = sorted(
        (r for r in reviews if r.kind == "critic" and r.quote),
        key=lambda r: r.score or 0,
        reverse=True,
    )[:n]
    return picked, _RULE_CRITIC.format(n=len(picked))


def _sample_user(reviews: list[Review], n: int) -> tuple[list[Review], str]:
    def _key(r: Review):
        return (-(r.thumbs_up or 0), -(len(r.review_date or "")), r.review_date or "")

    picked = sorted(
        (r for r in reviews if r.kind == "user" and r.quote),
        key=_key,
    )[:n]
    return picked, _RULE_USER.format(n=len(picked))


def _parse_llm_response(text: str) -> dict | None:
    """Return {"likes": str, "dislikes": str} or None if unparseable/invalid."""
    try:
        d = json.loads(text)
    except (json.JSONDecodeError, ValueError):
        return None
    if (
        isinstance(d, dict)
        and isinstance(d.get("likes"), str)
        and isinstance(d.get("dislikes"), str)
        and d["likes"].strip()
        and d["dislikes"].strip()
    ):
        return {"likes": d["likes"], "dislikes": d["dislikes"]}
    return None


def _build_reviews_text(reviews: list[Review]) -> str:
    lines = []
    for i, r in enumerate(reviews, 1):
        pub = f" ({r.publication})" if r.publication else ""
        lines.append(f"[{i}] Score: {r.score}/100{pub}\n{r.quote}")
    return "\n\n".join(lines)


LLMCallable = Callable[[list[dict]], "str | None"]


def generate_summaries(
    session: Session,
    game: Game,
    llm: LLMCallable,
) -> tuple:
    """
    Generate and persist critic + user summaries for a game.

    Returns (critic_written, user_written, llm_errors).
      critic_written / user_written — True if a summary row was written.
      llm_errors — count of times the LLM was called but failed (returned None
                   or malformed JSON).  Zero if there were no reviews to
                   summarise (that is a skip, not an error).
                   The crawl loop stores this in CrawlRun.llm_errors so
                   failures are visible in /health and the monitor.
    """
    all_reviews: list[Review] = (
        session.query(Review).filter_by(game_id=game.id).all()
    )

    critic_written, c_failed = _summarise_kind(
        session, game, all_reviews,
        kind="critic",
        sampler=lambda r: _sample_critic(r, settings.llm_max_reviews),
        llm=llm,
    )
    user_written, u_failed = _summarise_kind(
        session, game, all_reviews,
        kind="user",
        sampler=lambda r: _sample_user(r, settings.llm_max_reviews),
        llm=llm,
    )
    return critic_written, user_written, int(c_failed) + int(u_failed)


def _summarise_kind(
    session: Session,
    game: Game,
    all_reviews: list[Review],
    *,
    kind: str,
    sampler: Callable,
    llm: LLMCallable,
) -> tuple:
    """Returns (written: bool, failed: bool)."""
    picked, rule = sampler(all_reviews)
    if not picked:
        log.debug("skip %s summary for %s — no %s reviews with quotes", kind, game.slug, kind)
        return False, False

    prompt_text = _PROMPT.format(
        n=len(picked),
        kind=kind,
        title=game.title,
        reviews_text=_build_reviews_text(picked),
    )
    messages = [
        {"role": "system", "content": "You summarise game reviews concisely and accurately."},
        {"role": "user", "content": prompt_text},
    ]

    raw = llm(messages)
    if raw is None:
        log.warning("LLM returned None for %s %s summary — counted as llm_error", game.slug, kind)
        return False, True

    parsed = _parse_llm_response(raw)
    if parsed is None:
        log.warning(
            "unparseable LLM response for %s %s: %r — counted as llm_error",
            game.slug, kind, raw[:200],
        )
        return False, True

    session.execute(
        delete(Summary).where(
            Summary.game_id == game.id,
            Summary.kind == kind,
        )
    )
    session.add(Summary(
        game_id=game.id,
        kind=kind,
        likes=parsed["likes"],
        dislikes=parsed["dislikes"],
        model=settings.llm_model,
        source_review_count=len(picked),
        sampling_rule=rule,
        generated_at=datetime.utcnow(),
    ))
    return True, False

"""
LLM summary generation — critic and user kept separate.

SKIP RULES (both enforced before calling the LLM):
  1. A game with zero reviews of the relevant kind gets no summary row.
     New releases are unreleased; this is the common case, not the edge case.
  2. A game whose reviews are all missing quote text is treated as zero reviews.
     Summaries must come from actual review text, never from descriptions.

SAMPLING:
  critic: top MC_LLM_MAX_REVIEWS by score DESC (highest-rated critics first)
  user:   top MC_LLM_MAX_REVIEWS by thumbs_up DESC, then by review_date DESC
          (most-helpful users first; falls back to recency when thumbsUp is null)

  The rule name is stored in Summary.sampling_rule so downstream code can
  reason about what went into each summary.

MALFORMED RESPONSE:
  If the model returns something that is not {"likes": str, "dislikes": str},
  the summary is silently dropped (logged at WARNING).  Storing garbage is
  worse than storing nothing — a missing summary is obviously absent; bad text
  would be read as fact.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import json
import logging
from datetime import datetime
from typing import Callable

from sqlalchemy import delete
from sqlalchemy.orm import Session

from .config import settings
from .db.models import Game, Review, Summary

log = logging.getLogger(__name__)

_PROMPT = """\
Summarise the following {n} {kind} reviews for the game "{title}".

Reviews:
{reviews_text}

Reply with ONLY valid JSON (no markdown fences, no extra keys):
{{"likes": "2-3 sentences on what reviewers praised",\
 "dislikes": "2-3 sentences on what reviewers criticised or found lacking"}}"""

# Sampling rule names stored in DB.
_RULE_CRITIC = "top{n}_score"
_RULE_USER = "top{n}_thumbsup_then_recent"


def _sample_critic(reviews: list[Review], n: int) -> tuple[list[Review], str]:
    picked = sorted(
        (r for r in reviews if r.kind == "critic" and r.quote),
        key=lambda r: r.score or 0,
        reverse=True,
    )[:n]
    return picked, _RULE_CRITIC.format(n=len(picked))


def _sample_user(reviews: list[Review], n: int) -> tuple[list[Review], str]:
    def _key(r: Review):
        return (-(r.thumbs_up or 0), -(len(r.review_date or "")), r.review_date or "")

    picked = sorted(
        (r for r in reviews if r.kind == "user" and r.quote),
        key=_key,
    )[:n]
    return picked, _RULE_USER.format(n=len(picked))


def _parse_llm_response(text: str) -> dict | None:
    """Return {"likes": str, "dislikes": str} or None if unparseable/invalid."""
    try:
        d = json.loads(text)
    except (json.JSONDecodeError, ValueError):
        return None
    if (
        isinstance(d, dict)
        and isinstance(d.get("likes"), str)
        and isinstance(d.get("dislikes"), str)
        and d["likes"].strip()
        and d["dislikes"].strip()
    ):
        return {"likes": d["likes"], "dislikes": d["dislikes"]}
    return None


def _build_reviews_text(reviews: list[Review]) -> str:
    lines = []
    for i, r in enumerate(reviews, 1):
        pub = f" ({r.publication})" if r.publication else ""
        lines.append(f"[{i}] Score: {r.score}/100{pub}\n{r.quote}")
    return "\n\n".join(lines)


LLMCallable = Callable[[list[dict]], "str | None"]


def generate_summaries(
    session: Session,
    game: Game,
    llm: LLMCallable,
    *,
    skip_existing: bool = False,
) -> tuple:
    """
    Generate and persist critic + user summaries for a game.

    Returns (critic_written, user_written, llm_errors).
      critic_written / user_written — True if a summary row was written.
      llm_errors — count of times the LLM was called but failed (returned None
                   or malformed JSON).  Zero if there were no reviews to
                   summarise (that is a skip, not an error).
                   The crawl loop stores this in CrawlRun.llm_errors so
                   failures are visible in /health and the monitor.
      skip_existing — when True, do not re-generate summaries that are already
                      present.  Used by the backfill command to avoid wasting
                      LLM calls on games that were successfully summarised
                      during a previous crawl.
    """
    from sqlalchemy import select as _select

    all_reviews: list[Review] = (
        session.query(Review).filter_by(game_id=game.id).all()
    )

    existing_kinds: set = set()
    if skip_existing:
        existing_kinds = set(
            session.execute(
                _select(Summary.kind).where(Summary.game_id == game.id)
            ).scalars().all()
        )

    critic_written, c_failed = _summarise_kind(
        session, game, all_reviews,
        kind="critic",
        sampler=lambda r: _sample_critic(r, settings.llm_max_reviews),
        llm=llm,
        already_exists="critic" in existing_kinds,
    )
    user_written, u_failed = _summarise_kind(
        session, game, all_reviews,
        kind="user",
        sampler=lambda r: _sample_user(r, settings.llm_max_reviews),
        llm=llm,
        already_exists="user" in existing_kinds,
    )
    return critic_written, user_written, int(c_failed) + int(u_failed)


def _summarise_kind(
    session: Session,
    game: Game,
    all_reviews: list[Review],
    *,
    kind: str,
    sampler: Callable,
    llm: LLMCallable,
) -> tuple:
    """Returns (written: bool, failed: bool)."""
    picked, rule = sampler(all_reviews)
    if not picked:
        log.debug("skip %s summary for %s — no %s reviews with quotes", kind, game.slug, kind)
        return False, False

    prompt_text = _PROMPT.format(
        n=len(picked),
        kind=kind,
        title=game.title,
        reviews_text=_build_reviews_text(picked),
    )
    messages = [
        {"role": "system", "content": "You summarise game reviews concisely and accurately."},
        {"role": "user", "content": prompt_text},
    ]

    raw = llm(messages)
    if raw is None:
        log.warning("LLM returned None for %s %s summary — counted as llm_error", game.slug, kind)
        return False, True

    parsed = _parse_llm_response(raw)
    if parsed is None:
        log.warning(
            "unparseable LLM response for %s %s: %r — counted as llm_error",
            game.slug, kind, raw[:200],
        )
        return False, True

    session.execute(
        delete(Summary).where(
            Summary.game_id == game.id,
            Summary.kind == kind,
        )
    )
    session.add(Summary(
        game_id=game.id,
        kind=kind,
        likes=parsed["likes"],
        dislikes=parsed["dislikes"],
        model=settings.llm_model,
        source_review_count=len(picked),
        sampling_rule=rule,
        generated_at=datetime.utcnow(),
    ))
    return True, False
