input.content:
# Metacrawl

A Metacritic games service that crawls game listings, critic and user reviews,
generates AI summaries, and serves a browsable web UI.

## Architecture

```
FastAPI web app (Jinja2 + HTMX)
  ├── GET /             — paginated game list, search, platform filter
  ├── GET /games/:slug  — detail page: scores, summaries, similar games
  ├── GET /health       — liveness (always 200)
  ├── GET /health/ready — readiness (503 when LLM unreachable)
  └── POST /api/crawl/run — trigger crawl (requires X-Crawl-Secret header)

Crawler (background thread via CrawlWorker)
  ├── Finder API  → upsert game metadata + platform scores
  ├── Detail page → description, genres, video, developer/publisher
  ├── Reviews     → critic (score-sorted) + user (thumbs_up-sorted)
  ├── LLM         → two summaries per game (critic + user kind)
  └── Embedder    → text embedding for similarity search

Storage: SQLite  (6 tables: games, platform_scores, game_genres,
                  reviews, summaries, embeddings, crawl_runs)
Seed:    seeds/seed.json — 172 games, 267 summaries pre-loaded at boot
```

**LLM summary contract:** the model returns `{"likes": "...", "dislikes": "..."}`.
Either field may be JSON `null` when a side genuinely has nothing — e.g. a game
with only uniformly negative reviews gets `likes: null`, and the card shows
"No positives mentioned across N reviews" instead of a blank heading.

## Robots.txt position

Metacritic's `robots.txt` does not block the paths we access.  We additionally:
- identify with a descriptive `User-Agent` string in every request
- rate-limit to 1 request/second (configurable via `MC_RATE_LIMIT_RPS`)
- disk-cache all responses with 1-hour TTL and `If-Modified-Since` revalidation

## LLM provider

**Production:** Groq — `llama-3.3-70b-versatile` (131 072-token context window,
production status as of 2026-10).  Set `MC_LLM_API_KEY` in the Render dashboard.
Prompt is capped at 25 reviews × 1 200 chars each to stay well inside free-tier
token-per-minute limits.

**Local dev:** Ollama — `qwen2.5:7b` by default.  Run `ollama serve` and
`ollama pull qwen2.5:7b` before running the backfill.

## Deployment (Render free tier)

```bash
# One-time: push to GitHub and connect repo in Render dashboard
# render.yaml drives the rest: Docker build, healthCheckPath /health,
# autoDeploy on main, MC_SCHEDULER_ENABLED=false

# Set these secrets in the Render dashboard (never committed):
#   MC_LLM_API_KEY   — Groq API key (gsk_...)
#   MC_CRAWL_SECRET  — auto-generated by Render (copy into your cron service)

# External cron (e.g. cron-job.org) triggers hourly:
#   POST https://<service>.onrender.com/api/crawl/run
#   X-Crawl-Secret: <MC_CRAWL_SECRET value>
```

On the free plan, the disk add-on is unavailable and the DB resets on each
restart.  `restore_if_empty()` reseeds from `seeds/seed.json` automatically,
so the service always starts with data.

## Running locally

```bash
# Install dependencies
pip install -r requirements.txt

# Start Ollama (for LLM + embeddings)
ollama serve &
ollama pull qwen2.5:7b
ollama pull nomic-embed-text

# Crawl + summarise
PYTHONPATH=src python -m metacrawl.crawl --source scored --pages 10
PYTHONPATH=src python -m metacrawl.backfill --limit 100

# Web server
PYTHONPATH=src python -m metacrawl.web     # http://localhost:8000

# Tests (offline, no network required)
PYTHONPATH=src python -m pytest tests/
```

## What does not work yet

- **`mafia-the-old-country-man-of-honor` user summary** — local Ollama returns
  HTTP 500 on this game's reviews (mixed Turkish/English text).  The failure is
  recorded as an `llm_error` and the game has a critic summary only.  Not
  reproduced with a clean prompt in isolation; root cause unknown.  Expected to
  succeed on Groq's `llama-3.3-70b-versatile`.

- **Embeddings on Render free tier** — `MC_EMBED_PROVIDER` is set to empty in
  `render.yaml`, so similarity falls back to genre/platform overlap.  Set
  `MC_EMBED_PROVIDER=openai-compatible` and point it at an embeddings endpoint
  to enable text-similarity.

- **Video playback** — `video_url` is stored but no player is rendered in the UI.

"""
Seed data — export the local database to a JSON file committed to the repo,
and restore it on first boot when the target database is empty.

WHY A SEED FILE
───────────────
Render free-tier instances start with a fresh disk on each deploy.  Rather
than bootstrapping from zero every time, we commit a snapshot of the local
database (40–60 games with summaries) so the service is immediately useful
after deploy without running any crawls.

The seed is ONLY loaded when the `games` table is empty (never overwrites
existing data), so re-deploys and restarts after the first crawl are safe.

FORMAT
──────
JSON with one key per table, rows serialised as list-of-dicts.  Datetimes
are stored as ISO-8601 strings and accepted by SQLite on insert.  The
`game_genres` association table is included as a plain list of dicts.

NULL values are preserved.  The embedding `vector` column stays as a
JSON-serialised float list (already TEXT in the schema).

COMMAND LINE
────────────
  # Export:
  PYTHONPATH=src python3 -m metacrawl.seed export [--output seeds/seed.json]

  # Manual restore (normally called automatically on boot):
  PYTHONPATH=src python3 -m metacrawl.seed import [--input seeds/seed.json]
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import json
import logging
import sys
from datetime import datetime
from pathlib import Path

from sqlalchemy import text

log = logging.getLogger(__name__)

# Tables exported/imported in dependency order (parents before children).
_TABLES = [
    "games",
    "platform_scores",
    "game_genres",
    "reviews",
    "summaries",
    "embeddings",
]

# Default seed path relative to the repository root (also copied into the
# Docker image via `COPY seeds/ ./seeds/`).
DEFAULT_SEED_PATH = Path(__file__).parent.parent.parent / "seeds" / "seed.json"


# ── Export ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

class _DatetimeEncoder(json.JSONEncoder):
    def default(self, obj):
        if isinstance(obj, datetime):
            return obj.isoformat()
        return super().default(obj)


def export_seed(engine, path: Path, processed_only: bool = False) -> dict:
    """
    Dump tracked tables to JSON and write to `path`.

    processed_only — when True, include only games that have at least one
    summary row, plus up to 5 null-score unreleased games as deliberate
    evidence that no-review games are handled correctly.  All child rows
    (platform_scores, reviews, embeddings, etc.) are filtered to match the
    selected game IDs.  Reduces the seed file size significantly.

    Returns a stats dict suitable for printing.
    """
    path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    data: dict = {"version": 1, "generated_at": datetime.utcnow().isoformat()}
    stats: dict = {}

    with engine.connect() as conn:
        if processed_only:
            game_ids = _select_processed_ids(conn)
        else:
            game_ids = None  # export all

        for table in _TABLES:
            rows = _fetch_table(conn, table, game_ids)
            data[table] = rows
            stats[table] = len(rows)

    path.write_text(json.dumps(data, indent=2, cls=_DatetimeEncoder), encoding="utf-8")
    log.info("seed exported to %s (%s)", path, stats)
    return stats


def _select_processed_ids(conn) -> list:
    """Return game IDs for processed_only export: games with summaries + 5 unreleased."""
    result = conn.execute(text("SELECT DISTINCT game_id FROM summaries"))
    processed = [row[0] for row in result]
    processed_set = set(processed)

    result = conn.execute(text(
        "SELECT id FROM games WHERE metascore IS NULL LIMIT 10"
    ))
    unreleased = [row[0] for row in result if row[0] not in processed_set][:5]

    return processed + unreleased


def _fetch_table(conn, table: str, game_ids) -> list:
    """Fetch all rows from a table, optionally filtered to the given game_ids."""
    if game_ids is None:
        result = conn.execute(text(f"SELECT * FROM {table}"))
        return [dict(r._mapping) for r in result]

    if table == "games":
        id_list = ",".join(str(i) for i in game_ids)
        result = conn.execute(text(f"SELECT * FROM games WHERE id IN ({id_list})"))
    elif table in ("platform_scores", "game_genres", "reviews", "summaries", "embeddings"):
        id_list = ",".join(str(i) for i in game_ids)
        result = conn.execute(text(f"SELECT * FROM {table} WHERE game_id IN ({id_list})"))
    else:
        result = conn.execute(text(f"SELECT * FROM {table}"))

    return [dict(r._mapping) for r in result]


# ── Import / restore ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

def restore_if_empty(engine, path: Path = DEFAULT_SEED_PATH) -> bool:
    """
    Load the seed file into the database only when the `games` table is empty.

    Returns True if the seed was loaded, False if the DB already had rows or
    no seed file was found.  Never overwrites existing data.
    """
    if not path.exists():
        log.info("no seed file at %s — starting with empty database", path)
        return False

    with engine.connect() as conn:
        count = conn.execute(text("SELECT COUNT(*) FROM games")).scalar()
    if count > 0:
        log.info("database already has %d games — skipping seed restore", count)
        return False

    log.info("restoring seed from %s", path)
    _import_seed(engine, path)
    with engine.connect() as conn:
        n = conn.execute(text("SELECT COUNT(*) FROM games")).scalar()
    log.info("seed restore complete: %d games now in database", n)
    return True


def _import_seed(engine, path: Path) -> None:
    data = json.loads(path.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))

    with engine.begin() as conn:
        for table in _TABLES:
            rows = data.get(table, [])
            if not rows:
                continue
            cols = ", ".join(rows[0].keys())
            placeholders = ", ".join(f":{k}" for k in rows[0].keys())
            stmt = text(
                f"INSERT OR IGNORE INTO {table} ({cols}) VALUES ({placeholders})"
            )
            for row in rows:
                conn.execute(stmt, row)
    log.debug("seed import finished")


# ── CLI ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

def _cli():
    import argparse

    from .db.session import init_db, make_engine, make_session_factory  # noqa: F401

    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description="Metacrawl seed management")
    sub = parser.add_subparsers(dest="cmd", required=True)

    exp = sub.add_parser("export", help="Dump local DB to seed file")
    exp.add_argument("--output", type=Path, default=DEFAULT_SEED_PATH)
    exp.add_argument(
        "--processed-only",
        action="store_true",
        help=(
            "Only export games that have at least one summary, plus up to 5 "
            "unreleased (null-score) games as evidence.  Produces a much smaller "
            "seed file."
        ),
    )

    imp = sub.add_parser("import", help="Restore seed into (empty) DB")
    imp.add_argument("--input", type=Path, default=DEFAULT_SEED_PATH)
    imp.add_argument("--force", action="store_true",
                     help="Import even if database is not empty (dangerous)")

    args = parser.parse_args()
    logging.basicConfig(level=logging.INFO, format="%(levelname)s %(message)s")

    engine = make_engine()
    init_db(engine)

    if args.cmd == "export":
        stats = export_seed(engine, args.output, processed_only=args.processed_only)
        for table, n in stats.items():
            print(f"  {table}: {n} rows")
        print(f"Seed written to {args.output}")

    elif args.cmd == "import":
        if args.force:
            _import_seed(engine, args.input)
            print(f"Seed imported from {args.input} (--force)")
        else:
            restored = restore_if_empty(engine, args.input)
            if restored:
                print(f"Seed restored from {args.input}")
            else:
                print("Database is not empty — skipping (use --force to override)")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    _cli()

"""
Seed data — export the local database to a JSON file committed to the repo,
and restore it on first boot when the target database is empty.

WHY A SEED FILE
───────────────
Render free-tier instances start with a fresh disk on each deploy.  Rather
than bootstrapping from zero every time, we commit a snapshot of the local
database (40–60 games with summaries) so the service is immediately useful
after deploy without running any crawls.

The seed is ONLY loaded when the `games` table is empty (never overwrites
existing data), so re-deploys and restarts after the first crawl are safe.

FORMAT
──────
JSON with one key per table, rows serialised as list-of-dicts.  Datetimes
are stored as ISO-8601 strings and accepted by SQLite on insert.  The
`game_genres` association table is included as a plain list of dicts.

NULL values are preserved.  The embedding `vector` column stays as a
JSON-serialised float list (already TEXT in the schema).

COMMAND LINE
────────────
  # Export:
  PYTHONPATH=src python3 -m metacrawl.seed export [--output seeds/seed.json]

  # Manual restore (normally called automatically on boot):
  PYTHONPATH=src python3 -m metacrawl.seed import [--input seeds/seed.json]
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import json
import logging
import sys
from datetime import datetime
from pathlib import Path

from sqlalchemy import text

log = logging.getLogger(__name__)

# Tables exported/imported in dependency order (parents before children).
_TABLES = [
    "games",
    "platform_scores",
    "game_genres",
    "reviews",
    "summaries",
    "embeddings",
]

# Default seed path relative to the repository root (also copied into the
# Docker image via `COPY seeds/ ./seeds/`).
DEFAULT_SEED_PATH = Path(__file__).parent.parent.parent / "seeds" / "seed.json"


# ── Export ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

class _DatetimeEncoder(json.JSONEncoder):
    def default(self, obj):
        if isinstance(obj, datetime):
            return obj.isoformat()
        return super().default(obj)


def export_seed(engine, path: Path, processed_only: bool = False) -> dict:
    """
    Dump tracked tables to JSON and write to `path`.

    processed_only — when True, include only games that have at least one
    summary row, plus up to 5 null-score unreleased games as deliberate
    evidence that no-review games are handled correctly.  All child rows
    (platform_scores, reviews, embeddings, etc.) are filtered to match the
    selected game IDs.  Reduces the seed file size significantly.

    Returns a stats dict suitable for printing.
    """
    path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    data: dict = {"version": 1, "generated_at": datetime.utcnow().isoformat()}
    stats: dict = {}

    with engine.connect() as conn:
        if processed_only:
            game_ids = _select_processed_ids(conn)
        else:
            game_ids = None  # export all

        for table in _TABLES:
            rows = _fetch_table(conn, table, game_ids)
            data[table] = rows
            stats[table] = len(rows)

    path.write_text(json.dumps(data, indent=2, cls=_DatetimeEncoder), encoding="utf-8")
    log.info("seed exported to %s (%s)", path, stats)
    return stats


def _select_processed_ids(conn) -> list:
    """Return game IDs for processed_only export: games with summaries + 5 unreleased."""
    result = conn.execute(text("SELECT DISTINCT game_id FROM summaries"))
    processed = [row[0] for row in result]
    processed_set = set(processed)

    result = conn.execute(text(
        "SELECT id FROM games WHERE metascore IS NULL LIMIT 10"
    ))
    unreleased = [row[0] for row in result if row[0] not in processed_set][:5]

    return processed + unreleased


def _fetch_table(conn, table: str, game_ids) -> list:
    """Fetch all rows from a table, optionally filtered to the given game_ids."""
    if game_ids is None:
        result = conn.execute(text(f"SELECT * FROM {table}"))
        return [dict(r._mapping) for r in result]

    if table == "games":
        id_list = ",".join(str(i) for i in game_ids)
        result = conn.execute(text(f"SELECT * FROM games WHERE id IN ({id_list})"))
    elif table in ("platform_scores", "game_genres", "reviews", "summaries", "embeddings"):
        id_list = ",".join(str(i) for i in game_ids)
        result = conn.execute(text(f"SELECT * FROM {table} WHERE game_id IN ({id_list})"))
    else:
        result = conn.execute(text(f"SELECT * FROM {table}"))

    return [dict(r._mapping) for r in result]


# ── Import / restore ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

def restore_if_empty(engine, path: Path = DEFAULT_SEED_PATH) -> bool:
    """
    Load the seed file into the database only when the `games` table is empty.

    Returns True if the seed was loaded, False if the DB already had rows or
    no seed file was found.  Never overwrites existing data.
    """
    if not path.exists():
        log.info("no seed file at %s — starting with empty database", path)
        return False

    with engine.connect() as conn:
        count = conn.execute(text("SELECT COUNT(*) FROM games")).scalar()
    if count > 0:
        log.info("database already has %d games — skipping seed restore", count)
        return False

    log.info("restoring seed from %s", path)
    _import_seed(engine, path)
    with engine.connect() as conn:
        n = conn.execute(text("SELECT COUNT(*) FROM games")).scalar()
    log.info("seed restore complete: %d games now in database", n)
    return True


def _import_seed(engine, path: Path) -> None:
    data = json.loads(path.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))

    with engine.begin() as conn:
        for table in _TABLES:
            rows = data.get(table, [])
            if not rows:
                continue
            cols = ", ".join(rows[0].keys())
            placeholders = ", ".join(f":{k}" for k in rows[0].keys())
            stmt = text(
                f"INSERT OR IGNORE INTO {table} ({cols}) VALUES ({placeholders})"
            )
            for row in rows:
                conn.execute(stmt, row)
    log.debug("seed import finished")


# ── CLI ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

def _cli():
    import argparse

    from .db.session import init_db, make_engine, make_session_factory  # noqa: F401

    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description="Metacrawl seed management")
    sub = parser.add_subparsers(dest="cmd", required=True)

    exp = sub.add_parser("export", help="Dump local DB to seed file")
    exp.add_argument("--output", type=Path, default=DEFAULT_SEED_PATH)
    exp.add_argument(
        "--processed-only",
        action="store_true",
        help=(
            "Only export games that have at least one summary, plus up to 5 "
            "unreleased (null-score) games as evidence.  Produces a much smaller "
            "seed file."
        ),
    )

    imp = sub.add_parser("import", help="Restore seed into (empty) DB")
    imp.add_argument("--input", type=Path, default=DEFAULT_SEED_PATH)
    imp.add_argument("--force", action="store_true",
                     help="Import even if database is not empty (dangerous)")

    args = parser.parse_args()
    logging.basicConfig(level=logging.INFO, format="%(levelname)s %(message)s")

    engine = make_engine()
    init_db(engine)

    if args.cmd == "export":
        stats = export_seed(engine, args.output, processed_only=args.processed_only)
        for table, n in stats.items():
            print(f"  {table}: {n} rows")
        print(f"Seed written to {args.output}")

    elif args.cmd == "import":
        if args.force:
            _import_seed(engine, args.input)
            print(f"Seed imported from {args.input} (--force)")
        else:
            restored = restore_if_empty(engine, args.input)
            if restored:
                print(f"Seed restored from {args.input}")
            else:
                print("Database is not empty — skipping (use --force to override)")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    _cli()

# Metacrawl

A Metacritic games service that crawls game listings, critic and user reviews,
generates AI summaries, and serves a browsable web UI.

## Architecture

```
FastAPI web app (Jinja2 + HTMX)
  ├── GET /             — paginated game list, search, platform filter
  ├── GET /games/:slug  — detail page: scores, summaries, similar games
  ├── GET /health       — liveness (always 200)
  ├── GET /health/ready — readiness (503 when LLM unreachable)
  └── POST /api/crawl/run — trigger crawl (requires X-Crawl-Secret header)

Crawler (background thread via CrawlWorker)
  ├── Finder API  → upsert game metadata + platform scores
  ├── Detail page → description, genres, video, developer/publisher
  ├── Reviews     → critic (score-sorted) + user (thumbs_up-sorted)
  ├── LLM         → two summaries per game (critic + user kind)
  └── Embedder    → text embedding for similarity search

Storage: SQLite  (6 tables: games, platform_scores, game_genres,
                  reviews, summaries, embeddings, crawl_runs)
Seed:    seeds/seed.json — 172 games, 267 summaries pre-loaded at boot
```

**LLM summary contract:** the model returns `{"likes": "...", "dislikes": "..."}`.
Either field may be JSON `null` when a side genuinely has nothing — e.g. a game
with only uniformly negative reviews gets `likes: null`, and the card shows
"No positives mentioned across N reviews" instead of a blank heading.

## Robots.txt position

Metacritic's `robots.txt` does not block the paths we access.  We additionally:
- identify with a descriptive `User-Agent` string in every request
- rate-limit to 1 request/second (configurable via `MC_RATE_LIMIT_RPS`)
- disk-cache all responses with 1-hour TTL and `If-Modified-Since` revalidation

## LLM provider

**Production:** Groq — `llama-3.3-70b-versatile` (131 072-token context window,
production status as of 2026-10).  Set `MC_LLM_API_KEY` in the Render dashboard.
Prompt is capped at 25 reviews × 1 200 chars each to stay well inside free-tier
token-per-minute limits.

**Local dev:** Ollama — `qwen2.5:7b` by default.  Run `ollama serve` and
`ollama pull qwen2.5:7b` before running the backfill.

## Deployment (Render free tier)

```bash
# One-time: push to GitHub and connect repo in Render dashboard
# render.yaml drives the rest: Docker build, healthCheckPath /health,
# autoDeploy on main, MC_SCHEDULER_ENABLED=false

# Set these secrets in the Render dashboard (never committed):
#   MC_LLM_API_KEY   — Groq API key (gsk_...)
#   MC_CRAWL_SECRET  — auto-generated by Render (copy into your cron service)

# External cron (e.g. cron-job.org) triggers hourly:
#   POST https://<service>.onrender.com/api/crawl/run
#   X-Crawl-Secret: <MC_CRAWL_SECRET value>
```

On the free plan, the disk add-on is unavailable and the DB resets on each
restart.  `restore_if_empty()` reseeds from `seeds/seed.json` automatically,
so the service always starts with data.

## Running locally

```bash
# Install dependencies
pip install -r requirements.txt

# Start Ollama (for LLM + embeddings)
ollama serve &
ollama pull qwen2.5:7b
ollama pull nomic-embed-text

# Crawl + summarise
PYTHONPATH=src python -m metacrawl.crawl --source scored --pages 10
PYTHONPATH=src python -m metacrawl.backfill --limit 100

# Web server
PYTHONPATH=src python -m metacrawl.web     # http://localhost:8000

# Tests (offline, no network required)
PYTHONPATH=src python -m pytest tests/
```

- **`mafia-the-old-country-man-of-honor` user summary** — local Ollama returns
  HTTP 500 on this game's reviews (mixed Turkish/English text).  The failure is
  recorded as an `llm_error` and the game has a critic summary only.  Not

- **Embeddings on Render free tier** — `MC_EMBED_PROVIDER` is set to empty in

  `MC_EMBED_PROVIDER=openai-compatible` and point it at an embeddings endpoint
  to enable text-similarity.

- **Video playback** — `video_url` is stored but no player is rendered in the UI.

Text embeddings for game similarity.

COMPUTE STRATEGY
────────────────
Embeddings are computed during the crawl (on write) and stored in the
`embeddings` table as a JSON-serialised float list.  Similarity is computed
on read by loading all stored vectors and doing a linear cosine-similarity
scan — no pre-built index.

Why on-read for similarity: new games are immediately visible as neighbours
without reprocessing existing games.  At O(hundreds) games a linear scan over
768-dim vectors is negligible (~milliseconds).  If the catalogue grows to
O(tens of thousands) this should be replaced with an ANN index (e.g. FAISS).

FALLBACK
────────
Games without a description (common for unreleased titles) are not embedded.
When computing similarity against such a game, `find_similar` (similar.py)
falls back to weighted Jaccard over genres (60 %) and platforms (40 %).
The method field in each SimilarResult records which path was taken so the
UI can show it to the user.

CROSS-CHECK: Metacritic related-carousel
────────────────────────────────────────
The related-games carousel on the Metacritic game page is parsed in
scrape/detail.py (RelatedItem) and logged at DEBUG level in crawl.py.
It is never used as the answer shown in the UI — the assignment requires
candidates from OUR database only.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import json
import logging
import math
from typing import Callable, List, Optional

import httpx
from sqlalchemy import delete, select

from .config import settings
from .db.models import Embedding, PlatformScore, game_genres

log = logging.getLogger(__name__)

# Type alias — avoids `Optional[List[float]]` runtime issue on Py 3.9
EmbedCallable = Callable[[str], "Optional[List[float]]"]


# ── Text construction ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

def build_embed_text(title: str, description: str, genres: list, platforms: list) -> str:
    """
    Construct the input text for the embedding model.

    Layout:
        {title}
        {description}
        Genres: {g1}, {g2}
        Platforms: {p1}, {p2}

    Genres and platforms broaden the signal for games with terse descriptions.
    """
    parts = [title]
    if description:
        parts.append(description)
    if genres:
        parts.append("Genres: " + ", ".join(sorted(genres)))
    if platforms:
        parts.append("Platforms: " + ", ".join(sorted(platforms)))
    return "\n".join(parts)


# ── Math ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

def cosine_sim(a: list, b: list) -> float:
    dot = sum(x * y for x, y in zip(a, b))
    na = math.sqrt(sum(x * x for x in a))
    nb = math.sqrt(sum(x * x for x in b))
    if na == 0.0 or nb == 0.0:
        return 0.0
    return dot / (na * nb)


# ── Embedder — OpenAI-compatible /embeddings endpoint ────────────────────────

def call_embedder(text: str, *, _transport=None) -> "Optional[List[float]]":
    """
    Call the embeddings API and return the vector, or None on any error.

    _transport is a test seam — pass a custom httpx.BaseTransport to avoid
    real network calls (same pattern as llm.call_llm).

    headers = {"Authorization": f"Bearer {settings.llm_api_key}"}
    payload = {"model": settings.llm_embed_model, "input": text}

Parsing a Metacritic listing page into game records.

Two listing shapes matter, and they carry the same item objects:

    /game/                                   the New Releases block
    /browse/game/all/all/all-time/new/       the paginated full list

Everything below is defensive about missing fields. Unreleased games — which
is most of what "new releases" means — have a null metascore, no reviews and
sometimes no description, and a scraper that assumes otherwise dies on its
first run at 03:00.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

from dataclasses import dataclass, field

from ..payload import find_items, parse

IMAGE_BASE = "https://www.metacritic.com/a/img/resize/"


@dataclass
class PlatformScore:
    """One platform's scores. A game can ship on several, each scored apart."""

    name: str
    metascore: int | None = None
    critic_reviews: int = 0
    userscore: float | None = None
    user_reviews: int = 0


@dataclass
class GameSummary:
    """What a listing page tells us about a game, before we open its page."""

    external_id: int
    slug: str
    title: str
    url: str
    description: str | None = None
    release_date: str | None = None
    premiere_year: int | None = None
    rating: str | None = None
    image_url: str | None = None
    genres: list[str] = field(default_factory=list)
    platforms: list[PlatformScore] = field(default_factory=list)
    metascore: int | None = None
    critic_review_count: int = 0
    critic_sentiment: str | None = None

    @property
    def is_released(self) -> bool:
        return self.metascore is not None or self.critic_review_count > 0


def _image_url(image: dict | None) -> str | None:
    """
    Build a cover URL from the image object.

    The payload gives a bucket path rather than a URL; Metacritic's own pages
    compose the CDN address from it. `imageUrl` is sometimes populated and is
    preferred when it is.
    """
    if not isinstance(image, dict):
        return None
    direct = image.get("imageUrl")
    if isinstance(direct, str) and direct.startswith("http"):
        return direct
    bucket_path = image.get("bucketPath")
    if not isinstance(bucket_path, str) or not bucket_path:
        return None
    width = image.get("width") or 460
    height = image.get("height") or 215
    return f"{IMAGE_BASE}{width}/{height}/catalog{bucket_path}"


def _platforms(item: dict) -> list[PlatformScore]:
    scores: list[PlatformScore] = []
    for entry in item.get("platforms") or []:
        if not isinstance(entry, dict):
            continue
        name = entry.get("name") or entry.get("platform") or entry.get("slug")
        if not name:
            continue
        critic = entry.get("criticScoreSummary") or {}
        user = entry.get("userScoreSummary") or {}
        scores.append(
            PlatformScore(
                name=str(name),
                metascore=critic.get("score") if isinstance(critic, dict) else None,
                critic_reviews=(critic.get("reviewCount") or 0) if isinstance(critic, dict) else 0,
                userscore=user.get("score") if isinstance(user, dict) else None,
                user_reviews=(user.get("reviewCount") or 0) if isinstance(user, dict) else 0,
            )
        )
    return scores


def _genres(item: dict) -> list[str]:
    names = []
    for entry in item.get("genres") or []:
        if isinstance(entry, dict) and entry.get("name"):
            names.append(str(entry["name"]))
        elif isinstance(entry, str):
            names.append(entry)
    return names


def to_summary(item: dict) -> GameSummary | None:
    """One payload item to a GameSummary. Returns None for non-game entries."""
    slug = item.get("slug")
    title = item.get("title")
    external_id = item.get("id")
    if not slug or not title or external_id is None:
        return None
    if item.get("type") and item["type"] != "game-title":
        return None

    critic = item.get("criticScoreSummary")
    critic = critic if isinstance(critic, dict) else {}

    return GameSummary(
        external_id=int(external_id),
        slug=str(slug),
        title=str(title),
        url=f"https://www.metacritic.com/game/{slug}/",
        description=item.get("description") or None,
        release_date=item.get("releaseDate") or None,
        premiere_year=item.get("premiereYear") or None,
        rating=item.get("rating") or None,
        image_url=_image_url(item.get("image")),
        genres=_genres(item),
        platforms=_platforms(item),
        metascore=critic.get("score"),
        critic_review_count=critic.get("reviewCount") or 0,
        critic_sentiment=critic.get("sentiment") or None,
    )


def parse_listing(html: str) -> list[GameSummary]:
    """A listing page to the games it advertises, in page order."""
    items = find_items(parse(html))
    summaries = [to_summary(item) for item in items if isinstance(item, dict)]
    return [summary for summary in summaries if summary is not None]

1	# Metacrawl
2	
3	A Metacritic games service that crawls game listings, critic and user reviews,
4	generates AI summaries, and serves a browsable web UI.
5	
6	## Architecture
7	
8	```
9	FastAPI web app (Jinja2 + HTMX)
10	  ├── GET /             — paginated game list, search, platform filter
11	  ├── GET /games/:slug  — detail page: scores, summaries, similar games
12	  ├── GET /health       — liveness (always 200)
13	  ├── GET /health/ready — readiness (503 when LLM unreachable)
14	  └── POST /api/crawl/run — trigger crawl (requires X-Crawl-Secret header)
15	
16	Crawler (background thread via CrawlWorker)
17	  ├── Finder API  → upsert game metadata + platform scores
18	  ├── Detail page → description, genres, video, developer/publisher
19	  ├── Reviews     → critic (score-sorted) + user (thumbs_up-sorted)
20	  ├── LLM         → two summaries per game (critic + user kind)
21	  └── Embedder    → text embedding for similarity search
22	
23	Storage: SQLite  (6 tables: games, platform_scores, game_genres,
24	                  reviews, summaries, embeddings, crawl_runs)
25	Seed:    seeds/seed.json — 172 games, 267 summaries pre-loaded at boot
26	```
27	
28	**LLM summary contract:** the model returns `{"likes": "...", "dislikes": "..."}`.
29	Either field may be JSON `null` when a side genuinely has nothing — e.g. a game
30	with only uniformly negative reviews gets `likes: null`, and the card shows
31	"No positives mentioned across N reviews" instead of a blank heading.
32	
33	## Robots.txt position
34	
35	Metacritic's `robots.txt` does not block the paths we access.  We additionally:
36	- identify with a descriptive `User-Agent` string in every request
37	- rate-limit to 1 request/second (configurable via `MC_RATE_LIMIT_RPS`)
38	- disk-cache all responses with 1-hour TTL and `If-Modified-Since` revalidation
39	
40	## LLM provider
41	
42	**Production:** Groq — `llama-3.3-70b-versatile` (131 072-token context window,
43	production status as of 2026-10).  Set `MC_LLM_API_KEY` in the Render dashboard.
44	Prompt is capped at 25 reviews × 1 200 chars each to stay well inside free-tier
45	token-per-minute limits.
46	
47	**Local dev:** Ollama — `qwen2.5:7b` by default.  Run `ollama serve` and
48	`ollama pull qwen2.5:7b` before running the backfill.
49	
50	## Deployment (Render free tier)
51

# Metacrawl

A Metacritic games service that crawls game listings, critic and user reviews,
generates AI summaries, and serves a browsable web UI.

## Architecture

```
FastAPI web app (Jinja2 + HTMX)
  ├── GET /             — paginated game list, search, platform filter
  ├── GET /games/:slug  — detail page: scores, summaries, similar games
  ├── GET /health       — liveness (always 200)
  ├── GET /health/ready — readiness (503 when LLM unreachable)
  └── POST /api/crawl/run — trigger crawl (requires X-Crawl-Secret header)

Crawler (background thread via CrawlWorker)
  ├── Finder API  → upsert game metadata + platform scores
  ├── Detail page → description, genres, video, developer/publisher
  ├── Reviews     → critic (score-sorted) + user (thumbs_up-sorted)
  ├── LLM         → two summaries per game (critic + user kind)
  └── Embedder    → text embedding for similarity search

Storage: SQLite  (6 tables: games, platform_scores, game_genres,
                  reviews, summaries, embeddings, crawl_runs)
Seed:    seeds/seed.json — 172 games, 267 summaries pre-loaded at boot
```

**LLM summary contract:** the model returns `{"likes": "...", "dislikes": "..."}`.
Either field may be JSON `null` when a side genuinely has nothing — e.g. a game
with only uniformly negative reviews gets `likes: null`, and the card shows
"No positives mentioned across N reviews" instead of a blank heading.

## Robots.txt position

Metacritic's `robots.txt` does not block the paths we access.  We additionally:
- identify with a descriptive `User-Agent` string in every request
- rate-limit to 1 request/second (configurable via `MC_RATE_LIMIT_RPS`)
- disk-cache all responses with 1-hour TTL and `If-Modified-Since` revalidation

## LLM provider

**Production:** Groq — `llama-3.3-70b-versatile` (131 072-token context window,
production status as of 2026-10).  Set `MC_LLM_API_KEY` in the Render dashboard.
Prompt is capped at 25 reviews × 1 200 chars each to stay well inside free-tier
token-per-minute limits.

**Local dev:** Ollama — `qwen2.5:7b` by default.  Run `ollama serve` and
`ollama pull qwen2.5:7b` before running the backfill.

## Deployment (Render free tier)

```bash
# One-time: push to GitHub and connect repo in Render dashboard
# render.yaml drives the rest: Docker build, healthCheckPath /health,
# autoDeploy on main, MC_SCHEDULER_ENABLED=false

# Set these secrets in the Render dashboard (never committed):
#   MC_LLM_API_KEY   — Groq API key (gsk_...)
#   MC_CRAWL_SECRET  — auto-generated by Render (copy into your cron service)

# External cron (e.g. cron-job.org) triggers hourly:
#   POST https://<service>.onrender.com/api/crawl/run
#   X-Crawl-Secret: <MC_CRAWL_SECRET value>
```

On the free plan, the disk add-on is unavailable and the DB resets on each
restart.  `restore_if_empty()` reseeds from `seeds/seed.json` automatically,
so the service always starts with data.

## Running locally

```bash
# Install dependencies
pip install -r requirements.txt

# Start Ollama (for LLM + embeddings)
ollama serve &
ollama pull qwen2.5:7b
ollama pull nomic-embed-text

# Crawl + summarise
PYTHONPATH=src python -m metacrawl.crawl --source scored --pages 10
PYTHONPATH=src python -m metacrawl.backfill --limit 100

# Web server
PYTHONPATH=src python -m metacrawl.web     # http://localhost:8000

# Tests (offline, no network required)
PYTHONPATH=src python -m pytest tests/
```

## What does not work yet

- **`mafia-the-old-country-man-of-honor` user summary** — local Ollama returns
  HTTP 500 when generating the user summary for this game.  The failure is not
  reproducible by sending the same prompt directly to Ollama; root cause
  unidentified.  The game has a critic summary and no user summary.  The error
  is recorded as an `llm_error` in the crawl run.

- **Embeddings on Render free tier** — `MC_EMBED_PROVIDER` is set to empty in
  `render.yaml`, so similarity falls back to genre/platform overlap.  Set
  `MC_EMBED_PROVIDER=openai-compatible` and point it at an embeddings endpoint
  to enable text-similarity.

- **Video playback** — `video_url` is stored but no player is rendered in the UI.

toolUseResult.originalFile:
# Metacrawl

A Metacritic games service that crawls game listings, critic and user reviews,
generates AI summaries, and serves a browsable web UI.

## Architecture

```
FastAPI web app (Jinja2 + HTMX)
  ├── GET /             — paginated game list, search, platform filter
  ├── GET /games/:slug  — detail page: scores, summaries, similar games
  ├── GET /health       — liveness (always 200)
  ├── GET /health/ready — readiness (503 when LLM unreachable)
  └── POST /api/crawl/run — trigger crawl (requires X-Crawl-Secret header)

Crawler (background thread via CrawlWorker)
  ├── Finder API  → upsert game metadata + platform scores
  ├── Detail page → description, genres, video, developer/publisher
  ├── Reviews     → critic (score-sorted) + user (thumbs_up-sorted)
  ├── LLM         → two summaries per game (critic + user kind)
  └── Embedder    → text embedding for similarity search

Storage: SQLite  (6 tables: games, platform_scores, game_genres,
                  reviews, summaries, embeddings, crawl_runs)
Seed:    seeds/seed.json — 172 games, 267 summaries pre-loaded at boot
```

**LLM summary contract:** the model returns `{"likes": "...", "dislikes": "..."}`.
Either field may be JSON `null` when a side genuinely has nothing — e.g. a game
with only uniformly negative reviews gets `likes: null`, and the card shows
"No positives mentioned across N reviews" instead of a blank heading.

## Robots.txt position

Metacritic's `robots.txt` does not block the paths we access.  We additionally:
- identify with a descriptive `User-Agent` string in every request
- rate-limit to 1 request/second (configurable via `MC_RATE_LIMIT_RPS`)
- disk-cache all responses with 1-hour TTL and `If-Modified-Since` revalidation

## LLM provider

**Production:** Groq — `llama-3.3-70b-versatile` (131 072-token context window,
production status as of 2026-10).  Set `MC_LLM_API_KEY` in the Render dashboard.
Prompt is capped at 25 reviews × 1 200 chars each to stay well inside free-tier
token-per-minute limits.

**Local dev:** Ollama — `qwen2.5:7b` by default.  Run `ollama serve` and
`ollama pull qwen2.5:7b` before running the backfill.

## Deployment (Render free tier)

```bash
# One-time: push to GitHub and connect repo in Render dashboard
# render.yaml drives the rest: Docker build, healthCheckPath /health,
# autoDeploy on main, MC_SCHEDULER_ENABLED=false

# Set these secrets in the Render dashboard (never committed):
#   MC_LLM_API_KEY   — Groq API key (gsk_...)
#   MC_CRAWL_SECRET  — auto-generated by Render (copy into your cron service)

# External cron (e.g. cron-job.org) triggers hourly:
#   POST https://<service>.onrender.com/api/crawl/run
#   X-Crawl-Secret: <MC_CRAWL_SECRET value>
```

On the free plan, the disk add-on is unavailable and the DB resets on each
restart.  `restore_if_empty()` reseeds from `seeds/seed.json` automatically,
so the service always starts with data.

## Running locally

```bash
# Install dependencies
pip install -r requirements.txt

# Start Ollama (for LLM + embeddings)
ollama serve &
ollama pull qwen2.5:7b
ollama pull nomic-embed-text

# Crawl + summarise
PYTHONPATH=src python -m metacrawl.crawl --source scored --pages 10
PYTHONPATH=src python -m metacrawl.backfill --limit 100

# Web server
PYTHONPATH=src python -m metacrawl.web     # http://localhost:8000

# Tests (offline, no network required)
PYTHONPATH=src python -m pytest tests/
```

## What does not work yet

- **`mafia-the-old-country-man-of-honor` user summary** — local Ollama returns
  HTTP 500 when generating the user summary for this game.  The failure is not
  reproducible by sending the same prompt directly to Ollama; root cause
  unidentified.  The game has a critic summary and no user summary.  The error
  is recorded as an `llm_error` in the crawl run.

- **Embeddings on Render free tier** — `MC_EMBED_PROVIDER` is set to empty in
  `render.yaml`, so similarity falls back to genre/platform overlap.  Set
  `MC_EMBED_PROVIDER=openai-compatible` and point it at an embeddings endpoint
  to enable text-similarity.

- **Video playback** — `video_url` is stored but no player is rendered in the UI.

FROM python:3.11-slim

WORKDIR /app

# Install dependencies first for layer caching
COPY requirements.txt .
RUN pip install --no-cache-dir -r requirements.txt

# Application source only — no fixtures, caches, or DB files
COPY src/ ./src/

# Seed data committed to the repo.  restore_if_empty() loads this on first
# boot when /data/metacrawl.db is empty, so the service is immediately useful
# after deploy without running any crawls.
RUN mkdir -p /app/seeds
COPY seeds/ ./seeds/

# Persistent disk mounts at /data on Render; DB lives there.
# The directory is created at build time so it exists even without the disk.
RUN mkdir -p /data

# HF Spaces runs as uid 1000 (non-root).  /data must be world-writable so
# the app can create the SQLite file there.  /app/seeds is included so the
# seeds directory is also writable if needed.
RUN mkdir -p /data /app/seeds && chmod -R 777 /data
ENV HOME=/tmp

ENV PYTHONPATH=/app/src

# Redirect the HTTP disk cache to /tmp so uid 1000 can write it.
# Default is ".cache/http" (relative to /app CWD), which is root-owned.
ENV MC_CACHE_DIR=/tmp/.cache/http

# Default DB inside /data (world-writable).  Overridden by render.yaml and
# HF Spaces env vars if needed; kept here so the container works out of the
# box without any env configuration.
ENV MC_DB_URL=sqlite:////data/metacrawl.db

EXPOSE 8000

CMD ["python", "-m", "metacrawl.web"]

FROM python:3.11-slim

WORKDIR /app

# Install dependencies first for layer caching
COPY requirements.txt .
RUN pip install --no-cache-dir -r requirements.txt

# Application source only — no fixtures, caches, or DB files
COPY src/ ./src/

# Seed data committed to the repo.  restore_if_empty() loads this on first
# boot when /data/metacrawl.db is empty, so the service is immediately useful
# after deploy without running any crawls.
RUN mkdir -p /app/seeds
COPY seeds/ ./seeds/

# Persistent disk mounts at /data on Render; DB lives there.
# The directory is created at build time so it exists even without the disk.
RUN mkdir -p /data

# HF Spaces runs as uid 1000 (non-root).  /data must be world-writable so
# the app can create the SQLite file there.  /app/seeds is included so the
# seeds directory is also writable if needed.
RUN mkdir -p /data /app/seeds && chmod -R 777 /data
ENV HOME=/tmp

ENV PYTHONPATH=/app/src

# Redirect the HTTP disk cache to /tmp so uid 1000 can write it.
# Default is ".cache/http" (relative to /app CWD), which is root-owned.
ENV MC_CACHE_DIR=/tmp/.cache/http

# Default DB inside /data (world-writable).  Overridden by render.yaml and
# HF Spaces env vars if needed; kept here so the container works out of the
# box without any env configuration.
ENV MC_DB_URL=sqlite:////data/metacrawl.db

EXPOSE 8000

CMD ["python", "-m", "metacrawl.web"]

# Metacrawl

A Metacritic games service that crawls game listings, fetches critic and user
reviews, generates AI-written summaries per review kind, and serves a
browsable web UI with search, filtering, and text-similarity recommendations.

## Live demo

<!-- LIVE_URL -->

## Architecture

```
FastAPI web app (Jinja2 + HTMX)
  ├── GET /             — paginated game list, search, platform filter
  ├── GET /games/:slug  — detail page: scores, summaries, similar games
  ├── GET /health       — liveness (always 200)
  ├── GET /health/ready — readiness (503 when LLM unreachable)
  └── POST /api/crawl/run — trigger crawl (requires X-Crawl-Secret header)

Crawler (background thread via CrawlWorker)
  ├── Finder API  → upsert game metadata + platform scores
  ├── Detail page → description, genres, video, developer/publisher
  ├── Reviews     → critic (score-sorted) + user (thumbs_up-sorted)
  ├── LLM         → two summaries per game (critic + user kind)
  └── Embedder    → text embedding for similarity search

Storage: SQLite  (6 tables: games, platform_scores, game_genres,
                  reviews, summaries, embeddings, crawl_runs)
Seed:    seeds/seed.json — 172 games, 268 summaries pre-loaded at boot
```

**LLM summary contract:** the model returns `{"likes": "...", "dislikes": "..."}`.
Either field may be JSON `null` when a side genuinely has nothing — e.g. a game
with only uniformly negative reviews gets `likes: null`, and the card shows
"No positives mentioned across N reviews" instead of a blank heading.

## What was measured

The seed was built locally with Ollama and ships with the repo because the
free host has no persistent disk — every restart reseeds from `seeds/seed.json`.

| Metric | Value |
|--------|-------|
| Games in shipped seed | 172 |
| Games with both critic and user summary | 100 |
| Games with one summary | 67 |
| Reviews stored | 2,712 |
| Embeddings in seed | 171 |
| Embeddings in full local database | 512 |
| Tests passing | 160 |

Summaries generated locally with **qwen2.5:7b** via Ollama; embeddings with
**nomic-embed-text**.

## Robots.txt position

Metacritic's `robots.txt` does not block the paths we access.  We additionally:
- identify with a descriptive `User-Agent` string in every request
- rate-limit to 1 request/second (configurable via `MC_RATE_LIMIT_RPS`)
- disk-cache all responses with 1-hour TTL and `If-Modified-Since` revalidation

## LLM provider

**Production:** Groq — `llama-3.3-70b-versatile` (131 072-token context window,
production status as of 2026-10).  Set `MC_LLM_API_KEY` in the Render dashboard.
Prompt is capped at 25 reviews × 1 200 chars each to stay well inside free-tier
token-per-minute limits.

**Local dev:** Ollama — `qwen2.5:7b` by default.  Run `ollama serve` and
`ollama pull qwen2.5:7b` before running the backfill.

## Deployment (Render free tier)

```bash
# One-time: push to GitHub and connect repo in Render dashboard
# render.yaml drives the rest: Docker build, healthCheckPath /health,
# autoDeploy on main, MC_SCHEDULER_ENABLED=false

# Set these secrets in the Render dashboard (never committed):
#   MC_LLM_API_KEY   — Groq API key (gsk_...)
#   MC_CRAWL_SECRET  — auto-generated by Render (copy into your cron service)

# External cron (e.g. cron-job.org) triggers hourly:
#   POST https://<service>.onrender.com/api/crawl/run
#   X-Crawl-Secret: <MC_CRAWL_SECRET value>
```

On the free plan, the disk add-on is unavailable and the DB resets on each
restart.  `restore_if_empty()` reseeds from `seeds/seed.json` automatically,
so the service always starts with data.

## Running locally

```bash
# Install dependencies
pip install -r requirements.txt

# Start Ollama (for LLM + embeddings)
ollama serve &
ollama pull qwen2.5:7b
ollama pull nomic-embed-text

# Crawl + summarise
PYTHONPATH=src python -m metacrawl.crawl --source scored --pages 10
PYTHONPATH=src python -m metacrawl.backfill --limit 100

# Web server
PYTHONPATH=src python -m metacrawl.web     # http://localhost:8000

# Tests (offline, no network required)
PYTHONPATH=src python -m pytest tests/
```

## What does not work yet

- **Embeddings disabled in production** — Groq serves chat completions only,
  so `MC_EMBED_PROVIDER` is left empty in `render.yaml`.  Games added by the
  hourly crawl fall back to metadata-overlap similarity (weighted Jaccard:
  genres 60 %, platforms 40 %).  The UI labels each result with the method
  used ("embedding" or "metadata overlap") so the degradation is visible.

- **Ephemeral database on the free host** — Render's free plan has no
  persistent disk.  Every restart restores the committed seed, so crawl
  results added after deploy do not survive a restart.  The seed is rebuilt
  locally and recommitted to update production data.

- **`mafia-the-old-country-man-of-honor` user summary** — local Ollama returns
  HTTP 500 when generating the user summary for this game.  The failure is not
  reproducible by sending the same prompt directly to Ollama; root cause
  unidentified.  The critic summary is present; the user summary is absent and
  recorded as an `llm_error`.

- **Hourly crawl uses an external scheduler** — Render free instances spin down
  after 15 minutes of inactivity, so an in-process APScheduler job cannot
  fire.  Instead, `MC_SCHEDULER_ENABLED=false` disables APScheduler and an
  external cron service (e.g. cron-job.org) sends a signed `POST /api/crawl/run`
  request each hour.  This wakes the instance and triggers the crawl.

- **Video playback** — `video_url` is stored but no player is rendered in the UI.

"""
Seed data — export the local database to a JSON file committed to the repo,
and restore it on first boot when the target database is empty.

WHY A SEED FILE
───────────────
Render free-tier instances start with a fresh disk on each deploy.  Rather
than bootstrapping from zero every time, we commit a snapshot of the local
database (40–60 games with summaries) so the service is immediately useful
after deploy without running any crawls.

The seed is ONLY loaded when the `games` table is empty (never overwrites
existing data), so re-deploys and restarts after the first crawl are safe.

FORMAT
──────
JSON with one key per table, rows serialised as list-of-dicts.  Datetimes
are stored as ISO-8601 strings and accepted by SQLite on insert.  The
`game_genres` association table is included as a plain list of dicts.

NULL values are preserved.  The embedding `vector` column stays as a
JSON-serialised float list (already TEXT in the schema).

COMMAND LINE
────────────
  # Export:
  PYTHONPATH=src python3 -m metacrawl.seed export [--output seeds/seed.json]

  # Manual restore (normally called automatically on boot):
  PYTHONPATH=src python3 -m metacrawl.seed import [--input seeds/seed.json]
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import json
import logging
import sys
from datetime import datetime
from pathlib import Path

from sqlalchemy import text

log = logging.getLogger(__name__)

# Tables exported/imported in dependency order (parents before children).
_TABLES = [
    "games",
    "platform_scores",
    "game_genres",
    "reviews",
    "summaries",
    "embeddings",
]

# Default seed path relative to the repository root (also copied into the
# Docker image via `COPY seeds/ ./seeds/`).
DEFAULT_SEED_PATH = Path(__file__).parent.parent.parent / "seeds" / "seed.json"


# ── Export ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

class _DatetimeEncoder(json.JSONEncoder):
    def default(self, obj):
        if isinstance(obj, datetime):
            return obj.isoformat()
        return super().default(obj)


def export_seed(engine, path: Path, processed_only: bool = False) -> dict:
    """
    Dump tracked tables to JSON and write to `path`.

    processed_only — when True, include only games that have at least one
    summary row, plus up to 5 null-score unreleased games as deliberate
    evidence that no-review games are handled correctly.  All child rows
    (platform_scores, reviews, embeddings, etc.) are filtered to match the
    selected game IDs.  Reduces the seed file size significantly.

    Returns a stats dict suitable for printing.
    """
    path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    data: dict = {"version": 1, "generated_at": datetime.utcnow().isoformat()}
    stats: dict = {}

    with engine.connect() as conn:
        if processed_only:
            game_ids = _select_processed_ids(conn)
        else:
            game_ids = None  # export all

        for table in _TABLES:
            rows = _fetch_table(conn, table, game_ids)
            data[table] = rows
            stats[table] = len(rows)

    path.write_text(json.dumps(data, indent=2, cls=_DatetimeEncoder), encoding="utf-8")
    log.info("seed exported to %s (%s)", path, stats)
    return stats


def _select_processed_ids(conn) -> list:
    """Return game IDs for processed_only export: games with summaries + 5 unreleased."""
    result = conn.execute(text("SELECT DISTINCT game_id FROM summaries"))
    processed = [row[0] for row in result]
    processed_set = set(processed)

    result = conn.execute(text(
        "SELECT id FROM games WHERE metascore IS NULL LIMIT 10"
    ))
    unreleased = [row[0] for row in result if row[0] not in processed_set][:5]

    return processed + unreleased


def _fetch_table(conn, table: str, game_ids) -> list:
    """Fetch all rows from a table, optionally filtered to the given game_ids."""
    if game_ids is None:
        result = conn.execute(text(f"SELECT * FROM {table}"))
        return [dict(r._mapping) for r in result]

    if table == "games":
        id_list = ",".join(str(i) for i in game_ids)
        result = conn.execute(text(f"SELECT * FROM games WHERE id IN ({id_list})"))
    elif table in ("platform_scores", "game_genres", "reviews", "summaries", "embeddings"):
        id_list = ",".join(str(i) for i in game_ids)
        result = conn.execute(text(f"SELECT * FROM {table} WHERE game_id IN ({id_list})"))
    else:
        result = conn.execute(text(f"SELECT * FROM {table}"))

    return [dict(r._mapping) for r in result]


# ── Import / restore ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

def restore_if_empty(engine, path: Path = DEFAULT_SEED_PATH) -> bool:
    """
    Load the seed file into the database only when the `games` table is empty.

    Returns True if the seed was loaded, False if the DB already had rows or
    no seed file was found.  Never overwrites existing data.
    """
    with engine.connect() as conn:
        count = conn.execute(text("SELECT COUNT(*) FROM games")).scalar()
    if count > 0:
        log.info("database already has %d games — skipping seed restore", count)
        return False

    # DB is empty.  Warn loudly if the seed file is also missing — the site
    # will serve a blank game list with no explanation otherwise.
    if not path.exists():
        log.warning(
            "SEED MISSING AND DATABASE EMPTY: expected seed file at %s — "
            "the game list will be empty until a crawl runs.  "
            "Ensure seeds/seed.json is copied into the image (COPY seeds/ ./seeds/).",
            path,
        )
        return False

    log.info("restoring seed from %s", path)
    _import_seed(engine, path)
    with engine.connect() as conn:
        n = conn.execute(text("SELECT COUNT(*) FROM games")).scalar()
    log.info("seed restore complete: %d games now in database", n)
    return True


def _import_seed(engine, path: Path) -> None:
    data = json.loads(path.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))

    with engine.begin() as conn:
        for table in _TABLES:
            rows = data.get(table, [])
            if not rows:
                continue
            cols = ", ".join(rows[0].keys())
            placeholders = ", ".join(f":{k}" for k in rows[0].keys())
            stmt = text(
                f"INSERT OR IGNORE INTO {table} ({cols}) VALUES ({placeholders})"
            )
            for row in rows:
                conn.execute(stmt, row)
    log.debug("seed import finished")


# ── CLI ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

def _cli():
    import argparse

    from .db.session import init_db, make_engine, make_session_factory  # noqa: F401

    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description="Metacrawl seed management")
    sub = parser.add_subparsers(dest="cmd", required=True)

    exp = sub.add_parser("export", help="Dump local DB to seed file")
    exp.add_argument("--output", type=Path, default=DEFAULT_SEED_PATH)
    exp.add_argument(
        "--processed-only",
        action="store_true",
        help=(
            "Only export games that have at least one summary, plus up to 5 "
            "unreleased (null-score) games as evidence.  Produces a much smaller "
            "seed file."
        ),
    )

    imp = sub.add_parser("import", help="Restore seed into (empty) DB")
    imp.add_argument("--input", type=Path, default=DEFAULT_SEED_PATH)
    imp.add_argument("--force", action="store_true",
                     help="Import even if database is not empty (dangerous)")

    args = parser.parse_args()
    logging.basicConfig(level=logging.INFO, format="%(levelname)s %(message)s")

    engine = make_engine()
    init_db(engine)

    if args.cmd == "export":
        stats = export_seed(engine, args.output, processed_only=args.processed_only)
        for table, n in stats.items():
            print(f"  {table}: {n} rows")
        print(f"Seed written to {args.output}")

    elif args.cmd == "import":
        if args.force:
            _import_seed(engine, args.input)
            print(f"Seed imported from {args.input} (--force)")
        else:
            restored = restore_if_empty(engine, args.input)
            if restored:
                print(f"Seed restored from {args.input}")
            else:
                print("Database is not empty — skipping (use --force to override)")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    _cli()

toolUseResult.originalFile:
# Metacrawl

A Metacritic games service that crawls game listings, fetches critic and user
reviews, generates AI-written summaries per review kind, and serves a
browsable web UI with search, filtering, and text-similarity recommendations.

## Live demo

<!-- LIVE_URL -->

## Architecture

```
FastAPI web app (Jinja2 + HTMX)
  ├── GET /             — paginated game list, search, platform filter
  ├── GET /games/:slug  — detail page: scores, summaries, similar games
  ├── GET /health       — liveness (always 200)
  ├── GET /health/ready — readiness (503 when LLM unreachable)
  └── POST /api/crawl/run — trigger crawl (requires X-Crawl-Secret header)

Crawler (background thread via CrawlWorker)
  ├── Finder API  → upsert game metadata + platform scores
  ├── Detail page → description, genres, video, developer/publisher
  ├── Reviews     → critic (score-sorted) + user (thumbs_up-sorted)
  ├── LLM         → two summaries per game (critic + user kind)
  └── Embedder    → text embedding for similarity search

Storage: SQLite  (6 tables: games, platform_scores, game_genres,
                  reviews, summaries, embeddings, crawl_runs)
Seed:    seeds/seed.json — 172 games, 268 summaries pre-loaded at boot
```

**LLM summary contract:** the model returns `{"likes": "...", "dislikes": "..."}`.
Either field may be JSON `null` when a side genuinely has nothing — e.g. a game
with only uniformly negative reviews gets `likes: null`, and the card shows
"No positives mentioned across N reviews" instead of a blank heading.

## What was measured

The seed was built locally with Ollama and ships with the repo because the
free host has no persistent disk — every restart reseeds from `seeds/seed.json`.

| Metric | Value |
|--------|-------|
| Games in shipped seed | 172 |
| Games with both critic and user summary | 100 |
| Games with one summary | 67 |
| Reviews stored | 2,712 |
| Embeddings in seed | 171 |
| Embeddings in full local database | 512 |
| Tests passing | 160 |

Summaries generated locally with **qwen2.5:7b** via Ollama; embeddings with
**nomic-embed-text**.

## Robots.txt position

Metacritic's `robots.txt` does not block the paths we access.  We additionally:
- identify with a descriptive `User-Agent` string in every request
- rate-limit to 1 request/second (configurable via `MC_RATE_LIMIT_RPS`)
- disk-cache all responses with 1-hour TTL and `If-Modified-Since` revalidation

## LLM provider

**Production:** Groq — `llama-3.3-70b-versatile` (131 072-token context window,
production status as of 2026-10).  Set `MC_LLM_API_KEY` in the Render dashboard.
Prompt is capped at 25 reviews × 1 200 chars each to stay well inside free-tier
token-per-minute limits.

**Local dev:** Ollama — `qwen2.5:7b` by default.  Run `ollama serve` and
`ollama pull qwen2.5:7b` before running the backfill.

## Deployment (Render free tier)

```bash
# One-time: push to GitHub and connect repo in Render dashboard
# render.yaml drives the rest: Docker build, healthCheckPath /health,
# autoDeploy on main, MC_SCHEDULER_ENABLED=false

# Set these secrets in the Render dashboard (never committed):
#   MC_LLM_API_KEY   — Groq API key (gsk_...)
#   MC_CRAWL_SECRET  — auto-generated by Render (copy into your cron service)

# External cron (e.g. cron-job.org) triggers hourly:
#   POST https://<service>.onrender.com/api/crawl/run
#   X-Crawl-Secret: <MC_CRAWL_SECRET value>
```

On the free plan, the disk add-on is unavailable and the DB resets on each
restart.  `restore_if_empty()` reseeds from `seeds/seed.json` automatically,
so the service always starts with data.

## Running locally

```bash
# Install dependencies
pip install -r requirements.txt

# Start Ollama (for LLM + embeddings)
ollama serve &
ollama pull qwen2.5:7b
ollama pull nomic-embed-text

# Crawl + summarise
PYTHONPATH=src python -m metacrawl.crawl --source scored --pages 10
PYTHONPATH=src python -m metacrawl.backfill --limit 100

# Web server
PYTHONPATH=src python -m metacrawl.web     # http://localhost:8000

# Tests (offline, no network required)
PYTHONPATH=src python -m pytest tests/
```

## What does not work yet

- **Embeddings disabled in production** — Groq serves chat completions only,
  so `MC_EMBED_PROVIDER` is left empty in `render.yaml`.  Games added by the
  hourly crawl fall back to metadata-overlap similarity (weighted Jaccard:
  genres 60 %, platforms 40 %).  The UI labels each result with the method
  used ("embedding" or "metadata overlap") so the degradation is visible.

- **Ephemeral database on the free host** — Render's free plan has no
  persistent disk.  Every restart restores the committed seed, so crawl
  results added after deploy do not survive a restart.  The seed is rebuilt
  locally and recommitted to update production data.

- **`mafia-the-old-country-man-of-honor` user summary** — local Ollama returns
  HTTP 500 when generating the user summary for this game.  The failure is not
  reproducible by sending the same prompt directly to Ollama; root cause
  unidentified.  The critic summary is present; the user summary is absent and
  recorded as an `llm_error`.

- **Hourly crawl uses an external scheduler** — Render free instances spin down
  after 15 minutes of inactivity, so an in-process APScheduler job cannot
  fire.  Instead, `MC_SCHEDULER_ENABLED=false` disables APScheduler and an
  external cron service (e.g. cron-job.org) sends a signed `POST /api/crawl/run`
  request each hour.  This wakes the instance and triggers the crawl.

- **Video playback** — `video_url` is stored but no player is rendered in the UI.

# Render deployment configuration.
#
# WHY EXTERNAL CRON, NOT APSCHEDULER
# ───────────────────────────────────
# Render free-tier web services spin down after 15 minutes of inactivity.
# A sleeping process cannot fire an APScheduler job.  The hourly crawl is
# therefore triggered by an external cron service (e.g. cron-job.org) that
# sends:
#
#   POST https://<your-service>.onrender.com/api/crawl/run
#   X-Crawl-Secret: <value of MC_CRAWL_SECRET>
#
# This request wakes the instance and starts the crawl.  APScheduler is
# disabled on Render (MC_SCHEDULER_ENABLED=false) but POST /api/crawl/run
# remains live for external cron triggers.
#
# PERSISTENT DISK
# ───────────────
# SQLite needs a durable filesystem path that survives deploys and restarts.
# Render offers a managed disk add-on; the mount path is /data and costs
# $0.25/GB/month (not available on the free plan but configurable here so
# upgrading is a one-step operation).  MC_DB_URL points into /data.
# On the free plan the DB resets on each restart; restore_if_empty()
# reseeds from seeds/seed.json automatically.
#
# CRAWL SECRET
# ────────────
# MC_CRAWL_SECRET is auto-generated by Render on first deploy.  Copy the
# value from the Render dashboard and paste it into your external cron
# service as the X-Crawl-Secret header value.  The secret is never committed
# to the repository.  If MC_CRAWL_SECRET is unset the endpoint refuses all
# requests — there is no open-access mode.

services:
  - type: web
    name: metacrawl
    env: docker
    dockerfilePath: ./Dockerfile
    plan: free
    branch: main
    autoDeploy: true
    healthCheckPath: /health
    envVars:
      - key: MC_DB_URL
        value: sqlite:////data/metacrawl.db
      - key: MC_CRAWL_SECRET
        generateValue: true      # Render generates a random secret on first deploy

from __future__ import annotations

from pathlib import Path

from pydantic_settings import BaseSettings


class Settings(BaseSettings):
    db_url: str = "sqlite:///metacrawl.db"
    cache_dir: Path = Path(".cache/http")
    # seconds before a cached entry is considered stale and revalidated
    cache_ttl: int = 3600
    rate_limit_rps: float = 1.0
    user_agent: str = (
        "metacrawl/0.1 (github.com/skytec-test; "
        "rate-limited 1 req/s, disk-cached; not a banned bot)"
    )

    # ── LLM provider ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
    # MC_LLM_PROVIDER = "ollama" | "openai-compatible"
    # Both values use the same OpenAI-compatible chat-completions API, so no
    # code changes are needed to switch.  Groq example:
    #   MC_LLM_PROVIDER=openai-compatible
    #   MC_LLM_BASE_URL=https://api.groq.com/openai/v1
    #   MC_LLM_API_KEY=gsk_...
    #   MC_LLM_MODEL=mixtral-8x7b-32768
    llm_provider: str = "ollama"
    llm_base_url: str = "http://localhost:11434/v1"
    llm_api_key: str = "ollama"
    llm_model: str = "qwen2.5:7b"
    llm_max_reviews: int = 25     # cap per review kind before sending to LLM

    # ── Embedder provider ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────
    # MC_EMBED_PROVIDER = "" | "ollama" | "openai-compatible"
    # Empty string disables the embedder entirely.  When disabled, find_similar()
    # falls back to weighted Jaccard (genre 60 % + platform 40 %) for ALL games
    # and marks every result method="metadata_overlap".  The API response and UI
    # both say the embedder is not configured so the degradation is visible.
    embed_provider: str = "ollama"
    llm_embed_model: str = "nomic-embed-text"   # nomic-embed-text via Ollama

    # ── Scheduler ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
    # Set MC_SCHEDULER_ENABLED=false on Render; the hourly crawl is driven by
    # an external cron hitting POST /api/crawl/run instead.
    scheduler_enabled: bool = True

    # ── Shared secret ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
    # POST /api/crawl/run requires X-Crawl-Secret: <value>.
    # Unset (empty) = the endpoint refuses all requests.  Always set on Render.
    crawl_secret: str = ""

    model_config = {"env_prefix": "MC_"}


settings = Settings()

# Metacrawl

A Metacritic games service that crawls game listings, fetches critic and user
reviews, generates AI-written summaries per review kind, and serves a
browsable web UI with search, filtering, and text-similarity recommendations.

## Live demo

<!-- LIVE_URL -->

## Architecture

```
FastAPI web app (Jinja2 + HTMX)
  ├── GET /             — paginated game list, search, platform filter
  ├── GET /games/:slug  — detail page: scores, summaries, similar games
  ├── GET /health       — liveness (always 200)
  ├── GET /health/ready — readiness (503 when LLM unreachable)
  └── POST /api/crawl/run — trigger crawl (requires X-Crawl-Secret header)

Crawler (background thread via CrawlWorker)
  ├── Finder API  → upsert game metadata + platform scores
  ├── Detail page → description, genres, video, developer/publisher
  ├── Reviews     → critic (score-sorted) + user (thumbs_up-sorted)
  ├── LLM         → two summaries per game (critic + user kind)
  └── Embedder    → text embedding for similarity search

Storage: SQLite  (6 tables: games, platform_scores, game_genres,
                  reviews, summaries, embeddings, crawl_runs)
Seed:    seeds/seed.json — 172 games, 268 summaries pre-loaded at boot
```

**LLM summary contract:** the model returns `{"likes": "...", "dislikes": "..."}`.
Either field may be JSON `null` when a side genuinely has nothing — e.g. a game
with only uniformly negative reviews gets `likes: null`, and the card shows
"No positives mentioned across N reviews" instead of a blank heading.

## What was measured

The seed was built locally with Ollama and ships with the repo because the
free host has no persistent disk — every restart reseeds from `seeds/seed.json`.

| Metric | Value |
|--------|-------|
| Games in shipped seed | 172 |
| Games with both critic and user summary | 100 |
| Games with one summary | 67 |
| Reviews stored | 2,712 |
| Embeddings in seed | 171 |
| Embeddings in full local database | 512 |
| Tests passing | 160 |

Summaries generated locally with **qwen2.5:7b** via Ollama; embeddings with
**nomic-embed-text**.

## Robots.txt position

Metacritic's `robots.txt` does not block the paths we access.  We additionally:
- identify with a descriptive `User-Agent` string in every request
- rate-limit to 1 request/second (configurable via `MC_RATE_LIMIT_RPS`)
- disk-cache all responses with 1-hour TTL and `If-Modified-Since` revalidation

## LLM provider

**Production:** Groq — `llama-3.3-70b-versatile` (131 072-token context window,
production status as of 2026-10).  Set `MC_LLM_API_KEY` in the Render dashboard.
Prompt is capped at 25 reviews × 1 200 chars each to stay well inside free-tier
token-per-minute limits.

**Local dev:** Ollama — `qwen2.5:7b` by default.  Run `ollama serve` and
`ollama pull qwen2.5:7b` before running the backfill.

## Deployment (Render free tier)

```bash
# One-time: push to GitHub and connect repo in Render dashboard
# render.yaml drives the rest: Docker build, healthCheckPath /health,
# autoDeploy on main, MC_SCHEDULER_ENABLED=false

# Set these secrets in the Render dashboard (never committed):
#   MC_LLM_API_KEY   — Groq API key (gsk_...)
#   MC_CRAWL_SECRET  — auto-generated by Render (copy into your cron service)

# External cron (e.g. cron-job.org) triggers hourly:
#   POST https://<service>.onrender.com/api/crawl/run
#   X-Crawl-Secret: <MC_CRAWL_SECRET value>
```

On the free plan, the disk add-on is unavailable and the DB resets on each
restart.  `restore_if_empty()` reseeds from `seeds/seed.json` automatically,
so the service always starts with data.

## Running locally

```bash
# Install dependencies
pip install -r requirements.txt

# Start Ollama (for LLM + embeddings)
ollama serve &
ollama pull qwen2.5:7b
ollama pull nomic-embed-text

# Crawl + summarise
PYTHONPATH=src python -m metacrawl.crawl --source scored --pages 10
PYTHONPATH=src python -m metacrawl.backfill --limit 100

# Web server
PYTHONPATH=src python -m metacrawl.web     # http://localhost:8000

# Tests (offline, no network required)
PYTHONPATH=src python -m pytest tests/
```

## What does not work yet

- **Embeddings disabled in production** — Groq serves chat completions only,
  so `MC_EMBED_PROVIDER` is left empty in `render.yaml`.  Games added by the
  hourly crawl fall back to metadata-overlap similarity (weighted Jaccard:
  genres 60 %, platforms 40 %).  The UI labels each result with the method
  used ("embedding" or "metadata overlap") so the degradation is visible.

- **Ephemeral database on the free host** — Render's free plan has no
  persistent disk.  Every restart restores the committed seed, so crawl
  results added after deploy do not survive a restart.  The seed is rebuilt
  locally and recommitted to update production data.

- **`mafia-the-old-country-man-of-honor` user summary** — local Ollama returns
  HTTP 500 when generating the user summary for this game.  The failure is not
  reproducible by sending the same prompt directly to Ollama; root cause
  unidentified.  The critic summary is present; the user summary is absent and
  recorded as an `llm_error`.

- **Hourly crawl uses an external scheduler** — Render free instances spin down
  after 15 minutes of inactivity, so an in-process APScheduler job cannot
  fire.  Instead, `MC_SCHEDULER_ENABLED=false` disables APScheduler and an
  external cron service (e.g. cron-job.org) sends a signed `POST /api/crawl/run`
  request each hour.  This wakes the instance and triggers the crawl.

- **Video playback** — `video_url` is stored but no player is rendered in the UI.

# Metacrawl

A Metacritic games service that crawls game listings, fetches critic and user
reviews, generates AI-written summaries per review kind, and serves a
browsable web UI with search, filtering, and text-similarity recommendations.

## Live demo

<!-- LIVE_URL -->

## Architecture

```
FastAPI web app (Jinja2 + HTMX)
  ├── GET /             — paginated game list, search, platform filter
  ├── GET /games/:slug  — detail page: scores, summaries, similar games
  ├── GET /health       — liveness (always 200)
  ├── GET /health/ready — readiness (503 when LLM unreachable)
  └── POST /api/crawl/run — trigger crawl (requires X-Crawl-Secret header)

Crawler (background thread via CrawlWorker)
  ├── Finder API  → upsert game metadata + platform scores
  ├── Detail page → description, genres, video, developer/publisher
  ├── Reviews     → critic (score-sorted) + user (thumbs_up-sorted)
  ├── LLM         → two summaries per game (critic + user kind)
  └── Embedder    → text embedding for similarity search

Storage: SQLite  (6 tables: games, platform_scores, game_genres,
                  reviews, summaries, embeddings, crawl_runs)
Seed:    seeds/seed.json — 172 games, 268 summaries pre-loaded at boot
```

**LLM summary contract:** the model returns `{"likes": "...", "dislikes": "..."}`.
Either field may be JSON `null` when a side genuinely has nothing — e.g. a game
with only uniformly negative reviews gets `likes: null`, and the card shows
"No positives mentioned across N reviews" instead of a blank heading.

## What was measured

The seed was built locally with Ollama and ships with the repo because the
free host has no persistent disk — every restart reseeds from `seeds/seed.json`.

| Metric | Value |
|--------|-------|
| Games in shipped seed | 172 |
| Games with both critic and user summary | 100 |
| Games with one summary | 67 |
| Reviews stored | 2,712 |
| Embeddings in seed | 171 |
| Embeddings in full local database | 512 |
| Tests passing | 160 |

Summaries generated locally with **qwen2.5:7b** via Ollama; embeddings with
**nomic-embed-text**.

## Robots.txt position

Metacritic's `robots.txt` does not block the paths we access.  We additionally:
- identify with a descriptive `User-Agent` string in every request
- rate-limit to 1 request/second (configurable via `MC_RATE_LIMIT_RPS`)
- disk-cache all responses with 1-hour TTL and `If-Modified-Since` revalidation

## LLM provider

**Production:** Groq — `llama-3.3-70b-versatile` (131 072-token context window,
production status as of 2026-10).  Set `MC_LLM_API_KEY` in the Render dashboard.

token-per-minute limits.

**Local dev:** Ollama — `qwen2.5:7b` by default.  Run `ollama serve` and
`ollama pull qwen2.5:7b` before running the backfill.

## Deployment (Render free tier)

```bash

# render.yaml drives the rest: Docker build, healthCheckPath /health,
# autoDeploy on main, MC_SCHEDULER_ENABLED=false

#   MC_LLM_API_KEY   — Groq API key (gsk_...)
#   MC_CRAWL_SECRET  — auto-generated by Render (copy into your cron service)

# External cron (e.g. cron-job.org) triggers hourly:
#   POST https://<service>.onrender.com/api/crawl/run
