```bash
pip install -r requirements.txt

# Start Ollama (for LLM + embeddings)
ollama serve &
ollama pull qwen2.5:7b
ollama pull nomic-embed-text

# Crawl + summarise
PYTHONPATH=src python -m metacrawl.crawl --source scored --pages 10
PYTHONPATH=src python -m metacrawl.backfill --limit 100

# Web server
PYTHONPATH=src python -m metacrawl.web     # http://localhost:8000

# Tests (offline, no network required)
PYTHONPATH=src python -m pytest tests/
```

## What does not work yet

- **Embeddings disabled in production** — Groq serves chat completions only,
  so `MC_EMBED_PROVIDER` is left empty in `render.yaml`.  Games added by the
  hourly crawl fall back to metadata-overlap similarity (weighted Jaccard:
  genres 60 %, platforms 40 %).  The UI labels each result with the method
  used ("embedding" or "metadata overlap") so the degradation is visible.

- **Ephemeral database on the free host** — Render's free plan has no
  persistent disk.  Every restart restores the committed seed, so crawl
  results added after deploy do not survive a restart.  The seed is rebuilt
  locally and recommitted to update production data.

- **`mafia-the-old-country-man-of-honor` user summary** — local Ollama returns
  HTTP 500 when generating the user summary for this game.  The failure is not
  reproducible by sending the same prompt directly to Ollama; root cause
  unidentified.  The critic summary is present; the user summary is absent and
  recorded as an `llm_error`.

- **Hourly crawl uses an external scheduler** — Render free instances spin down
  after 15 minutes of inactivity, so an in-process APScheduler job cannot
  fire.  Instead, `MC_SCHEDULER_ENABLED=false` disables APScheduler and an
  external cron service (e.g. cron-job.org) sends a signed `POST /api/crawl/run`
  request each hour.  This wakes the instance and triggers the crawl.

- **Video playback** — `video_url` is stored but no player is rendered in the UI.

message.content: Three bugs on the live deployment. Fix in this order. 1. COVER IMAGES — every card on the live site is a broken image. Diagnosed: the composed URL is invalid, not blocked. https://www.metacritic.com/a/img/resize/460/215/catalog/provider/6/12/6-1-1087502-52.jpg returns 403 even with a browser User-Agent AND Referer: metacritic.com. So _image_url() composing IMAGE_BASE + width + height + "catalog" + bucketPath does not produce a real CDN path. Fix by reading real URLs instead of constructing them: - Open tests/fixtures/game.html and browse.html. Find what Metacritic's own markup uses as the for a game cover. Report the exact format, including any hash or token segment between /resize/ and the path. - Check the detail payload's product.item images object (BRIEF 1.3) for a field carrying a complete URL. - Use the real URL wherever the payload supplies one. Only fall back to composition if you can prove the composed form actually resolves — verify with curl, do not assume. - If NO complete URL exists anywhere in the payload, say so and stop; we will proxy or drop covers rather than ship broken images. - Add a test asserting a parsed game's cover_url matches the real format. - Once fixed, you will need to re-fetch covers for the 172 seeded games and re-export the seed. Write that as a small backfill pass; don't re-crawl everything. 2. llm_errors: 2 on the first production crawl — 2 games created, 0 summaries. Groq is reachable, so it fails after the connection. - Get the actual exception from the Render logs (widen the time window to the last hour and search "llm") or reproduce locally against Groq with llama-3.3-70b-versatile. - Likely the model returns JSON wrapped in a ```json fence, or ignores the null sentinel we added. Make the parser tolerant of fenced JSON; use Groq's JSON mode if the model supports it. - Add a test using the model's actual bad response as the fixture. - Do not widen validation to let malformed summaries through. 3. The "Run crawl" button does nothing. curl with X-Crawl-Secret works, so the button POSTs without it and HTMX silently swallows the 403. - Either authenticate server-side so the browser never holds the secret, or surface the error in the badge. A silent failure is worse than no button. - Add a test. Report findings for all three before pushing.

"""

SKIP RULES (both enforced before calling the LLM):
  1. A game with zero reviews of the relevant kind gets no summary row.
     New releases are unreleased; this is the common case, not the edge case.
  2. A game whose reviews are all missing quote text is treated as zero reviews.
     Summaries must come from actual review text, never from descriptions.

  critic: top MC_LLM_MAX_REVIEWS by score DESC (highest-rated critics first)
  user:   top MC_LLM_MAX_REVIEWS by thumbs_up DESC, then by review_date DESC
          (most-helpful users first; falls back to recency when thumbsUp is null)

  The rule name is stored in Summary.sampling_rule so downstream code can
  reason about what went into each summary.

NULL SENTINEL CONTRACT:
  The model may return null for likes or dislikes when that side genuinely
  has nothing — e.g. uniformly negative reviews → likes: null.  null is
  stored as-is and the card renders an explanatory line instead of a blank.
  Empty string or a string shorter than _MIN_SUMMARY_LEN is the truncation
  shape and is still rejected as a malformed response.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import json
import logging
from datetime import datetime
from typing import Callable

from sqlalchemy import delete
from sqlalchemy.orm import Session

from .config import settings
from .db.models import Game, Review, Summary

log = logging.getLogger(__name__)

_PROMPT = """\
Summarise the following {n} {kind} reviews for the game "{title}".

Reviews:
{reviews_text}

Reply with ONLY valid JSON (no markdown fences, no extra keys):
{{"likes": "2-3 sentences on what reviewers praised, or null if the reviews contain no praise",\
 "dislikes": "2-3 sentences on what reviewers criticised or found lacking, or null if the reviews contain no criticism"}}"""

# Sampling rule names stored in DB.
_RULE_CRITIC = "top{n}_score"
_RULE_USER = "top{n}_thumbsup_then_recent"


def _sample_critic(reviews: list[Review], n: int) -> tuple[list[Review], str]:
    picked = sorted(
        (r for r in reviews if r.kind == "critic" and r.quote),
        key=lambda r: r.score or 0,
        reverse=True,
    )[:n]
    return picked, _RULE_CRITIC.format(n=len(picked))


def _sample_user(reviews: list[Review], n: int) -> tuple[list[Review], str]:
    def _key(r: Review):
        return (-(r.thumbs_up or 0), -(len(r.review_date or "")), r.review_date or "")

    picked = sorted(
        (r for r in reviews if r.kind == "user" and r.quote),
        key=_key,
    )[:n]
    return picked, _RULE_USER.format(n=len(picked))


_MIN_SUMMARY_LEN = 20
_REVIEW_MAX_CHARS = 1200   # max chars per review quote sent to the LLM
_PROMPT_MAX_REVIEWS = 25   # hard ceiling regardless of MC_LLM_MAX_REVIEWS


def _parse_llm_response(text: str) -> dict | None:
    """
    Return {"likes": str|None, "dislikes": str|None} or None if invalid.

    Valid:   both fields are strings ≥ _MIN_SUMMARY_LEN chars after strip.
    Valid:   either field is JSON null — the model's sentinel for a side that
             genuinely has nothing (e.g. uniformly negative reviews → likes: null).
    Invalid: empty string or string shorter than _MIN_SUMMARY_LEN — that is
             the truncation/hallucination shape, not the null sentinel.
    Invalid: missing key, non-string/non-null value, unparseable JSON.
    """
    try:
        d = json.loads(text)
    except (json.JSONDecodeError, ValueError):
        return None
    if not isinstance(d, dict) or "likes" not in d or "dislikes" not in d:
        return None
    for val in (d["likes"], d["dislikes"]):
        if val is not None:
            if not isinstance(val, str) or len(val.strip()) < _MIN_SUMMARY_LEN:
                return None
    return {"likes": d["likes"], "dislikes": d["dislikes"]}


def _build_reviews_text(reviews: list[Review]) -> str:
    lines = []
    for i, r in enumerate(reviews, 1):
        pub = f" ({r.publication})" if r.publication else ""
        quote = (r.quote or "")[:_REVIEW_MAX_CHARS]
        lines.append(f"[{i}] Score: {r.score}/100{pub}\n{quote}")
    return "\n\n".join(lines)


LLMCallable = Callable[[list[dict]], "str | None"]


def generate_summaries(
    session: Session,
    game: Game,
    llm: LLMCallable,
    *,
    skip_existing: bool = False,
) -> tuple:
    """
    Generate and persist critic + user summaries for a game.

    Returns (critic_written, user_written, llm_errors).
      critic_written / user_written — True if a summary row was written.
      llm_errors — count of times the LLM was called but failed (returned None
                   or malformed JSON).  Zero if there were no reviews to
                   summarise (that is a skip, not an error).
                   The crawl loop stores this in CrawlRun.llm_errors so
                   failures are visible in /health and the monitor.
      skip_existing — when True, do not re-generate summaries that are already
                      present.  Used by the backfill command to avoid wasting
                      LLM calls on games that were successfully summarised
                      during a previous crawl.
    """
    from sqlalchemy import select as _select

    all_reviews: list[Review] = (
        session.query(Review).filter_by(game_id=game.id).all()
    )

    existing_kinds: set = set()
    if skip_existing:
        existing_kinds = set(
            session.execute(
                _select(Summary.kind).where(Summary.game_id == game.id)
            ).scalars().all()
        )

    _n = min(settings.llm_max_reviews, _PROMPT_MAX_REVIEWS)
    critic_written, c_failed = _summarise_kind(
        session, game, all_reviews,
        kind="critic",
        sampler=lambda r: _sample_critic(r, _n),
        llm=llm,
        already_exists="critic" in existing_kinds,
    )
    user_written, u_failed = _summarise_kind(
        session, game, all_reviews,
        kind="user",
        sampler=lambda r: _sample_user(r, _n),
        llm=llm,
        already_exists="user" in existing_kinds,
    )
    return critic_written, user_written, int(c_failed) + int(u_failed)


def _summarise_kind(
    session: Session,
    game: Game,
    all_reviews: list[Review],
    *,
    kind: str,
    sampler: Callable,
    llm: LLMCallable,
    already_exists: bool = False,
) -> tuple:
    """Returns (written: bool, failed: bool)."""
    if already_exists:
        log.debug("skip %s summary for %s — already exists", kind, game.slug)
        return False, False
    picked, rule = sampler(all_reviews)
    if not picked:
        log.debug("skip %s summary for %s — no %s reviews with quotes", kind, game.slug, kind)
        return False, False

    prompt_text = _PROMPT.format(
        n=len(picked),
        kind=kind,
        title=game.title,
        reviews_text=_build_reviews_text(picked),
    )
    messages = [
        {"role": "system", "content": "You summarise game reviews concisely and accurately."},
        {"role": "user", "content": prompt_text},
    ]

    raw = llm(messages)
    if raw is None:
        log.warning("LLM returned None for %s %s summary — counted as llm_error", game.slug, kind)
        return False, True

    parsed = _parse_llm_response(raw)
    if parsed is None:
        log.warning(
            "unparseable LLM response for %s %s: %r — counted as llm_error",
            game.slug, kind, raw[:200],
        )
        return False, True

    session.execute(
        delete(Summary).where(
            Summary.game_id == game.id,
            Summary.kind == kind,
        )
    )
    session.add(Summary(
        game_id=game.id,
        kind=kind,
        likes=parsed["likes"],
        dislikes=parsed["dislikes"],
        model=settings.llm_model,
        source_review_count=len(picked),
        sampling_rule=rule,
        generated_at=datetime.utcnow(),
    ))
    return True, False

"""
Parsing a Metacritic listing page into game records.

Two listing shapes matter, and they carry the same item objects:

    /game/                                   the New Releases block
    /browse/game/all/all/all-time/new/       the paginated full list

Everything below is defensive about missing fields. Unreleased games — which
is most of what "new releases" means — have a null metascore, no reviews and
sometimes no description, and a scraper that assumes otherwise dies on its
first run at 03:00.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

from dataclasses import dataclass, field

from ..payload import find_items, parse

IMAGE_BASE = "https://www.metacritic.com/a/img/resize/"


@dataclass
class PlatformScore:
    """One platform's scores. A game can ship on several, each scored apart."""

    name: str
    metascore: int | None = None
    critic_reviews: int = 0
    userscore: float | None = None
    user_reviews: int = 0


@dataclass
class GameSummary:
    """What a listing page tells us about a game, before we open its page."""

    external_id: int
    slug: str
    title: str
    url: str
    description: str | None = None
    release_date: str | None = None
    premiere_year: int | None = None
    rating: str | None = None
    image_url: str | None = None
    genres: list[str] = field(default_factory=list)
    platforms: list[PlatformScore] = field(default_factory=list)
    metascore: int | None = None
    critic_review_count: int = 0
    critic_sentiment: str | None = None

    @property
    def is_released(self) -> bool:
        return self.metascore is not None or self.critic_review_count > 0


def _image_url(image: dict | None) -> str | None:
    """
    Build a cover URL from the image object.

    The payload gives a bucket path rather than a URL; Metacritic's own pages
    compose the CDN address from it. `imageUrl` is sometimes populated and is
    preferred when it is.
    """
    if not isinstance(image, dict):
        return None
    direct = image.get("imageUrl")
    if isinstance(direct, str) and direct.startswith("http"):
        return direct
    bucket_path = image.get("bucketPath")
    if not isinstance(bucket_path, str) or not bucket_path:
        return None
    width = image.get("width") or 460
    height = image.get("height") or 215
    return f"{IMAGE_BASE}{width}/{height}/catalog{bucket_path}"


def _platforms(item: dict) -> list[PlatformScore]:
    scores: list[PlatformScore] = []
    for entry in item.get("platforms") or []:
        if not isinstance(entry, dict):
            continue
        name = entry.get("name") or entry.get("platform") or entry.get("slug")
        if not name:
            continue
        critic = entry.get("criticScoreSummary") or {}
        user = entry.get("userScoreSummary") or {}
        scores.append(
            PlatformScore(
                name=str(name),
                metascore=critic.get("score") if isinstance(critic, dict) else None,
                critic_reviews=(critic.get("reviewCount") or 0) if isinstance(critic, dict) else 0,
                userscore=user.get("score") if isinstance(user, dict) else None,
                user_reviews=(user.get("reviewCount") or 0) if isinstance(user, dict) else 0,
            )
        )
    return scores


def _genres(item: dict) -> list[str]:
    names = []
    for entry in item.get("genres") or []:
        if isinstance(entry, dict) and entry.get("name"):
            names.append(str(entry["name"]))
        elif isinstance(entry, str):
            names.append(entry)
    return names


def to_summary(item: dict) -> GameSummary | None:
    """One payload item to a GameSummary. Returns None for non-game entries."""
    slug = item.get("slug")
    title = item.get("title")
    external_id = item.get("id")
    if not slug or not title or external_id is None:
        return None
    if item.get("type") and item["type"] != "game-title":
        return None

    critic = item.get("criticScoreSummary")
    critic = critic if isinstance(critic, dict) else {}

    return GameSummary(
        external_id=int(external_id),
        slug=str(slug),
        title=str(title),
        url=f"https://www.metacritic.com/game/{slug}/",
        description=item.get("description") or None,
        release_date=item.get("releaseDate") or None,
        premiere_year=item.get("premiereYear") or None,
        rating=item.get("rating") or None,
        image_url=_image_url(item.get("image")),
        genres=_genres(item),
        platforms=_platforms(item),
        metascore=critic.get("score"),
        critic_review_count=critic.get("reviewCount") or 0,
        critic_sentiment=critic.get("sentiment") or None,
    )


def parse_listing(html: str) -> list[GameSummary]:
    """A listing page to the games it advertises, in page order."""
    items = find_items(parse(html))
    summaries = [to_summary(item) for item in items if isinstance(item, dict)]
    return [summary for summary in summaries if summary is not None]

"""
Parsing a Metacritic game detail page (game.html fixture).

All component lookups go by meta.componentName, never by index.
The BRIEF verified this is stable across fetches; the index order is not.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

from dataclasses import dataclass, field

from ..payload import parse


@dataclass
class PlatformDetail:
    name: str
    metascore: int | None = None
    critic_reviews: int = 0
    userscore: float | None = None
    user_reviews: int = 0


@dataclass
class ReviewItem:
    kind: str                          # 'critic' | 'user'
    author: str | None
    publication: str | None
    score: int | None
    quote: str | None
    review_date: str | None
    platform: str | None = None
    thumbs_up: int | None = None
    thumbs_down: int | None = None


@dataclass
class GameDetail:
    slug: str
    title: str | None = None
    description: str | None = None
    release_date: str | None = None
    rating: str | None = None
    developer: str | None = None
    publisher: str | None = None
    cover_url: str | None = None
    video_url: str | None = None
    metascore: int | None = None
    userscore: float | None = None
    critic_review_count: int = 0
    user_review_count: int = 0
    platforms: list[PlatformDetail] = field(default_factory=list)
    genres: list[str] = field(default_factory=list)
    critic_reviews: list[ReviewItem] = field(default_factory=list)
    user_reviews: list[ReviewItem] = field(default_factory=list)


def _by_name(components: list, name: str) -> dict | None:
    for c in components:
        if isinstance(c, dict) and (c.get("meta") or {}).get("componentName") == name:
            return c
    return None


def _platforms(item: dict) -> list[PlatformDetail]:
    out = []
    for p in (item.get("platforms") or []):
        if not isinstance(p, dict):
            continue
        name = p.get("name") or p.get("slug")
        if not name:
            continue
        cs = p.get("criticScoreSummary") or {}
        us = p.get("userScoreSummary") or {}
        out.append(PlatformDetail(
            name=str(name),
            metascore=cs.get("score") if isinstance(cs, dict) else None,
            critic_reviews=(cs.get("reviewCount") or 0) if isinstance(cs, dict) else 0,
            userscore=us.get("score") if isinstance(us, dict) else None,
            user_reviews=(us.get("reviewCount") or 0) if isinstance(us, dict) else 0,
        ))
    return out


def _genres(item: dict) -> list[str]:
    return [
        g["name"] for g in (item.get("genres") or [])
        if isinstance(g, dict) and g.get("name")
    ]


def _companies(item: dict) -> tuple[str | None, str | None]:
    """Return (developer_name, publisher_name) from production.companies."""
    developer = publisher = None
    for company in ((item.get("production") or {}).get("companies") or []):
        if not isinstance(company, dict):
            continue
        kind = company.get("typeName")
        name = company.get("name")
        if kind == "Developer" and developer is None:
            developer = name
        elif kind == "Publisher" and publisher is None:
            publisher = name
    return developer, publisher


def _video_url(item: dict) -> str | None:
    video = item.get("video")
    if not isinstance(video, dict):
        return None
    # embedUrl is an iframe-embeddable JW Player URL; url is null in the fixture.
    return video.get("embedUrl") or video.get("manifestUrl") or None


def _cover_url(item: dict) -> str | None:
    images = item.get("images") or []
    for img in images:
        if not isinstance(img, dict):
            continue
        url = img.get("imageUrl")
        if isinstance(url, str) and url.startswith("http"):
            return url
        bucket = img.get("bucketPath")
        if isinstance(bucket, str) and bucket:
            w = img.get("width") or 460
            h = img.get("height") or 215
            return f"https://www.metacritic.com/a/img/resize/{w}/{h}/catalog{bucket}"
    return None


def _critic_reviews(comp: dict) -> tuple[list[ReviewItem], int]:
    data = comp.get("data") or {}
    items = data.get("items") or []
    total = data.get("totalResults") or 0
    reviews = []
    for r in items:
        if not isinstance(r, dict):
            continue
        reviews.append(ReviewItem(
            kind="critic",
            author=r.get("author") or None,
            publication=r.get("publicationName") or None,
            score=r.get("score"),
            quote=r.get("quote") or None,
            review_date=r.get("date") or None,
            platform=r.get("platform") or None,
        ))
    return reviews, total


def _user_reviews(comp: dict) -> tuple[list[ReviewItem], int]:
    data = comp.get("data") or {}
    items = data.get("items") or []
    total = data.get("totalResults") or 0
    reviews = []
    for r in items:
        if not isinstance(r, dict):
            continue
        reviews.append(ReviewItem(
            kind="user",
            author=r.get("author") or None,
            publication=None,
            score=r.get("score"),
            quote=r.get("quote") or None,
            review_date=r.get("date") or None,
            platform=r.get("platform") or None,
            thumbs_up=r.get("thumbsUp"),
            thumbs_down=r.get("thumbsDown"),
        ))
    return reviews, total


def parse_detail(html: str, slug: str) -> GameDetail:
    """
    Parse a game detail page into a GameDetail.

    `slug` is used to locate the correct loadPage key; it must match the
    game's Metacritic slug exactly.
    """
    root = parse(html)
    page_key = f"loadPage:games:{slug}:"
    page = (root.get("data") or {}).get(page_key)
    if page is None:
        # Fallback: find any loadPage:games:…: key
        for k, v in (root.get("data") or {}).items():
            if k.startswith("loadPage:games:") and isinstance(v, dict):
                page = v
                break

    if page is None:
        # Handle review sub-pages (critic-reviews, user-reviews) whose keys
        # are loadPage:games-critic-reviews:… and loadPage:games-user-reviews:…
        for k, v in (root.get("data") or {}).items():
            if k.startswith("loadPage:games") and isinstance(v, dict):
                page = v
                break

    if page is None or not isinstance(page.get("components"), list):
        return GameDetail(slug=slug)

    comps = page["components"]
    detail = GameDetail(slug=slug)

    # --- product component ---
    prod_comp = _by_name(comps, "product")
    if prod_comp:
        item = (prod_comp.get("data") or {}).get("item") or {}
        detail.title = item.get("title")
        detail.description = item.get("description") or None
        detail.release_date = item.get("releaseDate") or None
        detail.rating = item.get("rating") or None
        detail.developer, detail.publisher = _companies(item)
        detail.video_url = _video_url(item)
        detail.cover_url = _cover_url(item)
        detail.platforms = _platforms(item)
        detail.genres = _genres(item)

    # --- critic-score-summary ---
    cs_comp = _by_name(comps, "critic-score-summary")
    if cs_comp:
        cs = (cs_comp.get("data") or {}).get("item") or {}
        detail.metascore = cs.get("score")
        detail.critic_review_count = cs.get("reviewCount") or 0

    # --- user-score-summary ---
    us_comp = _by_name(comps, "user-score-summary")
    if us_comp:
        us = (us_comp.get("data") or {}).get("item") or {}
        detail.userscore = us.get("score")
        detail.user_review_count = us.get("reviewCount") or 0

    # --- critic-reviews ---
    cr_comp = _by_name(comps, "critic-reviews")
    if cr_comp:
        detail.critic_reviews, _ = _critic_reviews(cr_comp)

    # --- user-reviews ---
    ur_comp = _by_name(comps, "user-reviews")
    if ur_comp:
        detail.user_reviews, _ = _user_reviews(ur_comp)

    return detail

"""Tests for scrape/listing.py — parsing both HTML pages and API JSON items."""
from __future__ import annotations

import json

import pytest

from metacrawl.scrape.listing import GameSummary, PlatformScore, _image_url, parse_listing, to_summary


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# parse_listing() on browse.html
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

def test_browse_html_yields_24_games(browse_html):
    games = parse_listing(browse_html)
    assert len(games) == 24


def test_browse_game_has_required_fields(browse_html):
    games = parse_listing(browse_html)
    first = games[0]
    assert isinstance(first.external_id, int) and first.external_id > 0
    assert isinstance(first.slug, str) and first.slug
    assert isinstance(first.title, str) and first.title
    assert first.url.startswith("https://www.metacritic.com/game/")


def test_browse_all_games_are_game_summaries(browse_html):
    games = parse_listing(browse_html)
    assert all(isinstance(g, GameSummary) for g in games)


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# to_summary() on API JSON items
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

def test_api_new_releases_yields_20_summaries(api_new_releases):
    items = api_new_releases["data"]["items"]
    summaries = [to_summary(item) for item in items if isinstance(item, dict)]
    summaries = [s for s in summaries if s is not None]
    assert len(summaries) == 20


def test_api_page2_yields_24_summaries(api_page2):
    items = api_page2["data"]["items"]
    summaries = [to_summary(item) for item in items if isinstance(item, dict)]
    summaries = [s for s in summaries if s is not None]
    assert len(summaries) == 24


def test_api_item_fields_correct(api_new_releases):
    item = api_new_releases["data"]["items"][0]
    s = to_summary(item)
    assert s is not None
    assert s.external_id == item["id"]
    assert s.slug == item["slug"]
    assert s.title == item["title"]


def test_api_item_metascore_parsed(api_new_releases):
    # First item in the new-releases fixture has score=68 (over-the-hill)
    item = api_new_releases["data"]["items"][0]
    s = to_summary(item)
    assert s.metascore == item["criticScoreSummary"]["score"]


def test_api_item_platform_names(api_new_releases):
    item = api_new_releases["data"]["items"][0]
    s = to_summary(item)
    assert len(s.platforms) == len(item["platforms"])
    expected = {p["name"] for p in item["platforms"]}
    actual = {p.name for p in s.platforms}
    assert actual == expected


def test_api_item_with_null_description(api_new_releases):
    # Unreleased / minimal entries have null description — must not crash.
    null_desc = next(
        (item for item in api_new_releases["data"]["items"] if item.get("description") is None),
        None,
    )
    if null_desc is None:
        pytest.skip("fixture has no item with null description")
    s = to_summary(null_desc)
    assert s is not None
    assert s.description is None


def test_api_item_genre_names(api_new_releases):
    item = api_new_releases["data"]["items"][0]
    s = to_summary(item)
    expected = [g["name"] for g in item["genres"] if isinstance(g, dict) and g.get("name")]
    assert s.genres == expected


def test_to_summary_returns_none_for_non_game():
    bad = {"id": 1, "slug": "x", "title": "X", "type": "movie-title"}
    assert to_summary(bad) is None


def test_to_summary_returns_none_for_missing_slug():
    assert to_summary({"id": 1, "title": "X"}) is None


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# _image_url() helper
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

def test_image_url_prefers_direct_url():
    img = {"imageUrl": "https://cdn.example.com/cover.jpg", "bucketPath": "/foo/bar.jpg",
           "width": 460, "height": 215}
    assert _image_url(img) == "https://cdn.example.com/cover.jpg"


def test_image_url_falls_back_to_bucket_path():
    img = {"imageUrl": None, "bucketPath": "/provider/7/2/123.jpg", "width": 373, "height": 560}
    url = _image_url(img)
    assert url == "https://www.metacritic.com/a/img/resize/373/560/catalog/provider/7/2/123.jpg"


def test_image_url_none_for_null_image():
    assert _image_url(None) is None
    assert _image_url({}) is None

"""
Tests for POST /api/crawl/run auth — crawl secret enforcement.

All offline; no DB or scheduler involved.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

from unittest.mock import MagicMock

import pytest
from fastapi import FastAPI
from fastapi.testclient import TestClient

from metacrawl.web.routes import router


@pytest.fixture
def crawl_client():
    """Minimal FastAPI app with just the crawl router and a mock worker."""
    app = FastAPI()
    app.include_router(router)
    worker = MagicMock()
    worker.submit.return_value = True
    worker.is_running = False
    app.state.worker = worker
    app.state.session_factory = MagicMock()
    return TestClient(app)


def test_crawl_run_refuses_when_secret_not_configured(monkeypatch, crawl_client):
    """MC_CRAWL_SECRET unset → 403, never runs open."""
    monkeypatch.setattr("metacrawl.web.routes.settings.crawl_secret", "")
    resp = crawl_client.post("/api/crawl/run")
    assert resp.status_code == 403


def test_crawl_run_refuses_with_wrong_secret(monkeypatch, crawl_client):
    """Correct secret configured, wrong header → 403."""
    monkeypatch.setattr("metacrawl.web.routes.settings.crawl_secret", "correct-secret")
    resp = crawl_client.post(
        "/api/crawl/run", headers={"X-Crawl-Secret": "wrong-secret"}
    )
    assert resp.status_code == 403


def test_crawl_run_refuses_when_secret_header_missing(monkeypatch, crawl_client):
    """Correct secret configured, no header → 403."""
    monkeypatch.setattr("metacrawl.web.routes.settings.crawl_secret", "correct-secret")
    resp = crawl_client.post("/api/crawl/run")
    assert resp.status_code == 403


def test_crawl_run_accepts_correct_secret(monkeypatch, crawl_client):
    """Correct secret configured and provided → 200."""
    monkeypatch.setattr("metacrawl.web.routes.settings.crawl_secret", "correct-secret")
    resp = crawl_client.post(
        "/api/crawl/run", headers={"X-Crawl-Secret": "correct-secret"}
    )
    assert resp.status_code == 200

1	"""
2	Reading Metacritic's page payload.
3	
4	Metacritic is a server-rendered Nuxt 3 application. Every page embeds the data
5	its components rendered from in a `<script id="__NUXT_DATA__">` blob, so the
6	scraper reads structured objects — ids, scores, platforms, release dates —
7	instead of matching CSS classes.
8	
9	That choice is the difference between a scraper that survives a redeploy and
10	one that silently returns empty lists the next morning. Class names like
11	`c-finderProductCard_title` change without notice; the payload is the data the
12	page itself runs on.
13	
14	The blob is devalue-encoded, the format Nuxt uses for hydration: a flat array
15	where every value is either a literal or an integer index pointing at another
16	slot in the same array, which is how it deduplicates repeated strings and
17	handles cycles. Negative indices encode the JavaScript values JSON cannot —
18	undefined, holes, NaN, the infinities and negative zero.
19	
20	`parse` turns that back into ordinary Python.
21	"""
22	
23	from __future__ import annotations
24	
25	import json
26	import re
27	from typing import Any
28	
29	PAYLOAD = re.compile(
30	    r'<script[^>]*id="__NUXT_DATA__"[^>]*>(?P<body>.*?)</script>', re.S
31	)
32	
33	# devalue's negative sentinels.
34	SENTINELS: dict[int, Any] = {
35	    -1: None,        # undefined
36	    -2: None,        # array hole
37	    -3: float("nan"),
38	    -4: float("inf"),
39	    -5: float("-inf"),
40	    -6: -0.0,
41	}
42	
43	# Wrappers Nuxt adds around reactive state. The value we want is inside.
44	UNWRAP = {"Reactive", "ShallowReactive", "Ref", "ShallowRef", "EmptyRef", "Object"}
45	
46	MAX_DEPTH = 80
47	
48	
49	class PayloadError(RuntimeError):
50	    """The page carried no payload, or one we could not read."""
51	
52	
53	def extract(html: str) -> list:
54	    """Pull the raw devalue array out of a page."""
55	    match = PAYLOAD.search(html)
56	    if match is None:
57	        raise PayloadError(
58	            "no __NUXT_DATA__ block in this page — Metacritic may have changed "
59	            "its rendering, or this is an error or consent page rather than content"
60	        )
61	    try:
62	        data = json.loads(match.group("body"))
63	    except json.JSONDecodeError as exc:
64	        raise PayloadError(f"__NUXT_DATA__ is not valid JSON: {exc}") from exc
65	    if not isinstance(data, list):
66	        raise PayloadError(f"expected a devalue array, got {type(data).__name__}")
67	    return data
68	
69	
70	def resolve(data: list, index: Any, depth: int = 0) -> Any:
71	    """Resolve one slot of a devalue array into a plain Python value."""
72	    if depth > MAX_DEPTH:
73	        # Nuxt payloads contain cycles (a page references its own route).
74	        # Depth-limiting is enough: nothing we read lives this deep.
75	        return None
76	
77	    if isinstance(index, bool):
78	        return index
79	    if isinstance(index, int):
80	        if index in SENTINELS:
81	            return SENTINELS[index]
82	        if not 0 <= index < len(data):
83	            return None
84	        value = data[index]
85	    else:
86	        value = index
87	
88	    if isinstance(value, list):
89	        if value and isinstance(value[0], str):
90	            tag = value[0]
91	            if tag in UNWRAP:
92	                return resolve(data, value[1], depth + 1)
93	            if tag == "Date":
94	                return resolve(data, value[1], depth + 1)
95	            if tag == "Set":
96	                return [resolve(data, item, depth + 1) for item in value[1:]]
97	            if tag == "Map":
98	                flat = [resolve(data, item, depth + 1) for item in value[1:]]
99	                return dict(zip(flat[::2], flat[1::2]))
100	            if tag == "BigInt":
101	                raw = resolve(data, value[1], depth + 1)
102	                return int(raw) if raw is not None else None
103	        return [resolve(data, item, depth + 1) for item in value]
104	
105	    if isinstance(value, dict):
106	        return {key: resolve(data, slot, depth + 1) for key, slot in value.items()}
107	
108	    return value
109	
110	
111	def parse(html: str) -> dict:
112	    """Page HTML to the resolved payload root."""
113	    root = resolve(extract(html), 0)
114	    if not isinstance(root, dict):
115	        raise PayloadError(f"payload root is {type(root).__name__}, expected an object")
116	    return root
117	
118	
119	def find_items(root: dict, marker: str = "items") -> list[dict]:
120	    """
121	    Locate the list of content items in a resolved payload.
122	
123	    The key that holds them encodes the request path — for example
124	    `browse-game-/browse/game/all/all/all-time/new/` — so it cannot be
125	    hard-coded across pages. Searching `data` for the first list of objects
126	    carrying both an id and a title survives Metacritic renaming its routes,
127	    which hard-coding would not.
128	    """
129	    data = root.get("data")
130	    if not isinstance(data, dict):
131	        return []
132	
133	    def looks_like_content(value: Any) -> bool:
134	        return (
135	            isinstance(value, list)
136	            and value
137	            and isinstance(value[0], dict)
138	            and "title" in value[0]
139	            and "id" in value[0]
140	        )
141	
142	    for section in data.values():
143	        if isinstance(section, dict):
144	            candidate = section.get(marker)
145	            if looks_like_content(candidate):
146	                return candidate
147	    # Fall back to a shallow sweep for payload shapes that nest one deeper.
148	    for section in data.values():
149	        if isinstance(section, dict):
150	            for value in section.values():
151	                if looks_like_content(value):
152	                    return value
153	    return []
154

1	"""
2	Backfill command — walk games already in the database and complete them:
3	detail page, reviews, embeddings, and LLM summaries.
4	
5	WHY THIS EXISTS
6	───────────────
7	The regular hourly crawl processes only games seen on the browse/new-releases
8	listing.  Games that appeared during periods when the LLM or embedder was
9	offline may have reviews but no summaries, or may be missing developer info
10	that only appears on the detail page.  This command fills those gaps
11	without touching the crawl machinery.
12	
13	RESUMABLE
14	─────────
15	Each game is committed in its own transaction.  If the command is interrupted
16	(Ctrl-C, timeout, crash) the next run picks up from the next unprocessed
17	game — already-complete games are detected cheaply from DB state and skipped.
18	
19	PRIORITY ORDER
20	──────────────
21	  1. Games with a metascore AND a description (released, has reviewable text)
22	  2. Everything else (unreleased, null score, no description yet)
23	  Within each tier: highest metascore first, then most-recent release.
24	
25	COMMAND LINE
26	────────────
27	  PYTHONPATH=src python -m metacrawl.backfill [--limit N] [--only-missing-summaries]
28	"""
29	from __future__ import annotations
30	
31	import logging
32	import sys
33	from dataclasses import dataclass
34	from typing import Optional
35	
36	from sqlalchemy import and_, case, select
37	
38	from .api.detail import fetch_critic_reviews, fetch_detail, fetch_user_reviews
39	from .db.models import Game, Review, Summary
40	from .db.upsert import apply_detail
41	from .embed import call_embedder, embed_game
42	from .http import HttpClient
43	from .llm import call_llm
44	from .summarise import generate_summaries
45	
46	log = logging.getLogger(__name__)
47	
48	
49	@dataclass
50	class GameResult:
51	    slug: str
52	    critic_reviews: int = 0
53	    user_reviews: int = 0
54	    critic_written: bool = False
55	    user_written: bool = False
56	    llm_errors: int = 0
57	    skipped_no_reviews: bool = False   # unreleased: metascore IS NULL, expected
58	    scored_no_reviews: bool = False    # has metascore but MC returned 0 reviews
59	    already_complete: bool = False
60	    error: Optional[str] = None
61	
62	    @property
63	    def ok(self) -> bool:
64	        return self.error is None
65	
66	
67	def _priority_query(session, only_missing_summaries: bool):
68	    """
69	    Return a query for Game rows in processing priority order.
70	
71	    Priority 0 (first): has both metascore and description.
72	    Priority 1 (later): anything else.
73	    Within each priority tier: metascore DESC NULLS LAST, then by id.
74	
75	    Both modes pre-filter to games that actually need work, so the limit
76	    is consumed only by games with genuine gaps (no wasted API calls on
77	    already-complete entries).
78	    """
79	    priority = case(
80	        (and_(Game.metascore.isnot(None), Game.description.isnot(None)), 0),
81	        else_=1,
82	    )
83	    query = (
84	        session.query(Game)
85	        .order_by(priority, Game.metascore.desc().nullslast(), Game.id)
86	    )
87	
88	    has_critic_rev = session.query(Review.game_id).filter(Review.kind == "critic")
89	    has_user_rev   = session.query(Review.game_id).filter(Review.kind == "user")
90	    has_critic_sum = session.query(Summary.game_id).filter(Summary.kind == "critic")
91	    has_user_sum   = session.query(Summary.game_id).filter(Summary.kind == "user")
92	
93	    if only_missing_summaries:
94	        # Games with reviews of a kind but no summary for that kind.
95	        needs_critic = and_(Game.id.in_(has_critic_rev), ~Game.id.in_(has_critic_sum))
96	        needs_user   = and_(Game.id.in_(has_user_rev),   ~Game.id.in_(has_user_sum))
97	        query = query.filter(needs_critic | needs_user)
98	    else:
99	        # Full backfill: only games that have actual gaps.
100	        # A game is complete when it has a description AND summaries exist for
101	        # every review kind that has reviews.  Exclude those; include everything else.
102	        needs_work = (
103	            Game.description.is_(None)                                       # detail not fetched
104	            | (Game.id.in_(has_critic_rev) & ~Game.id.in_(has_critic_sum))   # critic summary missing
105	            | (Game.id.in_(has_user_rev)   & ~Game.id.in_(has_user_sum))     # user summary missing
106	        )
107	        query = query.filter(needs_work)
108	
109	    return query
110	
111	
112	def _process_game(
113	    session,
114	    game: Game,
115	    client: HttpClient,
116	    only_missing_summaries: bool,
117	) -> GameResult:
118	    """Process one game: detail + reviews + summaries.  Idempotent."""
119	    slug = game.slug
120	
121	    if not only_missing_summaries:
122	        try:
123	            detail = fetch_detail(client, slug)
124	            critic_revs = fetch_critic_reviews(client, slug, limit=50)
125	            user_revs = fetch_user_reviews(client, slug, limit=50)
126	            if critic_revs:
127	                detail.critic_reviews = critic_revs
128	            if user_revs:
129	                detail.user_reviews = user_revs
130	            apply_detail(session, game, detail)
131	            session.flush()
132	
133	            outcome = embed_game(session, game, call_embedder)
134	            if outcome.stored:
135	                session.flush()
136	        except Exception as exc:
137	            log.exception("detail/review fetch failed for %s", slug)
138	            return GameResult(slug=slug, error=str(exc)[:120])
139	
140	    critic_n: int = session.query(Review).filter_by(game_id=game.id, kind="critic").count()
141	    user_n: int = session.query(Review).filter_by(game_id=game.id, kind="user").count()
142	
143	    if critic_n == 0 and user_n == 0:
144	        if game.metascore is not None:
145	            return GameResult(slug=slug, scored_no_reviews=True)
146	        return GameResult(slug=slug, skipped_no_reviews=True)
147	
148	    existing_kinds = set(
149	        session.execute(
150	            select(Summary.kind).where(Summary.game_id == game.id)
151	        ).scalars().all()
152	    )
153	    need_critic = critic_n > 0 and "critic" not in existing_kinds
154	    need_user = user_n > 0 and "user" not in existing_kinds
155	
156	    if not need_critic and not need_user:
157	        return GameResult(
158	            slug=slug,
159	            critic_reviews=critic_n,
160	            user_reviews=user_n,
161	            already_complete=True,
162	        )
163	
164	    c_written, u_written, llm_errs = generate_summaries(
165	        session, game, call_llm, skip_existing=True
166	    )
167	    return GameResult(
168	        slug=slug,
169	        critic_reviews=critic_n,
170	        user_reviews=user_n,
171	        critic_written=bool(c_written),
172	        user_written=bool(u_written),
173	        llm_errors=llm_errs,
174	    )
175	
176	
177	def _print_result(idx: int, total: int, r: GameResult) -> None:
178	    prefix = f"[{idx:4d}/{total}] {r.slug:<45}"
179	    if r.error:
180	        print(f"{prefix} ERROR: {r.error}", flush=True)
181	    elif r.scored_no_reviews:
182	        print(f"{prefix} scored but no reviews (metascore present, MC returned 0)", flush=True)
183	    elif r.skipped_no_reviews:
184	        print(f"{prefix} skipped (unreleased, no reviews)", flush=True)
185	    elif r.already_complete:
186	        print(f"{prefix} {r.critic_reviews}c+{r.user_reviews}u  already complete", flush=True)
187	    else:
188	        c = "critic✓" if r.critic_written else ("critic–" if r.critic_reviews == 0 else "critic✓had")
189	        u = "user✓" if r.user_written else ("user–" if r.user_reviews == 0 else "user✓had")
190	        llm = f"  [{r.llm_errors} llm_err]" if r.llm_errors else ""
191	        print(f"{prefix} {r.critic_reviews}c+{r.user_reviews}u  {c} {u}{llm}", flush=True)
192	
193	
194	def run_backfill(
195	    session_factory,
196	    *,
197	    limit: Optional[int] = None,
198	    only_missing_summaries: bool = False,
199	) -> list:
200	    """
201	    Walk games in priority order and fill gaps.  Commits after each game.
202	    Returns the list of GameResult objects (one per processed game).
203	    """
204	    with session_factory() as session:
205	        query = _priority_query(session, only_missing_summaries)
206	        if limit is not None:
207	            query = query.limit(limit)
208	        # Load IDs only — game objects will be reloaded in fresh sessions below.
209	        game_ids = [g.id for g in query.all()]
210	
211	    total = len(game_ids)
212	    if total == 0:
213	        print("Nothing to backfill.", flush=True)
214	        return []
215	
216	    mode = "--only-missing-summaries" if only_missing_summaries else "full"
217	    lim_str = f" (limit {limit})" if limit is not None else ""
218	    print(f"Backfilling {total} games [{mode}]{lim_str}", flush=True)
219	
220	    results: list = []
221	    with HttpClient() as client:
222	        for idx, game_id in enumerate(game_ids, 1):
223	            with session_factory() as session:
224	                game = session.get(Game, game_id)
225	                if game is None:
226	                    continue
227	                result = _process_game(session, game, client, only_missing_summaries)
228	                session.commit()
229	
230	            results.append(result)
231	            _print_result(idx, total, result)
232	
233	    new_summaries = sum(r.critic_written + r.user_written for r in results)
234	    complete = sum(r.already_complete for r in results)
235	    skipped = sum(r.skipped_no_reviews for r in results)

"""
Backfill command — walk games already in the database and complete them:
detail page, reviews, embeddings, and LLM summaries.

WHY THIS EXISTS
───────────────
The regular hourly crawl processes only games seen on the browse/new-releases
listing.  Games that appeared during periods when the LLM or embedder was
offline may have reviews but no summaries, or may be missing developer info
that only appears on the detail page.  This command fills those gaps
without touching the crawl machinery.

RESUMABLE
─────────
Each game is committed in its own transaction.  If the command is interrupted
(Ctrl-C, timeout, crash) the next run picks up from the next unprocessed
game — already-complete games are detected cheaply from DB state and skipped.

PRIORITY ORDER
──────────────
  1. Games with a metascore AND a description (released, has reviewable text)
  2. Everything else (unreleased, null score, no description yet)
  Within each tier: highest metascore first, then most-recent release.

COMMAND LINE
────────────
  PYTHONPATH=src python -m metacrawl.backfill [--limit N] [--only-missing-summaries]
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import logging
import sys
from dataclasses import dataclass
from typing import Optional

from sqlalchemy import and_, case, select

from .api.detail import fetch_critic_reviews, fetch_detail, fetch_user_reviews
from .db.models import Game, Review, Summary
from .db.upsert import apply_detail
from .embed import call_embedder, embed_game
from .http import HttpClient
from .llm import call_llm
from .summarise import generate_summaries

log = logging.getLogger(__name__)


@dataclass
class GameResult:
    slug: str
    critic_reviews: int = 0
    user_reviews: int = 0
    critic_written: bool = False
    user_written: bool = False
    llm_errors: int = 0
    skipped_no_reviews: bool = False   # unreleased: metascore IS NULL, expected
    scored_no_reviews: bool = False    # has metascore but MC returned 0 reviews
    already_complete: bool = False
    error: Optional[str] = None

    @property
    def ok(self) -> bool:
        return self.error is None


def _priority_query(session, only_missing_summaries: bool):
    """
    Return a query for Game rows in processing priority order.

    Priority 0 (first): has both metascore and description.
    Priority 1 (later): anything else.
    Within each priority tier: metascore DESC NULLS LAST, then by id.

    Both modes pre-filter to games that actually need work, so the limit
    is consumed only by games with genuine gaps (no wasted API calls on
    already-complete entries).
    """
    priority = case(
        (and_(Game.metascore.isnot(None), Game.description.isnot(None)), 0),
        else_=1,
    )
    query = (
        session.query(Game)
        .order_by(priority, Game.metascore.desc().nullslast(), Game.id)
    )

    has_critic_rev = session.query(Review.game_id).filter(Review.kind == "critic")
    has_user_rev   = session.query(Review.game_id).filter(Review.kind == "user")
    has_critic_sum = session.query(Summary.game_id).filter(Summary.kind == "critic")
    has_user_sum   = session.query(Summary.game_id).filter(Summary.kind == "user")

    if only_missing_summaries:
        # Games with reviews of a kind but no summary for that kind.
        needs_critic = and_(Game.id.in_(has_critic_rev), ~Game.id.in_(has_critic_sum))
        needs_user   = and_(Game.id.in_(has_user_rev),   ~Game.id.in_(has_user_sum))
        query = query.filter(needs_critic | needs_user)
    else:
        # Full backfill: only games that have actual gaps.
        # A game is complete when it has a description AND summaries exist for
        # every review kind that has reviews.  Exclude those; include everything else.
        needs_work = (
            Game.description.is_(None)                                       # detail not fetched
            | (Game.id.in_(has_critic_rev) & ~Game.id.in_(has_critic_sum))   # critic summary missing
            | (Game.id.in_(has_user_rev)   & ~Game.id.in_(has_user_sum))     # user summary missing
        )
        query = query.filter(needs_work)

    return query


def _process_game(
    session,
    game: Game,
    client: HttpClient,
    only_missing_summaries: bool,
) -> GameResult:
    """Process one game: detail + reviews + summaries.  Idempotent."""
    slug = game.slug

    if not only_missing_summaries:
        try:
            detail = fetch_detail(client, slug)
            critic_revs = fetch_critic_reviews(client, slug, limit=50)
            user_revs = fetch_user_reviews(client, slug, limit=50)
            if critic_revs:
                detail.critic_reviews = critic_revs
            if user_revs:
                detail.user_reviews = user_revs
            apply_detail(session, game, detail)
            session.flush()

            outcome = embed_game(session, game, call_embedder)
            if outcome.stored:
                session.flush()
        except Exception as exc:
            log.exception("detail/review fetch failed for %s", slug)
            return GameResult(slug=slug, error=str(exc)[:120])

    critic_n: int = session.query(Review).filter_by(game_id=game.id, kind="critic").count()
    user_n: int = session.query(Review).filter_by(game_id=game.id, kind="user").count()

    if critic_n == 0 and user_n == 0:
        if game.metascore is not None:
            return GameResult(slug=slug, scored_no_reviews=True)
        return GameResult(slug=slug, skipped_no_reviews=True)

    existing_kinds = set(
        session.execute(
            select(Summary.kind).where(Summary.game_id == game.id)
        ).scalars().all()
    )
    need_critic = critic_n > 0 and "critic" not in existing_kinds
    need_user = user_n > 0 and "user" not in existing_kinds

    if not need_critic and not need_user:
        return GameResult(
            slug=slug,
            critic_reviews=critic_n,
            user_reviews=user_n,
            already_complete=True,
        )

    c_written, u_written, llm_errs = generate_summaries(
        session, game, call_llm, skip_existing=True
    )
    return GameResult(
        slug=slug,
        critic_reviews=critic_n,
        user_reviews=user_n,
        critic_written=bool(c_written),
        user_written=bool(u_written),
        llm_errors=llm_errs,
    )


def _print_result(idx: int, total: int, r: GameResult) -> None:
    prefix = f"[{idx:4d}/{total}] {r.slug:<45}"
    if r.error:
        print(f"{prefix} ERROR: {r.error}", flush=True)
    elif r.scored_no_reviews:
        print(f"{prefix} scored but no reviews (metascore present, MC returned 0)", flush=True)
    elif r.skipped_no_reviews:
        print(f"{prefix} skipped (unreleased, no reviews)", flush=True)
    elif r.already_complete:
        print(f"{prefix} {r.critic_reviews}c+{r.user_reviews}u  already complete", flush=True)
    else:
        c = "critic✓" if r.critic_written else ("critic–" if r.critic_reviews == 0 else "critic✓had")
        u = "user✓" if r.user_written else ("user–" if r.user_reviews == 0 else "user✓had")
        llm = f"  [{r.llm_errors} llm_err]" if r.llm_errors else ""
        print(f"{prefix} {r.critic_reviews}c+{r.user_reviews}u  {c} {u}{llm}", flush=True)


def run_backfill(
    session_factory,
    *,
    limit: Optional[int] = None,
    only_missing_summaries: bool = False,
) -> list:
    """
    Walk games in priority order and fill gaps.  Commits after each game.
    Returns the list of GameResult objects (one per processed game).
    """
    with session_factory() as session:
        query = _priority_query(session, only_missing_summaries)
        if limit is not None:
            query = query.limit(limit)
        # Load IDs only — game objects will be reloaded in fresh sessions below.
        game_ids = [g.id for g in query.all()]

    total = len(game_ids)
    if total == 0:
        print("Nothing to backfill.", flush=True)
        return []

    mode = "--only-missing-summaries" if only_missing_summaries else "full"
    lim_str = f" (limit {limit})" if limit is not None else ""
    print(f"Backfilling {total} games [{mode}]{lim_str}", flush=True)

    results: list = []
    with HttpClient() as client:
        for idx, game_id in enumerate(game_ids, 1):
            with session_factory() as session:
                game = session.get(Game, game_id)
                if game is None:
                    continue
                result = _process_game(session, game, client, only_missing_summaries)
                session.commit()

            results.append(result)
            _print_result(idx, total, result)

    new_summaries = sum(r.critic_written + r.user_written for r in results)
    complete = sum(r.already_complete for r in results)
    skipped = sum(r.skipped_no_reviews for r in results)
    scored_no_rev = sum(r.scored_no_reviews for r in results)
    errors = sum(r.error is not None for r in results)
    games_with_new = sum(r.critic_written or r.user_written for r in results)
    print(
        f"\nDone: {new_summaries} new summaries on {games_with_new} games, "
        f"{complete} already complete, "
        f"{skipped} skipped (unreleased), "
        f"{scored_no_rev} scored-but-no-reviews, "
        f"{errors} errors",
        flush=True,
    )
    return results


def _cli() -> None:
    import argparse

    from .db.session import init_db, make_engine, make_session_factory

    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(
        description="Backfill games in the database with detail, reviews, and summaries."
    )
    parser.add_argument(
        "--limit", type=int, default=None,
        help="Maximum number of games to process (default: all)",
    )
    parser.add_argument(
        "--only-missing-summaries", action="store_true",
        help="Only process games that have reviews but are missing summaries",
    )
    args = parser.parse_args()

    logging.basicConfig(
        level=logging.INFO,
        format="%(asctime)s %(levelname)s %(name)s: %(message)s",
        datefmt="%H:%M:%S",
    )
    # Suppress noisy sub-loggers during the run.
    logging.getLogger("httpx").setLevel(logging.WARNING)
    logging.getLogger("httpcore").setLevel(logging.WARNING)

    engine = make_engine()
    init_db(engine)
    session_factory = make_session_factory(engine)

    run_backfill(
        session_factory,
        limit=args.limit,
        only_missing_summaries=args.only_missing_summaries,
    )


if __name__ == "__main__":
    _cli()

"""
Parsing a Metacritic listing page into game records.

Two listing shapes matter, and they carry the same item objects:

    /game/                                   the New Releases block
    /browse/game/all/all/all-time/new/       the paginated full list

Everything below is defensive about missing fields. Unreleased games — which
is most of what "new releases" means — have a null metascore, no reviews and
sometimes no description, and a scraper that assumes otherwise dies on its
first run at 03:00.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

from dataclasses import dataclass, field

from ..payload import find_items, parse

IMAGE_BASE = "https://www.metacritic.com/a/img/resize/"


@dataclass
class PlatformScore:
    """One platform's scores. A game can ship on several, each scored apart."""

    name: str
    metascore: int | None = None
    critic_reviews: int = 0
    userscore: float | None = None
    user_reviews: int = 0


@dataclass
class GameSummary:
    """What a listing page tells us about a game, before we open its page."""

    external_id: int
    slug: str
    title: str
    url: str
    description: str | None = None
    release_date: str | None = None
    premiere_year: int | None = None
    rating: str | None = None
    image_url: str | None = None
    genres: list[str] = field(default_factory=list)
    platforms: list[PlatformScore] = field(default_factory=list)
    metascore: int | None = None
    critic_review_count: int = 0
    critic_sentiment: str | None = None

    @property
    def is_released(self) -> bool:
        return self.metascore is not None or self.critic_review_count > 0


def _image_url(image: dict | None) -> str | None:
    """
    Build a cover URL from the image object.

    The payload gives a bucket path rather than a URL; Metacritic's own pages
    compose the CDN address from it. `imageUrl` is sometimes populated and is
    preferred when it is.
    """
    if not isinstance(image, dict):
        return None
    direct = image.get("imageUrl")
    if isinstance(direct, str) and direct.startswith("http"):
        return direct
    bucket_path = image.get("bucketPath")
    if not isinstance(bucket_path, str) or not bucket_path:
        return None
    width = image.get("width") or 460
    height = image.get("height") or 215
    return f"{IMAGE_BASE}{width}/{height}/catalog{bucket_path}"


def _platforms(item: dict) -> list[PlatformScore]:
    scores: list[PlatformScore] = []
    for entry in item.get("platforms") or []:
        if not isinstance(entry, dict):
            continue
        name = entry.get("name") or entry.get("platform") or entry.get("slug")
        if not name:
            continue
        critic = entry.get("criticScoreSummary") or {}
        user = entry.get("userScoreSummary") or {}
        scores.append(
            PlatformScore(
                name=str(name),
                metascore=critic.get("score") if isinstance(critic, dict) else None,
                critic_reviews=(critic.get("reviewCount") or 0) if isinstance(critic, dict) else 0,
                userscore=user.get("score") if isinstance(user, dict) else None,
                user_reviews=(user.get("reviewCount") or 0) if isinstance(user, dict) else 0,
            )
        )
    return scores


def _genres(item: dict) -> list[str]:
    names = []
    for entry in item.get("genres") or []:
        if isinstance(entry, dict) and entry.get("name"):
            names.append(str(entry["name"]))
        elif isinstance(entry, str):
            names.append(entry)
    return names


def to_summary(item: dict) -> GameSummary | None:
    """One payload item to a GameSummary. Returns None for non-game entries."""
    slug = item.get("slug")
    title = item.get("title")
    external_id = item.get("id")
    if not slug or not title or external_id is None:
        return None
    if item.get("type") and item["type"] != "game-title":
        return None

    critic = item.get("criticScoreSummary")
    critic = critic if isinstance(critic, dict) else {}

    return GameSummary(
        external_id=int(external_id),
        slug=str(slug),
        title=str(title),
        url=f"https://www.metacritic.com/game/{slug}/",
        description=item.get("description") or None,
        release_date=item.get("releaseDate") or None,
        premiere_year=item.get("premiereYear") or None,
        rating=item.get("rating") or None,
        image_url=_image_url(item.get("image")),
        genres=_genres(item),
        platforms=_platforms(item),
        metascore=critic.get("score"),
        critic_review_count=critic.get("reviewCount") or 0,
        critic_sentiment=critic.get("sentiment") or None,
    )


def parse_listing(html: str) -> list[GameSummary]:
    """A listing page to the games it advertises, in page order."""
    items = find_items(parse(html))
    summaries = [to_summary(item) for item in items if isinstance(item, dict)]
    return [summary for summary in summaries if summary is not None]

"""
Parsing a Metacritic listing page into game records.

Two listing shapes matter, and they carry the same item objects:

    /game/                                   the New Releases block
    /browse/game/all/all/all-time/new/       the paginated full list

Everything below is defensive about missing fields. Unreleased games — which
is most of what "new releases" means — have a null metascore, no reviews and
sometimes no description, and a scraper that assumes otherwise dies on its
first run at 03:00.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

from dataclasses import dataclass, field

from ..payload import find_items, parse, scrape_image_urls

IMAGE_BASE = "https://www.metacritic.com/a/img/resize/"


@dataclass
class PlatformScore:
    """One platform's scores. A game can ship on several, each scored apart."""

    name: str
    metascore: int | None = None
    critic_reviews: int = 0
    userscore: float | None = None
    user_reviews: int = 0


@dataclass
class GameSummary:
    """What a listing page tells us about a game, before we open its page."""

    external_id: int
    slug: str
    title: str
    url: str
    description: str | None = None
    release_date: str | None = None
    premiere_year: int | None = None
    rating: str | None = None
    image_url: str | None = None
    genres: list[str] = field(default_factory=list)
    platforms: list[PlatformScore] = field(default_factory=list)
    metascore: int | None = None
    critic_review_count: int = 0
    critic_sentiment: str | None = None

    @property
    def is_released(self) -> bool:
        return self.metascore is not None or self.critic_review_count > 0


def _image_url(image: dict | None) -> str | None:
    """
    Build a cover URL from the image object.

    The payload gives a bucket path rather than a URL; Metacritic's own pages
    compose the CDN address from it. `imageUrl` is sometimes populated and is
    preferred when it is.
    """
    if not isinstance(image, dict):
        return None
    direct = image.get("imageUrl")
    if isinstance(direct, str) and direct.startswith("http"):
        return direct
    bucket_path = image.get("bucketPath")
    if not isinstance(bucket_path, str) or not bucket_path:
        return None
    width = image.get("width") or 460
    height = image.get("height") or 215
    return f"{IMAGE_BASE}{width}/{height}/catalog{bucket_path}"


def _platforms(item: dict) -> list[PlatformScore]:
    scores: list[PlatformScore] = []
    for entry in item.get("platforms") or []:
        if not isinstance(entry, dict):
            continue
        name = entry.get("name") or entry.get("platform") or entry.get("slug")
        if not name:
            continue
        critic = entry.get("criticScoreSummary") or {}
        user = entry.get("userScoreSummary") or {}
        scores.append(
            PlatformScore(
                name=str(name),
                metascore=critic.get("score") if isinstance(critic, dict) else None,
                critic_reviews=(critic.get("reviewCount") or 0) if isinstance(critic, dict) else 0,
                userscore=user.get("score") if isinstance(user, dict) else None,
                user_reviews=(user.get("reviewCount") or 0) if isinstance(user, dict) else 0,
            )
        )
    return scores


def _genres(item: dict) -> list[str]:
    names = []
    for entry in item.get("genres") or []:
        if isinstance(entry, dict) and entry.get("name"):
            names.append(str(entry["name"]))
        elif isinstance(entry, str):
            names.append(entry)
    return names


def to_summary(item: dict) -> GameSummary | None:
    """One payload item to a GameSummary. Returns None for non-game entries."""
    slug = item.get("slug")
    title = item.get("title")
    external_id = item.get("id")
    if not slug or not title or external_id is None:
        return None
    if item.get("type") and item["type"] != "game-title":
        return None

    critic = item.get("criticScoreSummary")
    critic = critic if isinstance(critic, dict) else {}

    return GameSummary(
        external_id=int(external_id),
        slug=str(slug),
        title=str(title),
        url=f"https://www.metacritic.com/game/{slug}/",
        description=item.get("description") or None,
        release_date=item.get("releaseDate") or None,
        premiere_year=item.get("premiereYear") or None,
        rating=item.get("rating") or None,
        image_url=_image_url(item.get("image")),
        genres=_genres(item),
        platforms=_platforms(item),
        metascore=critic.get("score"),
        critic_review_count=critic.get("reviewCount") or 0,
        critic_sentiment=critic.get("sentiment") or None,
    )


def parse_listing(html: str) -> list[GameSummary]:
    """A listing page to the games it advertises, in page order."""
    items = find_items(parse(html))
    summaries = [to_summary(item) for item in items if isinstance(item, dict)]
    return [summary for summary in summaries if summary is not None]

"""
Parsing a Metacritic game detail page (game.html fixture).

All component lookups go by meta.componentName, never by index.
The BRIEF verified this is stable across fetches; the index order is not.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

from dataclasses import dataclass, field

from ..payload import parse


@dataclass
class PlatformDetail:
    name: str
    metascore: int | None = None
    critic_reviews: int = 0
    userscore: float | None = None
    user_reviews: int = 0


@dataclass
class ReviewItem:
    kind: str                          # 'critic' | 'user'
    author: str | None
    publication: str | None
    score: int | None
    quote: str | None
    review_date: str | None
    platform: str | None = None
    thumbs_up: int | None = None
    thumbs_down: int | None = None


@dataclass
class GameDetail:
    slug: str
    title: str | None = None
    description: str | None = None
    release_date: str | None = None
    rating: str | None = None
    developer: str | None = None
    publisher: str | None = None
    cover_url: str | None = None
    video_url: str | None = None
    metascore: int | None = None
    userscore: float | None = None
    critic_review_count: int = 0
    user_review_count: int = 0
    platforms: list[PlatformDetail] = field(default_factory=list)
    genres: list[str] = field(default_factory=list)
    critic_reviews: list[ReviewItem] = field(default_factory=list)
    user_reviews: list[ReviewItem] = field(default_factory=list)


def _by_name(components: list, name: str) -> dict | None:
    for c in components:
        if isinstance(c, dict) and (c.get("meta") or {}).get("componentName") == name:
            return c
    return None


def _platforms(item: dict) -> list[PlatformDetail]:
    out = []
    for p in (item.get("platforms") or []):
        if not isinstance(p, dict):
            continue
        name = p.get("name") or p.get("slug")
        if not name:
            continue
        cs = p.get("criticScoreSummary") or {}
        us = p.get("userScoreSummary") or {}
        out.append(PlatformDetail(
            name=str(name),
            metascore=cs.get("score") if isinstance(cs, dict) else None,
            critic_reviews=(cs.get("reviewCount") or 0) if isinstance(cs, dict) else 0,
            userscore=us.get("score") if isinstance(us, dict) else None,
            user_reviews=(us.get("reviewCount") or 0) if isinstance(us, dict) else 0,

    platforms: list[PlatformDetail] = field(default_factory=list)
    genres: list[str] = field(default_factory=list)
    critic_reviews: list[ReviewItem] = field(default_factory=list)
    user_reviews: list[ReviewItem] = field(default_factory=list)


def _by_name(components: list, name: str) -> dict | None:
    for c in components:
        if isinstance(c, dict) and (c.get("meta") or {}).get("componentName") == name:
            return c
    return None


def _platforms(item: dict) -> list[PlatformDetail]:
    out = []
    for p in (item.get("platforms") or []):
        if not isinstance(p, dict):
            continue
        name = p.get("name") or p.get("slug")
        if not name:
            continue
        cs = p.get("criticScoreSummary") or {}
        us = p.get("userScoreSummary") or {}
        out.append(PlatformDetail(
            name=str(name),
            metascore=cs.get("score") if isinstance(cs, dict) else None,
            critic_reviews=(cs.get("reviewCount") or 0) if isinstance(cs, dict) else 0,
            userscore=us.get("score") if isinstance(us, dict) else None,
            user_reviews=(us.get("reviewCount") or 0) if isinstance(us, dict) else 0,
        ))
    return out


def _genres(item: dict) -> list[str]:
    return [
        g["name"] for g in (item.get("genres") or [])
        if isinstance(g, dict) and g.get("name")
    ]


def _companies(item: dict) -> tuple[str | None, str | None]:
    """Return (developer_name, publisher_name) from production.companies."""
    developer = publisher = None
    for company in ((item.get("production") or {}).get("companies") or []):
        if not isinstance(company, dict):
            continue
        kind = company.get("typeName")
        name = company.get("name")
        if kind == "Developer" and developer is None:
            developer = name
        elif kind == "Publisher" and publisher is None:
            publisher = name
    return developer, publisher


def _video_url(item: dict) -> str | None:
    video = item.get("video")
    if not isinstance(video, dict):
        return None
    # embedUrl is an iframe-embeddable JW Player URL; url is null in the fixture.
    return video.get("embedUrl") or video.get("manifestUrl") or None


def _cover_url(item: dict, url_map: dict | None = None) -> str | None:
    images = item.get("images") or []
    for img in images:
        if not isinstance(img, dict):
            continue
        url = img.get("imageUrl")
        if isinstance(url, str) and url.startswith("http"):
            return url
        bucket = img.get("bucketPath")
        if isinstance(bucket, str) and bucket:
            if url_map and bucket in url_map:
                return url_map[bucket]
            w = img.get("width") or 460
            h = img.get("height") or 215
            return f"https://www.metacritic.com/a/img/resize/{w}/{h}/catalog{bucket}"
    return None


def _critic_reviews(comp: dict) -> tuple[list[ReviewItem], int]:
    data = comp.get("data") or {}
    items = data.get("items") or []
    total = data.get("totalResults") or 0
    reviews = []
    for r in items:
        if not isinstance(r, dict):
            continue
        reviews.append(ReviewItem(
            kind="critic",
            author=r.get("author") or None,
            publication=r.get("publicationName") or None,
            score=r.get("score"),
            quote=r.get("quote") or None,
            review_date=r.get("date") or None,
            platform=r.get("platform") or None,
        ))
    return reviews, total


def _user_reviews(comp: dict) -> tuple[list[ReviewItem], int]:
    data = comp.get("data") or {}
    items = data.get("items") or []
    total = data.get("totalResults") or 0
    reviews = []
    for r in items:
        if not isinstance(r, dict):
            continue
        reviews.append(ReviewItem(
            kind="user",
            author=r.get("author") or None,
            publication=None,
            score=r.get("score"),
            quote=r.get("quote") or None,
            review_date=r.get("date") or None,
            platform=r.get("platform") or None,
            thumbs_up=r.get("thumbsUp"),
            thumbs_down=r.get("thumbsDown"),
        ))
    return reviews, total


def parse_detail(html: str, slug: str) -> GameDetail:
    """
    Parse a game detail page into a GameDetail.

    `slug` is used to locate the correct loadPage key; it must match the
    game's Metacritic slug exactly.
    """
    url_map = scrape_image_urls(html)
    root = parse(html)
    page_key = f"loadPage:games:{slug}:"
    page = (root.get("data") or {}).get(page_key)
    if page is None:
        # Fallback: find any loadPage:games:…: key
        for k, v in (root.get("data") or {}).items():
            if k.startswith("loadPage:games:") and isinstance(v, dict):
                page = v
                break

    if page is None:
        # Handle review sub-pages (critic-reviews, user-reviews) whose keys
        # are loadPage:games-critic-reviews:… and loadPage:games-user-reviews:…
        for k, v in (root.get("data") or {}).items():
            if k.startswith("loadPage:games") and isinstance(v, dict):
                page = v
                break

    if page is None or not isinstance(page.get("components"), list):
        return GameDetail(slug=slug)

    comps = page["components"]
    detail = GameDetail(slug=slug)

    # --- product component ---
    prod_comp = _by_name(comps, "product")
    if prod_comp:
        item = (prod_comp.get("data") or {}).get("item") or {}
        detail.title = item.get("title")
        detail.description = item.get("description") or None
        detail.release_date = item.get("releaseDate") or None
        detail.rating = item.get("rating") or None
        detail.developer, detail.publisher = _companies(item)
        detail.video_url = _video_url(item)
        detail.cover_url = _cover_url(item)
        detail.platforms = _platforms(item)
        detail.genres = _genres(item)

    # --- critic-score-summary ---
    cs_comp = _by_name(comps, "critic-score-summary")
    if cs_comp:
        cs = (cs_comp.get("data") or {}).get("item") or {}
        detail.metascore = cs.get("score")
        detail.critic_review_count = cs.get("reviewCount") or 0

    # --- user-score-summary ---
    us_comp = _by_name(comps, "user-score-summary")
    if us_comp:
        us = (us_comp.get("data") or {}).get("item") or {}
        detail.userscore = us.get("score")
        detail.user_review_count = us.get("reviewCount") or 0

    # --- critic-reviews ---
    cr_comp = _by_name(comps, "critic-reviews")
    if cr_comp:
        detail.critic_reviews, _ = _critic_reviews(cr_comp)

    # --- user-reviews ---
    ur_comp = _by_name(comps, "user-reviews")
    if ur_comp:
        detail.user_reviews, _ = _user_reviews(ur_comp)

    return detail
